0.core_image: 一只手抓起一把黑土，土在指缝间碎成细粒，旁边是刚播下的种子

0.sceneCN: 这里 fertility 指「土地的肥力」（第 3 个义项：土壤能供养植物旺盛生长的性质）；句意为多年施用堆肥让这块田的肥力恢复了。可辨识物件：黑土团、指缝落下的土粒、育苗盘、休耕的田垄。

senses.title: The capacity to conceive and bear young
senses.titleCN: 能受孕并生育子女的能力
senses.definition: the natural ability of a person to conceive and give birth to children
senses.definitionCN: 人自然受孕并生育子女的能力
senses.example: Fertility falls sharply after the middle thirties.
senses.exampleCN: 生育能力在三十五岁之后明显下降。
senses.why: fertility names a capacity rather than an event: the Latin adjective fertilis already meant 'able to produce', so the noun describes a state of being able.
senses.whyCN: fertility 指的是能力而不是事件：拉丁形容词 fertilis 本义就是「能出产的」，所以这个名词描述的是「有能力」这一状态。

senses.title: Childbearing measured across a population
senses.definition: the actual level of childbearing in a population, usually counted as births per woman
senses.definitionCN: 某一人口的实际生育水平，通常按每名妇女的生育数计算
senses.example: The census put national fertility below replacement level.
senses.exampleCN: 人口普查显示全国生育水平低于更替水平。
senses.why: demographers turned a personal capacity into a statistic, so the same noun now names a rate that can be counted and compared.
senses.whyCN: 人口学家把个人能力变成了统计量，于是同一个名词也指可以计数、可以比较的比率。

senses.title: The power of soil to grow crops
senses.definition: the quality of soil that allows plants to grow strongly and yield well
senses.definitionCN: 土壤使植物旺盛生长并高产的性质
senses.example: Years of compost have restored the fertility of this field.
senses.exampleCN: 多年施用堆肥让这块田的肥力恢复了。
senses.why: the metaphor is agricultural: land that can 'bear' crops is fertile in exactly the way a body is fertile, because both produce abundantly.
senses.whyCN: 这是农业上的比喻：能「承载」作物的土地与能生育的身体一样肥沃，因为两者都能大量出产。

senses.title: Richness of a whole region
senses.definition: the general richness of a region that makes it good for farming
senses.definitionCN: 使某一地区适于耕作的总体富饶程度
senses.example: The valley's fertility drew settlers long before the railway.
senses.exampleCN: 早在铁路出现之前，这条河谷的富饶就吸引了定居者。
senses.why: once soil fertility is summed over a landscape, the word shifts from a sample of earth to the character of a place.
senses.whyCN: 当土壤肥力被累加到整片地景上，这个词就从一把土的性状变成了一个地方的特征。

senses.title: A productive imagination
senses.definition: the power of a mind or an age to produce many works or ideas
senses.definitionCN: 某人的心智或某个时代产出大量作品或想法的能力
senses.example: The fertility of her imagination produced three novels in a decade.
senses.exampleCN: 她想象力的丰产让她十年内写出了三部小说。
senses.why: the word spreads from soil and bodies to minds because all three are judged by how much they bring forth.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从土壤与身体扩展到心智，因为三者都以「出产多少」来衡量。

senses.title: An ecosystem's capacity to support life
senses.titleCN: 生态系统的承载与出产能力
senses.definition: the capacity of an ecosystem to support abundant plant and animal life
senses.definitionCN: 生态系统供养大量动植物生命的能力
senses.example: Upwelling gives the coast extraordinary fertility.
senses.exampleCN: 上升流让这片海岸拥有非凡的生产力。
senses.why: ecology needed a word for how much life a system can carry, and borrowed the agricultural one rather than coining a new term.
senses.whyCN: 生态学需要一个词来表示一个系统能承载多少生命，于是直接借用了农业上的说法，而没有另造新词。

senses.title: The fertilizing power of gametes
senses.titleCN: 生物学：配子的受精能力
senses.definition: the ability of pollen or sperm to fertilize an egg successfully
senses.definitionCN: 花粉或精子成功使卵细胞受精的能力
senses.example: The lab tests the fertility of stored pollen before each cross.
senses.exampleCN: 实验室在每次杂交前都检测储存花粉的受精能力。
senses.why: in reproductive biology the capacity is narrowed to the single step of fertilization, so fertility becomes a measurable property of cells.
senses.whyCN: 在生殖生物学中，这种能力被收窄到受精这一步，于是 fertility 成了可测量的细胞属性。

senses.title: Fertility as a branch of medicine
senses.definition: used before another noun for the medical field that treats the ability to conceive
senses.definitionCN: 作定语，指治疗受孕能力的医学领域
senses.example: She was referred to a fertility clinic after two years of trying.
senses.exampleCN: 尝试两年之后，她被转诊到一家生育诊所。
senses.why: a clinic that treats fertility takes the abstract noun as its label, so the word also names an institution and a specialty.
senses.whyCN: 治疗生育力的诊所直接用这个抽象名词作名称，于是这个词也指一种机构与一门专科。

intro.en: Fertility comes straight from Latin through Old French, and every one of its senses still rests on the root ferre 'to carry, to bear'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: fertility 经古法语直接来自拉丁语，它的每一个义项都仍立根于 ferre「携带、承载」这个词根。年代均为约数。

items.en: Latin fertilis meant 'bearing in abundance, fruitful, productive'. It was formed from ferre 'to carry, bear' plus the adjective suffix -ilis 'able to be, capable of'.
items.cn: 拉丁 fertilis 意为「大量出产的、丰饶的、多产的」，由 ferre「携带、承载」加形容词后缀 -ilis「能……的」构成。

items.en: Ferre 'to bear, carry' is one of the oldest Latin verbs and supplies transfer, refer, offer and suffer. Its Indo-European root is reconstructed as *bher-, 'to carry', which also underlies English bear and birth.
items.cn: ferre「承载、携带」是最古老的拉丁动词之一，衍生出 transfer、refer、offer、suffer。它的印欧词根被重构为 *bher-「携带」，英语 bear 与 birth 也出自这里。

items.en: The abstract noun suffix -itas (genitive -itatis) turned an adjective of quality into a noun of state; through French it became English -ity, as in fertility, clarity and purity.
items.cn: 抽象名词后缀 -itas（属格 -itatis）把表示性质的形容词变成表示状态的名词；经法语进入英语后成为 -ity，如 fertility、clarity、purity。

items.en: Old French fertilité carried the word into Middle English in the early fifteenth century, first of land and crops, then of people and animals.
items.cn: 古法语 fertilité 在十五世纪初把这个词带进中古英语，先用于土地与庄稼，随后才用于人与动物。

items.en: From the nineteenth century the counting of births gave the fixed phrase fertility rate, and the word acquired its statistical sense alongside the bodily one.
items.cn: 从十九世纪起，对出生人数的统计形成了固定搭配 fertility rate（生育率），这个词在身体义之外又获得了统计义。

items.en: Source uncertain: the exact first recorded English use is usually dated to the early 1400s but the dating rests on a small number of texts, and the pre-Indo-European history of *bher- is a reconstruction rather than a fact.
items.cn: 来源不确定：英语首见通常定在十五世纪初，但依据的文本很少；*bher- 在印欧语之前的历史属重构形式，而非已证事实。

note.en: Group one holds words that look or sound close to fertility; group two holds the neighbouring ideas of producing abundantly.
note.cn: 第一组是与 fertility 形近或音近的词；第二组是表示「大量出产」的邻近概念。

entries.definition: Pointlessness; from Latin futilis 'easily poured out, worthless', a root quite separate from ferre.
entries.definitionCN: 无益、徒劳；来自拉丁 futilis「容易倒出的、无价值的」，与 ferre 完全不同源。

entries.definition: The adjective behind the noun; fertility is the state, fertile is the quality.
entries.definitionCN: 名词背后的形容词；fertility 是状态，fertile 是性质。

entries.definition: To add nutrients to soil or to unite a gamete with an egg; it names the action, not the capacity.
entries.definitionCN: 指给土壤加养分或使配子与卵结合；它指动作，不指能力。

entries.definition: The material spread on land to raise its fertility; the noun ends in -er like a doer.
entries.definitionCN: 撒在土地上以提高肥力的物质；这个词以 -er 结尾，像表示施动者。

entries.definition: The actual rate of producing offspring, often used of animals and plants; it measures output, while fertility measures capacity.
entries.definitionCN: 实际繁殖后代的速度，多用于动植物；它量的是产出，而 fertility 量的是能力。

entries.definition: The state of yielding much fruit or many results; it points to the harvest rather than the ground.
entries.definitionCN: 指多结果实或多出成果的状态；它指向收成，而不是土地。

entries.definition: The quality of producing a lot of work or goods; it is wider than fertility and not tied to living things.
entries.definitionCN: 指大量产出工作或产品的性质；它比 fertility 宽，也不限于生命体。

entries.definition: A large quantity of something present at once; fertility is the power behind such plenty, not the plenty itself.
entries.definitionCN: 指同时存在的大量事物；fertility 是造成这种丰盛的能力，而不是丰盛本身。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real root fer-, the real suffix family and the fixed technical phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的词根 fer-、真实的后缀族与固定的技术搭配。

normal.en: fer- 'carry' + -ile 'able to' + -ity 'state': the state of being able to carry fruit.
normal.cn: fer-「承载」+ -ile「能」+ -ity「状态」：能够承载果实的状态。

normal.en: The family runs fertile, fertilize, fertilization, fertilizer, infertility.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 fertile、fertilize、fertilization、fertilizer、infertility。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the two main fields: soil fertility in farming, fertility rate in demography.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出两大领域：农业中的土壤肥力，人口学中的生育率。

normal.en: Do not link it to futility: futility comes from futilis 'worthless', not from ferre.
normal.cn: 不要把它和 futility 联系起来：futility 来自 futilis「无价值的」，不是 ferre。

normal.en: Latin ferre also gives transfer, refer and offer, all of which carry something somewhere.
normal.cn: 拉丁 ferre 还衍生 transfer、refer、offer，它们都表示把某物带向某处。

abstract.en: Picture a handful of dark soil that holds both water and roots at the same time.
abstract.cn: 想象一把黑土，既能蓄水又能抓住根系。

abstract.en: Picture an orchard where every branch carries fruit in the same season.
abstract.cn: 想象一座果园，每条枝在一个季节里都挂着果子。

abstract.en: Picture a bank account of new lives: deposits must outrun withdrawals for the balance to hold.
abstract.cn: 想象一个「新生命账户」：只有存进去的多过取出的，余额才守得住。

examples.en: Soil fertility depends on organic matter as much as on minerals.
examples.cn: 土壤肥力既取决于矿物质，也同样取决于有机质。

examples.en: The region's fertility has fallen for six straight years.
examples.cn: 该地区的生育水平已连续六年下降。

examples.en: Rising temperatures threaten the fertility of many crop varieties.
examples.cn: 气温上升威胁着许多作物品种的结实能力。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「fer（负）+ ti（体）+ lity（力）」——能把果实背在身上的力量 → 生育力；肥力

0.root: 拉丁 fertilis「丰产的」← ferre「携带、承载」+ -ilis「能……的」；-ity 来自拉丁 -itas，表示状态。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses fan out from one root idea, being able to carry and bring forth: a body conceives, a population is counted, soil yields, a landscape is rich, a mind is productive, an ecosystem carries life, gametes fertilize, and medicine turns the capacity into a specialty.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从一个核心意思「能承载、能出产」展开：身体能受孕，人口被计数，土壤能出产，地景富饶，心智丰产，生态系统承载生命，配子能受精，医学把它变成一门专科。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand holding dark soil in which roots and seeds can both take hold.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手握着黑土，根与种子都能在其中扎住。

branches.en: BODILY CAPACITY: the plain medical reading, the ability to conceive and carry a child.
branches.cn: 身体能力：最基本的医学读法，能受孕并孕育子女。

branches.en: MEASURED RATE: the same capacity counted across a whole population.
branches.cn: 可测比率：把同一能力放到整个人口上计数。

branches.en: SOIL AND LAND: fertility moves from a sample of earth to the character of a region.
branches.cn: 土壤与地景：肥力从一把土扩展到整个地区的性状。

branches.en: METAPHORICAL YIELD: minds and ecosystems are praised for how much life or work they bring forth.
branches.cn: 比喻性出产：心智与生态系统都以「出产多少生命或作品」来衡量。

branches.en: CELL AND CLINIC: the capacity is narrowed to gametes, then institutionalised as a medical field.
branches.cn: 细胞与诊所：能力先收窄到配子，再被机构化为一门医学专科。

intro.en: Fertility is a Latin adjective plus an abstract suffix; the root fer- is one of the most productive carriers in English.
intro.cn: fertility 是一个拉丁形容词加抽象后缀；词根 fer- 是英语中最能产的「携带」词根之一。

latinIntro.en: The Latin family runs fertilis, fertilitas and ferre; the derived English words all keep the sense of carrying or making fruitful.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词族包括 fertilis、fertilitas、ferre；由它衍生的英语词都保留「携带」或「使丰产」的意思。

items.meaning: able to produce fruit or young
items.example: The soil here is deep and fertile.
items.exampleCN: 这里的土壤又深又肥。

items.meaning: to make fruitful; to unite with a gamete
items.meaningCN: 施肥；使受精（-ize 表示「使……化」）
items.example: Bees fertilize the blossoms as they feed.
items.exampleCN: 蜜蜂在取食时让花朵受精。

items.meaning: the act or process of fertilizing
items.meaningCN: 受精；施肥（-ation 表示过程或结果）
items.example: Fertilization occurs inside the flower.
items.exampleCN: 受精在花内部发生。

items.meaning: a substance added to soil to raise fertility
items.meaningCN: 肥料（-er 表示施动的物）
items.example: They spread fertilizer before sowing.
items.exampleCN: 他们在播种前撒肥料。

items.meaning: the state of being unable to conceive
items.meaningCN: 不育；贫瘠（in- 表示否定）
items.example: The clinic treats both male and female infertility.
items.exampleCN: 这家诊所治疗男性与女性的不育。

items.meaningCN: 肥沃；能生育（-ness 表示性质状态）
items.example: Growers judge fertileness by root depth.
items.exampleCN: 种植者靠根系深度判断土壤的肥力。

items.meaning: to carry from one place or person to another
items.meaningCN: 转移；调动（trans- 表示「越过」，fer- 表示「携带」）
items.example: The seed bank transfers duplicates to other countries.
items.exampleCN: 种子库把副本转移到其他国家。

items.meaning: to send back to a source or authority
items.meaningCN: 提及；转诊（re- 表示「回」，fer- 表示「带」）
items.example: The doctor referred her to a specialist.
items.exampleCN: 医生把她转给了专科医生。

items.meaning: to bring something forward for someone to take
items.meaningCN: 提供；献上（ob- 表示「朝向」，fer- 表示「带」）
items.example: They offered the farmers free seed.
items.exampleCN: 他们向农民免费提供种子。

items.meaning: to carry a burden under pressure
items.meaningCN: 遭受；承受（sub- 表示「在下」，fer- 表示「承载」）
items.example: The crop suffered in the dry spring.
items.exampleCN: 干旱的春天让庄稼受了苦。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 表示状态或性质的名词后缀

1.definition_zh: 不育的；不能生育的；贫瘠的；不结果实的
1.definition_en: unable to produce young, seed or fruit, or unable to support crops
1.core_image: 一块干裂的坡地，裂缝里连草根都没有，界桩歪在一边
1.scene: 山坡上只剩碎石和矮草，农学家蹲下抓了一把土，摇摇头。Decades of heavy grazing left the hillside infertile.
1.sceneCN: 这里 infertile 指「贫瘠、不能供养作物」（第 4 个义项：土地无法生长庄稼）；句意为数十年的重度放牧让这片山坡变得贫瘠。可辨识物件：碎石坡、矮草、干裂土块、倒斜的界桩。

pos.zh: 不育的；不能生育的；贫瘠的；不结果实的

collocations.zh: 贫瘠的土地；无成果的领域

forms.label: 副词（贫瘠地；不能生育地）

senses.title: A person who cannot conceive
senses.definition: of a person, unable to conceive a child after prolonged attempts
senses.definitionCN: 指人经过长期尝试仍不能受孕
senses.example: The couple learned that one partner was infertile.
senses.exampleCN: 这对夫妇得知其中一方不能生育。
senses.why: in- says 'not' and fertilis says 'able to produce', so the adjective simply denies the capacity; in medicine it is the neutral clinical wording.
senses.whyCN: in- 表示「不」，fertilis 表示「能出产」，这个形容词就是直接否定这种能力；在医学中它是中性的临床说法。

senses.title: An animal that cannot breed
senses.definition: of an animal, unable to produce offspring
senses.definitionCN: 指动物不能产生后代
senses.example: The herd grew infertile after generations of inbreeding.
senses.exampleCN: 经过数代近亲繁殖，这群牲畜变得不能生育。
senses.why: the same denial applies to animals, and the adjective often carries a cause such as inbreeding or age rather than a diagnosis.
senses.whyCN: 同样的否定也用于动物，只是这个形容词往往带有近亲繁殖或年龄等成因，而不只是一项诊断。

senses.title: A plant that sets no seed
senses.titleCN: 植物不结实、不产生种子
senses.definition: of a plant or flower, unable to produce viable seed or fruit
senses.definitionCN: 指植物或花朵不能产生可育种子或果实
senses.example: The hybrid is infertile and must be raised from cuttings.
senses.exampleCN: 这个杂交种不结实，只能靠扦插繁殖。
senses.why: botany keeps the oldest agricultural sense of fertilis, but applies it to seed set rather than to soil.
senses.whyCN: 植物学保留了 fertilis 最古老的农业义，只是把对象从土壤换成了结种。

senses.title: Land that will not grow crops
senses.definition: of land, too poor in nutrients or too damaged to support crops
senses.definitionCN: 指土地养分太少或受损过重，无法供养作物
senses.example: Decades of heavy grazing left the hillside infertile.
senses.exampleCN: 数十年的重度放牧让这片山坡变得贫瘠。
senses.why: the agricultural transfer is direct: ground that cannot 'bear' a crop is infertile in the same literal way a body is.
senses.whyCN: 这一农业转义很直接：不能「承载」庄稼的地，与不能生育的身体在字面上是同一种否定。

senses.title: Soil stripped of its nutrients
senses.definition: of soil, lacking the minerals and organic matter that plants need
senses.definitionCN: 指土壤缺乏植物所需的矿物质与有机质
senses.example: Acid deposition rendered the catchment infertile.
senses.exampleCN: 酸性沉降让这片集水区的土壤变得贫瘠。
senses.why: here the adjective describes a chemical state rather than a farming outcome, which is why it pairs with catchments and plots in soil science.
senses.whyCN: 这里这个形容词描述的是化学状态而非耕作结果，因此在土壤学中常与集水区、样地搭配。

senses.title: Gametes that cannot fertilize
senses.definition: of pollen, sperm or eggs, unable to complete fertilization
senses.definitionCN: 指花粉、精子或卵细胞无法完成受精
senses.example: The pollen proved infertile under the microscope.
senses.exampleCN: 显微镜下证实这些花粉不能受精。
senses.why: reproductive biology narrows the denial to a single cellular event, so the word can describe a grain of pollen rather than a whole organism.
senses.whyCN: 生殖生物学把这一否定收窄到单个细胞事件，因此这个词可以形容一粒花粉，而不必形容整个生物体。

senses.title: A debate that yields nothing
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：毫无成果的讨论
senses.definition: of a discussion or period, producing no useful result or idea
senses.definitionCN: 指讨论或时期没有产生有用的结果或想法
senses.example: An infertile debate produced no policy at all.
senses.exampleCN: 一场毫无成果的辩论没有催生任何政策。
senses.why: the metaphor keeps the agricultural logic: where nothing can take root, nothing grows, so the adjective judges output.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻保留了农业逻辑：什么都扎不下根的地方，什么也长不出来，所以这个形容词评判的是产出。

senses.title: An imagination that produces nothing
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：缺乏创造力的心智
senses.definition: of a mind or an age, unable to produce new works or ideas
senses.definitionCN: 指某人的心智或某个时代无法产出新作品或新想法
senses.example: Critics called the period an infertile one for poetry.
senses.exampleCN: 批评家称那个时期是诗歌上的贫瘠时代。
senses.why: once fertility was extended to minds, its negative followed, so infertile can now describe a decade as readily as a field.
senses.whyCN: 一旦 fertility 扩展到心智，它的否定形式也随之而来，于是 infertile 既能形容田地，也能形容一个年代。

intro.en: Infertile is the Latin negative of fertilis, and it entered English as a learned word rather than a native one. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: infertile 是拉丁 fertilis 的否定形式，作为学术借词而非本族词进入英语。年代均为约数。

items.en: The Latin negative prefix in- means 'not'. Before l and r it assimilates to il- and ir-, and before p, b and m to im-, but before f it stays in-, which is why the form is infertile and not imfertile.
items.cn: 拉丁否定前缀 in- 意为「不」。它在 l、r 前同化为 il-、ir-，在 p、b、m 前同化为 im-，但在 f 前保持 in-，所以词形是 infertile 而不是 imfertile。

items.en: Fertilis 'fruitful, able to produce' comes from ferre 'to carry, bear' plus -ilis 'able to'; the positive word was already common in farming and in poetry.
items.cn: fertilis「丰产的、能出产的」由 ferre「携带、承载」加 -ilis「能……」构成；这个肯定形式在农事与诗歌中早已常见。

items.en: Late Latin formed infertilis by adding the negative prefix to fertilis; the compound is generally treated as a later learned formation rather than an inherited word.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语在 fertilis 前加否定前缀构成 infertilis；一般认为这是较晚的学术构词，而非承继词。

items.en: English records infertile in the seventeenth century, at first of land and plants, and only later of people and animals.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪记录到 infertile，最初用于土地与植物，之后才用于人与动物。

items.en: Reproductive medicine of the twentieth century made the word a standard clinical term, and fertility clinics fixed the pair fertile and infertile as a neutral opposition.
items.cn: 二十世纪的生殖医学使这个词成为标准临床术语，生育诊所也把 fertile 与 infertile 固定为一组中性对立。

items.en: Source uncertain: the exact first English citation is not settled, and whether infertilis was used in classical Latin or only in later technical writing is disputed.
items.cn: 来源不确定：英语首见的确切出处尚无定论；infertilis 是古典拉丁语已用，还是只见于后世技术文献，也存在争议。

note.en: Group one holds close spellings that are not related in meaning; group two holds the synonyms, each with a different scope.
note.cn: 第一组是拼写接近但意义无关的词；第二组是近义词，各自范围不同。

entries.definition: Childish or baby-like; from Latin infans 'not speaking', unrelated to fertilis.
entries.definitionCN: 幼稚的；婴儿般的；来自拉丁 infans「不会说话的」，与 fertilis 无关。

entries.definition: Able to produce; the two words differ only by the negative prefix in-.
entries.definitionCN: 能出产的；两词只差一个否定前缀 in-。

entries.definition: Of hell or hellish; from Latin infernus 'below', built on a different stem entirely.
entries.definitionCN: 地狱的；地狱般的；来自拉丁 infernus「下面的」，词干完全不同。

entries.definition: The state named by the adjective; the noun is much more common in medical writing than the adjective alone.
entries.definitionCN: 这个形容词所指的状态；在医学文献中，名词比单用的形容词更常见。

entries.definition: Unable to produce young, and also free of microorganisms; infertile never carries the hygiene sense.
entries.definitionCN: 不能生育，同时也可指无菌；infertile 从不带无菌这一层意思。

entries.definition: Bare of vegetation or unable to bear young; it is more literary and harsher than infertile.
entries.definitionCN: 寸草不生的；不能生育的；比 infertile 更文学化、语气更重。

entries.definition: Producing no fruit or no useful result; it stresses the missing outcome rather than the missing capacity.
entries.definitionCN: 不结果实的；无成果的；强调结果缺失，而非能力缺失。

entries.definition: Yielding little work or value; it is the widest of these words and applies to people, land and meetings.
entries.definitionCN: 产出少的；价值低的；范围最宽，可用于人、土地与会议。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real negative prefix, the real adjective and the fixed clinical phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的否定前缀、真实的形容词与固定的临床搭配。

normal.en: in- 'not' + fertile: the whole word is one negation of one adjective.
normal.cn: in-「不」+ fertile：整个词就是对一个形容词的否定。

normal.en: The pairing fertile / infertile mirrors Latin fertilis / infertilis exactly.
normal.cn: fertile 与 infertile 的配对完全对应拉丁 fertilis 与 infertilis。

normal.en: Clinical phrases: infertile couple, infertility treatment, male infertility.
normal.cn: 临床搭配：不育夫妇、不育治疗、男性不育。

normal.en: Agricultural phrases keep the older sense: infertile soil, infertile land, infertile ground.
normal.cn: 农业搭配保留较老的义项：贫瘠土壤、不毛之地、贫瘠土地。

normal.en: Compare sterile, which adds the meaning 'free of germs' that infertile never has.
normal.cn: 比较 sterile：它多了「无菌」这一义，而 infertile 从不带这层意思。

abstract.en: Picture a cracked slope where even weeds give up.
abstract.cn: 想象一片裂开的山坡，连野草都放弃了。

abstract.en: Picture a seed packet that will never sprout, however long it is watered.
abstract.cn: 想象一包种子无论浇多久都不会发芽。

abstract.en: Picture a room full of talk where not one sentence takes root.
abstract.cn: 想象满屋的谈论，却没有一句话能扎下根。

examples.en: The test showed that the eggs were infertile.
examples.cn: 检测显示这些卵不能受精。

examples.en: Overgrazing turns fertile grassland into infertile scrub.
examples.cn: 过度放牧把肥沃的草场变成贫瘠的灌丛。

examples.en: Some hybrids are infertile and cannot reproduce themselves.
examples.cn: 有些杂交种不育，无法自行繁衍。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「in（不）+ fertile（肥）」——不肥的、不长东西的 → 贫瘠的；不能生育的

1.root: 拉丁 in-「不」+ fertilis「丰产的」← ferre「携带、承载」+ -ilis「能……的」；晚期拉丁 infertilis 为加缀构词。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all say one thing: the power to produce is absent. The absence is then located in a person, an animal, a plant, the land, the soil, a gamete, a debate and finally a mind.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项说的都是同一件事：出产的能力缺席。这个「缺席」随后被安置到人、动物、植物、土地、土壤、配子、辩论，最后是心智上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a cracked slope where nothing can take root.
core.cn: 核心意象：一片裂开的坡地，什么都扎不下根。

branches.en: HUMAN MEDICINE: the plain clinical denial of the ability to conceive.
branches.cn: 人类医学：对受孕能力最直接的临床否定。

branches.en: ANIMAL BREEDING: the same denial, usually with a stated cause such as inbreeding.
branches.cn: 动物繁殖：同样的否定，通常带有近亲繁殖等成因。

branches.en: BOTANY: the oldest agricultural sense, moved from soil to seed set.
branches.cn: 植物学：最古老的农业义，只是对象从土壤换成结种。

branches.en: LAND AND SOIL: ground that cannot bear a crop, first as a farming fact, then as a chemical one.
branches.cn: 土地与土壤：不能承载庄稼的地，先是耕作事实，后是化学状态。

branches.en: DOWN TO CELLS AND OUT TO THOUGHT: gametes, arguments and imaginations can all be called infertile.
branches.cn: 向下到细胞、向外到思想：配子、辩论与想象力都可以被称为贫瘠。

intro.en: Infertile is a prefix plus an adjective, and its prefix is the standard Latin negation whose shape changes with the following consonant.
intro.cn: infertile 是一个前缀加一个形容词，其前缀是标准的拉丁否定成分，词形随后接辅音而变化。

latinIntro.en: Latin in- 'not' plus fertilis gives infertilis; English -ity later formed the noun infertility.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 in-「不」加 fertilis 构成 infertilis；英语再用 -ity 构成名词 infertility。

items.example: The prefix stays in- before f, as in infertile.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀在 f 前保持 in-，如 infertile。

items.meaningCN: 不（在 l 前的同化形式）
items.example: Illegal and illogical show this shape.
items.exampleCN: illegal 与 illogical 显示了这一变形。

items.structure: in- assimilated before p, b, m
items.meaningCN: 不（在 p、b、m 前的同化形式）
items.example: Impossible and immature use im-.
items.exampleCN: impossible 与 immature 用 im-。

items.meaningCN: 不（在 r 前的同化形式）
items.example: Irregular and irreversible show ir-.
items.exampleCN: irregular 与 irreversible 用 ir-。

items.meaning: the state of being unable to conceive
items.example: Infertility affects roughly one couple in six.
items.exampleCN: 大约每六对夫妇中有一对受不育困扰。

items.meaningCN: 贫瘠地；不能生育地（-ly 构成副词）
items.example: The plot yielded infertilely for years.
items.exampleCN: 这块地多年来产量极低。

items.example: The river's silt keeps the fields fertile.
items.exampleCN: 河里的泥沙让田地保持肥沃。

items.meaning: to make free of germs; to make unable to reproduce
items.meaningCN: 杀菌；使绝育（-ize 表示使……化）
items.example: The tools were sterilized before use.
items.exampleCN: 器械在使用前经过消毒。

2.definition_en: the wearing away and removal of topsoil by water, wind or human activity
2.core_image: 暴雨后的坡面出现一道道浅沟，表土顺水滑走，露出下面的石砾
2.scene: 暴雨过后，田边新出现几道浅浅的沟，冲走的表土堆在坡脚。Heavy rain strips the slope, and soil erosion leaves deep ruts across the field.
2.sceneCN: 这里 soil erosion 指「表土被水或风剥离并搬走的过程」（第 1 个义项：土壤流失这一整体过程）；句意为暴雨冲刷坡面，土壤侵蚀在田里留下深沟。可辨识物件：坡面浅沟、被带走的表土、坡脚的泥堆、裸露的石砾。

pos.zh: 不可数名词：土壤侵蚀；水土流失

senses.title: The general process of losing topsoil
senses.definition: the process by which the upper layer of soil is detached and carried away
senses.definitionCN: 土壤上层被剥离并搬运走的过程
senses.example: Heavy rain strips the slope, and soil erosion leaves deep ruts across the field.
senses.exampleCN: 暴雨冲刷坡面，土壤侵蚀在田里留下深沟。
senses.why: soil names the material and erosion names the act of gnawing away, so the phrase reads as 'the ground being eaten back'.
senses.whyCN: soil 指材料，erosion 指被一点点啃掉的动作，因此这个短语字面上就是「地面被啃回去」。

senses.title: Erosion by running water
senses.definition: the removal of soil by rainwash, rills, streams or rivers
senses.definitionCN: 雨水、细沟、小河或河流搬走土壤
senses.example: Water erosion peaks in the first storm after ploughing.
senses.exampleCN: 水蚀在翻耕后的第一场暴雨中达到高峰。
senses.why: water is the commonest agent, and the phrase is routinely divided into water erosion and wind erosion to name the agent.
senses.whyCN: 水是最常见的营力，因此这个短语常被分成水蚀与风蚀，用来指明营力。

senses.title: Erosion by wind
senses.titleCN: 风蚀：风力搬运造成的侵蚀
senses.definition: the removal of loose dry soil by wind, common in flat and arid land
senses.definitionCN: 干燥疏松的土壤被风搬走，常见于平坦干旱地区
senses.example: Wind erosion removes the finest particles first.
senses.exampleCN: 风蚀先带走最细的颗粒。
senses.why: where vegetation is thin and the surface is dry, air does the work that water does elsewhere, so the phrase pairs with wind.
senses.whyCN: 在植被稀疏、地表干燥的地方，风干了别处由水干的事，因此这个短语与 wind 搭配。

senses.title: Sheet erosion: a whole surface thinned
senses.titleCN: 片蚀：整片地表被均匀削薄
senses.definition: the even removal of a thin layer of soil across a whole slope
senses.definitionCN: 整面坡地上薄薄一层土壤被均匀剥去
senses.example: Sheet erosion is easy to miss because no channel forms.
senses.exampleCN: 片蚀很难被察觉，因为并没有形成沟道。
senses.why: when the rain is steady and the slope is even, the loss is spread over the surface and leaves no trace, hence the name sheet.
senses.whyCN: 当降雨平稳、坡面均匀时，流失会摊在整面上而不留痕迹，因此得名「片」。

senses.title: Gully erosion: channels cut deep
senses.definition: the concentrated removal of soil that cuts channels too deep to plough across
senses.definitionCN: 土壤被集中冲走，切出深到无法横耕的沟道
senses.example: Gully erosion can swallow a track in a single season.
senses.exampleCN: 沟蚀能在一个季节里吞掉一条小路。
senses.why: once water collects into a line, it cuts downward instead of spreading, so the phrase marks the stage where a rill becomes a gully.
senses.whyCN: 一旦水汇成一线，它便向下切而不是摊开，因此这个短语标记了细沟变成冲沟的阶段。

senses.title: Erosion accelerated by land use
senses.definition: the sharp increase in soil loss caused by clearing, ploughing or overgrazing
senses.definitionCN: 因清林、翻耕或过度放牧造成的土壤流失急剧增加
senses.example: Accelerated soil erosion followed the clearing of the catchment.
senses.exampleCN: 集水区的森林被清掉之后，土壤侵蚀随之加速。
senses.why: geologists compare the human rate with the natural background rate, and the phrase carries the word accelerated whenever people are the cause.
senses.whyCN: 地质学家把人为速率与自然背景速率相比，只要成因是人，这个短语就会带上 accelerated 一词。

senses.title: Off-site damage from eroded soil
senses.titleCN: 流失土壤造成的异地危害
senses.definition: the harm done where eroded soil is deposited, such as silted rivers and buried roads
senses.definitionCN: 流失土壤沉积处造成的危害，如河道淤积与道路被埋
senses.example: Soil erosion upstream silted the reservoir within a decade.
senses.exampleCN: 上游的土壤侵蚀在十年内就让水库淤积。
senses.why: the damage is felt where the soil lands rather than where it leaves, so the phrase also names an off-site problem.
senses.whyCN: 损害发生在土壤落下的地方而非离开的地方，因此这个短语也指一种异地问题。

senses.title: Abstract: any foundation worn away
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：任何根基被一点点磨掉
senses.definition: used figuratively for the slow loss of the base that supports something
senses.definitionCN: 比喻用法，指支撑某事物的根基缓慢流失
senses.example: Trust suffered its own soil erosion as promises went unmet.
senses.exampleCN: 承诺屡屡落空，信任也经历了它自己的「水土流失」。
senses.why: erosion is a slow, invisible wearing away, which makes it a ready metaphor for any support that disappears by degrees.
senses.whyCN: 侵蚀是缓慢而不易察觉的消磨，因此很容易成为「支撑一点点消失」的比喻。

intro.en: Soil erosion joins a Latin noun for ground to a Latin noun of gnawing away; both halves entered English through French. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: soil erosion 把一个表示「地面」的拉丁名词与一个表示「啃掉」的拉丁名词并置；两部分都经法语进入英语。年代均为约数。

items.en: Solum meant 'ground, floor, bottom'. Old French turned it into soil 'a piece of ground', which English borrowed in the thirteenth century; the farming sense of tilled earth followed.
items.cn: solum 意为「地面、地板、底部」。古法语把它变成 soil「一块地」，英语在十三世纪借入；随后才出现「耕作的泥土」这一农业义。

items.en: The verb soil 'to make dirty' comes from Old French souillier, probably from Latin sullus or an unrelated source; it is not the same word as the noun soil and has nothing to do with erosion.
items.cn: 动词 soil「弄脏」来自古法语 souillier，可能出自拉丁 sullus，也可能另有来源；它与名词 soil 不是同一个词，与侵蚀也无关。

items.en: Erodere 'to gnaw away, consume' was built from e- 'out' and rodere 'to gnaw', the same verb that gives rodent and corrode.
items.cn: erodere「啃掉、消耗」由 e-「出」与 rodere「啃」构成，后者也衍生 rodent 与 corrode。

items.en: English erosion appears in the early seventeenth century as a medical and general word for a gnawing sore, then widened to any gradual wearing away.
items.cn: 英语 erosion 在十七世纪初出现，先是医学与一般用语，指啃噬性的溃烂，随后扩展到任何缓慢的磨损。

items.en: Nineteenth-century geology fixed erosion as the technical name for the wearing down of land by water, ice and wind, and the compound soil erosion followed as the agricultural and engineering form.
items.cn: 十九世纪的地质学把 erosion 固定为水、冰、风磨蚀地表的专业名称，随后才有 soil erosion 这一农业与工程说法。

items.en: Source uncertain: the first appearance of the exact phrase soil erosion is not well recorded, and the deeper Indo-European origin of rodere is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定：soil erosion 这一确切短语的首见记录不详；rodere 更深的印欧语来源属重构形式。

note.en: Group one holds the terms built on the same erosion stock; group two holds processes that remove rock or soil but in a different way.
note.cn: 第一组是同出 erosion 词干的术语；第二组是同样移除岩石或土壤、但机制不同的过程。

entries.definition: Wearing away of rock or land in general; soil erosion specifies that the material lost is topsoil.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指岩石或地面的磨蚀；soil erosion 特指流失物是表土。

entries.definition: Having the power to erode; it describes the force, not the loss of soil.
entries.definitionCN: 有侵蚀力的；它形容营力，而不指土壤流失。

entries.definition: The measured quantity of soil removed; soil erosion names the process that produces that quantity.
entries.definitionCN: 被移走的土壤数量；soil erosion 指造成这一数量的过程。

entries.definition: The extremely slow downhill drift of soil under gravity; it is not the same as erosion and often has no flowing agent.
entries.definitionCN: 土壤在重力下极缓慢地下移；它与侵蚀不同，往往没有流动营力。

entries.definition: The breaking up of rock where it stands; erosion then removes the pieces, so the two are stages rather than synonyms.
entries.definitionCN: 岩石在原地破碎；侵蚀随后把碎块搬走，因此两者是阶段关系而非同义。

entries.definition: The total process by which a landscape is stripped and lowered; soil erosion is one part of it.
entries.definitionCN: 地景被剥离并降低的总过程；土壤侵蚀只是其中一部分。

entries.definition: Land turning into desert; severe soil erosion is one route to that outcome, not the outcome itself.
entries.definitionCN: 土地变成荒漠；严重的土壤侵蚀是通向该结果的路径之一，而非结果本身。

entries.definition: The depositing of the material that erosion removed; it names where the soil goes, not where it came from.
entries.definitionCN: 被侵蚀移走的物质重新沉积；它指土壤去了哪里，而非来自哪里。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Latin parts, the real agent words and the real sub-types used by soil scientists.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的拉丁成分、真实的营力词，以及土壤学家实际使用的亚类名称。

normal.en: soil 'ground' + erosion 'gnawing away': the ground being eaten back.
normal.cn: soil「地面」+ erosion「啃掉」：地面被一点点啃回去。

normal.en: e- 'out' + rodere 'gnaw' gives erosion; rodent comes from the same gnawing verb.
normal.cn: e-「出」+ rodere「啃」构成 erosion；rodent 也出自同一个「啃」动词。

normal.en: Fixed agent phrases: water erosion, wind erosion; fixed scales: sheet erosion, gully erosion.
normal.cn: 固定营力搭配：水蚀、风蚀；固定尺度：片蚀、沟蚀。

normal.en: The culprit pairs are accelerated and severe: accelerated soil erosion, severe soil erosion.
normal.cn: 常见修饰搭配是与 accelerated、severe 连用：加速的土壤侵蚀、严重的土壤侵蚀。

normal.en: Remember the noun soil is unrelated to the verb soil 'to dirty'.
normal.cn: 记住：名词 soil 与动词 soil「弄脏」无关。

abstract.en: Picture a field losing one thin slice of itself with every storm.
abstract.cn: 想象一块田，每场暴雨都削掉薄薄一层。

abstract.en: Picture a river below the slope carrying away what the hill used to be.
abstract.cn: 想象坡下的河带走了这座山丘曾经的自己。

abstract.en: Picture a promise worn away not by one blow but by many small rains.
abstract.cn: 想象一个承诺不是被一击打碎，而是被许多小雨一点点磨掉。

examples.en: Terracing is the oldest defence against soil erosion on steep land.
examples.cn: 梯田是陡坡地上最古老的抗蚀措施。

examples.en: Soil erosion reduces both yields and water quality.
examples.cn: 土壤侵蚀既降低产量，也降低水质。

examples.en: The project pays farmers to keep cover crops that limit soil erosion.
examples.cn: 该项目付钱给农民，让他们保留限制土壤侵蚀的覆盖作物。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「soil（土）+ e（出去）+ rosion（揉损）」——土被一点点带出去、磨掉 → 土壤侵蚀

2.root: soil 来自拉丁 solum「地面」（经古法语）；erosion 来自拉丁 erodere「啃掉」← e-「出」+ rodere「啃」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one loss: soil is detached, the agent is water or wind, the shape is a sheet or a gully, people accelerate it, the damage lands downstream, and finally any foundation can wear away the same way.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一场流失展开：土壤被剥离，营力是水或风，形态是片状或沟状，人为因素使其加速，危害落在下游，最后任何根基都能以同样方式被磨掉。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a slope after a storm, thin channels cut into it and the lost earth piled at the foot.
core.cn: 核心意象：暴雨后的坡面，被切出一道道细沟，流失的土堆在坡脚。

branches.en: THE WHOLE PROCESS: material named first, removal named second.
branches.cn: 整体过程：先说材料，再说被搬走。

branches.en: THE AGENT: water does the work in wet climates, wind in dry ones.
branches.cn: 营力：湿润地区靠水，干旱地区靠风。

branches.en: THE SHAPE: even sheets hide the loss, concentrated lines cut gullies.
branches.cn: 形态：均匀片状掩盖流失，集中成线则切出冲沟。

branches.en: THE HUMAN RATE: clearing and ploughing push the loss far past its natural pace.
branches.cn: 人为速率：清林与翻耕把流失推得远超自然速度。

branches.en: WHERE IT LANDS AND WHAT IT MEANS: silt downstream, and any support worn away by degrees.
branches.cn: 落点与引申：下游淤积，以及任何支撑被一点点磨掉。

intro.en: The phrase is two free nouns, but both halves still show their Latin make-up: solum for ground, e- plus rodere for gnawing away.
intro.cn: 这个短语是两个自由名词的组合，但两部分都仍能看出拉丁构词：solum 表示地面，e- 加 rodere 表示啃掉。

latinIntro.en: Latin solum gives soil and solifluction; erodere gives erode, erosion and erosive; rodere also gives rodent, corrode and erode.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 solum 衍生 soil 与 solifluction；erodere 衍生 erode、erosion、erosive；rodere 还衍生 rodent、corrode、erode。

items.meaning: to wear away by gradual removal
items.meaningCN: 侵蚀；逐步削弱（e- 表示「出」，rod- 表示「啃」）
items.example: Waves erode the cliff a little each winter.
items.exampleCN: 海浪每年冬天都侵蚀一点崖壁。

items.meaningCN: 侵蚀过程（-ion 表示过程）
items.example: Erosion cut the bank back by a metre.
items.exampleCN: 侵蚀把河岸掏退了一米。

items.meaningCN: 有侵蚀力的（-ive 表示具有性质）
items.example: Fast water is the most erosive agent here.
items.exampleCN: 急流是这里侵蚀力最强的营力。

items.meaningCN: 侵蚀形成的（-al 表示与……相关）
items.example: An erosional valley has a V-shaped profile.
items.exampleCN: 侵蚀谷呈 V 形剖面。

items.example: The soil here is barely a hand deep.
items.exampleCN: 这里的土层还不到一掌深。

items.meaningCN: 表土（最上面的一层沃土）
items.example: Topsoil washes off first.
items.exampleCN: 表土最先被冲走。

items.example: Subsoil holds little organic matter.
items.exampleCN: 底土含有机质很少。

items.meaningCN: 啮齿动物（rod- 表示「啃」，-ent 表示施动者）
items.example: Rodents gnaw to wear down their teeth.
items.exampleCN: 啮齿动物靠啃咬磨牙。

items.meaning: to eat away gradually, as rust does
items.meaningCN: 腐蚀（cor- 表示「彻底」，rod- 表示「啃」）
items.example: Salt corrodes the metal frame.
items.exampleCN: 盐分腐蚀了金属框架。

3.definition_zh: 冲积的；由流水沉积形成的；淤积的
3.definition_en: made of or relating to material that running water has carried and then deposited
3.core_image: 河湾退水后留下的一层细腻黑泥，光滑得像刚抹过
3.scene: 河湾的田里，拖拉机翻起一层细腻的黑土，那是洪水年年留下的。The farm sits on alluvial ground laid down by the river over centuries.
3.sceneCN: 这里 alluvial 指「由河流搬运并沉积形成的」（第 1 个义项：流水携带的泥沙堆积而成）；句意为这座农场建在河流数百年沉积出的冲积地上。可辨识物件：河湾、翻起的细土、犁沟、远处的河道。

pos.zh: 冲积的；由流水沉积形成的；淤积的

forms.label: 相关形容词（洪积的，成因不同）

senses.title: Deposited by running water
senses.definition: formed from material that a river or stream carried and then dropped
senses.definitionCN: 由河流或溪流搬运后落下的物质形成的
senses.example: The farm sits on alluvial ground laid down by the river over centuries.
senses.exampleCN: 这座农场建在河流数百年沉积出的冲积地上。
senses.why: the Latin verb behind the word means 'to wash against', so alluvial material is literally what water washed into place and left.
senses.whyCN: 这个词背后的拉丁动词意为「冲刷到……上」，因此冲积物字面上就是水冲刷过来又留下的东西。

senses.title: Fine, layered, fertile soil
senses.definition: of soil, fine-grained, sorted into layers and usually rich in nutrients
senses.definitionCN: 指土壤颗粒细、分成层理，且通常养分充足
senses.example: Alluvial soil holds water well and ploughs easily.
senses.exampleCN: 冲积土保水好，也容易耕。
senses.why: water sorts grains by size as it slows, so what settles is fine and well mixed, which is exactly what crops like.
senses.whyCN: 水在减速时按颗粒大小分选，因此沉下来的土细而均匀，正好适合作物。

senses.title: An alluvial plain
senses.definition: a wide flat plain built up by sediment spread across a valley floor
senses.definitionCN: 由泥沙铺在谷底堆高而成的宽阔平地
senses.example: Rice dominates the alluvial plain below the hills.
senses.exampleCN: 丘陵以下的冲积平原上以水稻为主。
senses.why: when a river repeatedly floods the same floor, the layers add up into a plain, and the adjective names its origin rather than its shape.
senses.whyCN: 当河流反复淹同一片谷底，层理累积成平原，这个形容词说明的是它的来源而非形状。

senses.title: An alluvial fan
senses.definition: a fan-shaped deposit where a steep stream spreads out onto flatter ground
senses.definitionCN: 陡坡上的水流到平缓地面散开时形成的扇形沉积
senses.example: The village stands on an alluvial fan at the gorge mouth.
senses.exampleCN: 村子坐落在峡口的一处冲积扇上。
senses.why: where the slope suddenly ends, the water loses speed and drops its load in a fan, so the adjective marks both origin and geometry.
senses.whyCN: 坡度突然结束时，水流减速并把载荷摊成扇形，因此这个形容词同时标记来源与几何形状。

senses.title: Placer deposits: gold in river gravel
senses.definition: of minerals concentrated in river gravel because they are heavy and settle out
senses.definitionCN: 指因比重大而在河流砾石中富集下来的矿物
senses.example: Alluvial gold was panned from the gravel bars.
senses.exampleCN: 人们从砾石滩里淘洗冲积金。
senses.why: a heavy grain sinks while lighter sand washes on, so river gravel becomes the natural concentrator that miners call a placer.
senses.whyCN: 重的颗粒下沉，轻的沙子被冲走，于是河流砾石成了天然的富集器，采矿者称之为砂矿。

senses.title: An alluvial aquifer
senses.definition: of groundwater stored in sand and gravel deposited by a river
senses.definitionCN: 指储存在河流沉积的砂砾中的地下水
senses.example: Wells tap the alluvial aquifer beneath the valley.
senses.exampleCN: 水井开采谷底下的冲积含水层。
senses.why: river gravel is porous and permeable, so it holds water that can be pumped, and hydrogeology names such a body by its origin.
senses.whyCN: 河流砾石多孔且透水，能储水并可供抽取，水文地质学便按成因给这类水体命名。

senses.title: Land gained by accretion in law
senses.titleCN: 法律：因淤积而新增的土地
senses.definition: of land slowly added to a river bank by deposition, which the owner may gain title to
senses.definitionCN: 指因沉积缓慢添加到河岸、所有者可能取得所有权的土地
senses.example: The boundary follows the alluvial strip added since the survey.
senses.exampleCN: 边界线沿测量之后新增的冲积地带划定。
senses.why: property law separates land gained slowly by water from land cut off suddenly, and it reserves the word alluvial for the slow addition.
senses.whyCN: 财产法把水慢慢添上的土地与突然被切走的土地区分开，只用 alluvial 指前者。

senses.title: Layers that bury an ancient site
senses.titleCN: 考古：掩埋遗址的冲积层
senses.definition: of sediment layers that covered and preserved an archaeological site
senses.definitionCN: 指覆盖并保存了考古遗址的沉积层
senses.example: The pottery lay under three metres of alluvial silt.
senses.exampleCN: 那些陶器埋在三米厚的冲积粉砂之下。
senses.why: floodplains bury what people leave, so archaeologists read alluvial layers as both a clock and a protective lid.
senses.whyCN: 洪泛平原会把人的遗留物埋起来，因此考古学家把冲积层既看作时钟，也看作保护盖。

intro.en: Alluvial is a Latin adjective of washing, borrowed into English in the eighteenth century through scientific writing. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: alluvial 是一个表示「冲刷」的拉丁形容词，十八世纪经科学文献借入英语。年代均为约数。

items.en: Alluere 'to wash against, flow to' was built from ad- 'to, toward' and luere 'to wash'. The same luere underlies abluere 'to wash off', which gives ablution.
items.cn: alluere「冲刷、流向」由 ad-「朝向」与 luere「洗」构成。同一个 luere 也构成 abluere「洗去」，后者衍生 ablution。

items.en: Alluvies meant 'an inundation, a washing against'; the adjective alluvius 'alluvial' and the noun alluvio came from it.
items.cn: alluvies 意为「泛滥、冲刷」；形容词 alluvius「冲积的」与名词 alluvio 都由它而来。

items.en: Latin has two verbs spelled luere: one means 'to wash', the other 'to pay, atone'. Alluvial belongs to the washing one; the atoning one gives the legal sense of 'expiation', not this word.
items.cn: 拉丁语有两个拼作 luere 的动词：一个意为「洗」，另一个意为「偿付、赎罪」。alluvial 属于「洗」那一个；「赎罪」那一个衍生的是法律上的「抵偿」，与本词无关。

items.en: English borrowed alluvium in the seventeenth century for matter deposited by flowing water; the adjective alluvial followed in the eighteenth.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪借入 alluvium，指流水沉积的物质；形容词 alluvial 在十八世纪随后进入。

items.en: Geology fixed phrases such as alluvial fan and alluvial plain in the nineteenth century, while property law kept alluvial land for the slow addition of soil to a bank.
items.cn: 地质学在十九世纪固定了 alluvial fan、alluvial plain 等说法，而财产法则用 alluvial land 指土壤缓慢添加到河岸的土地。

items.en: Source uncertain: the first English use of the adjective is dated only approximately, and the deeper Indo-European root of luere 'to wash' is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定：这个形容词的英语首见只有约略年代；luere「洗」更深的印欧词根属重构形式。

note.en: Group one holds words that look similar but name different deposits; group two holds the related geological adjectives by agent.
note.cn: 第一组是外形相近但所指沉积不同的词；第二组是按营力区分的相关地质形容词。

entries.definition: Hinting indirectly; from Latin alludere 'to play with', built on ludere 'to play', not on luere 'to wash'.
entries.definitionCN: 暗示的；间接提及的；来自拉丁 alludere「戏弄」，建于 ludere「玩弄」之上，而非 luere「洗」。

entries.definition: The deposit itself; alluvial describes material of that origin.
entries.definitionCN: 指沉积物本身；alluvial 形容具有这一来源的物质。

entries.definition: A specific fan-shaped deposit; the bare adjective applies to any water-laid material.
entries.definitionCN: 特指扇形沉积体；单用的形容词可指任何流水沉积物。

entries.definition: Of material washed downward into a lower soil layer; the movement is into the profile, not onto the surface.
entries.definitionCN: 指被淋洗进下层土壤的物质；运移方向是进入剖面内部，而不是铺到地表。

entries.definition: Relating to a river or its action; alluvial specifically describes what the river left behind.
entries.definitionCN: 与河流或其作用有关的；alluvial 特指河流留下的东西。

entries.definition: Of material moved downhill by gravity and slope wash; it never travelled in a channel.
entries.definitionCN: 指由重力和坡面冲刷下移的物质；它从未在河道中运移。

entries.definition: Of deposits attributed to a great flood; an older geological term now largely replaced by alluvial for river work.
entries.definitionCN: 指被认为由大洪水造成的沉积；这是较老的地质术语，河流成因现在多用 alluvial。

entries.definition: Of rock formed from deposited material of any agent; alluvial is one narrow source within that class.
entries.definitionCN: 指由任何营力的沉积物形成的岩石；alluvial 只是这一大类中的一个窄来源。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Latin verb, the real landform phrases and the real contrast with colluvial.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的拉丁动词、真实的地貌搭配，以及与前塌积的对比。

normal.en: al- 'to' + luere 'wash': washed onto a place and left there.
normal.cn: al-「向」+ luere「洗」：冲洗到某处并留在那里。

normal.en: The noun family: alluvium, alluvion, alluvia, alluvial.
normal.cn: 名词词族：alluvium、alluvion、alluvia、alluvial。

normal.en: Landform phrases: alluvial fan, alluvial plain, alluvial terrace.
normal.cn: 地貌搭配：冲积扇、冲积平原、冲积阶地。

normal.en: Economic phrases: alluvial gold, alluvial diamond, alluvial tin.
normal.cn: 经济搭配：砂金、砂钻、砂锡。

normal.en: Contrast pairs: water lays alluvial material, gravity lays colluvial material.
normal.cn: 对比记忆：水铺下冲积物，重力铺下崩积物。

abstract.en: Picture a river writing its history in layers, one flood per page.
abstract.cn: 想象一条河把自己的历史写成层理，一次洪水就是一页。

abstract.en: Picture a fan of sand opening where the mountain gives up its slope.
abstract.cn: 想象山势陡然放开处展开的一把沙扇。

abstract.en: Picture gold hiding in gravel because it was too heavy to be carried on.
abstract.cn: 想象金子藏在砾石里，因为它太重而没能被继续带走。

examples.en: Alluvial deposits along the delta are several metres thick.
examples.cn: 三角洲一带的冲积层有好几米厚。

examples.en: The alluvial plain supports two harvests a year.
examples.cn: 这片冲积平原一年可以收两季。

examples.en: Miners followed the alluvial gravel upstream.
examples.cn: 采矿者沿冲积砾石向上游追索。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿（a）+ 露（llu）+ 维（vi）+ 尔（al）」——河水露过一遍留下的泥 → 冲积的

3.root: 拉丁 alluvius「冲积的」← alluere「冲刷」← ad-「向」+ luere「洗」；名词 alluvies「泛滥」同源。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one deposit from its making to its uses: water lays material down, that material makes soil, plains and fans; it concentrates gold and stores water; law and archaeology then read the same layers for ownership and for time.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一沉积从形成到用途展开：水把物质铺下，这些物质造出土壤、平原与冲积扇；它富集金子、储存地下水；法律与考古再从同一层理读出所有权与年代。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a river laying down a smooth dark layer of silt after the flood goes down.
core.cn: 核心意象：洪水退去后，河流铺下一层细腻的黑泥。

branches.en: MATERIAL AND SOIL: the plain reading, then the properties that make it good farmland.
branches.cn: 物质与土壤：最朴素的读法，随后是使它宜耕的性质。

branches.en: LANDFORMS: a flat plain on the valley floor and a fan at the mountain front.
branches.cn: 地貌：谷底的平平原与山前的扇形地。

branches.en: RESOURCES: heavy minerals concentrate as placers, and porous gravel stores groundwater.
branches.cn: 资源：重矿物富集成砂矿，多孔砾石储存地下水。

branches.en: LAW: slow addition to a bank becomes a question of title.
branches.cn: 法律：缓慢添加的河岸变成所有权问题。

branches.en: ARCHAEOLOGY: the same layers both bury and date what people left.
branches.cn: 考古：同样的层理既掩埋也标定人的遗留物。

intro.en: Alluvial is a Latin participle stem plus an adjective suffix, and the family divides cleanly into the washing root and the resulting deposit nouns.
intro.cn: alluvial 是一个拉丁分词词干加形容词后缀，其词族清楚地分成「洗」的词根与由此产生的沉积名词。

latinIntro.en: Alluere gives alluvius and alluvio; the root lu- 'wash' also appears in abluere, from which English takes ablution.
latinIntro.cn: alluere 衍生 alluvius 与 alluvio；词根 lu-「洗」也出现在 abluere 中，英语由此得到 ablution。

items.meaningCN: 流水沉积物（-ium 构成物质名词）
items.example: The valley floor is deep alluvium.
items.exampleCN: 谷底是深厚的冲积物。

items.meaning: the act of washing up; land so formed
items.meaningCN: 淤积作用；由此形成的土地
items.example: The alluvion added several metres to the bank.
items.exampleCN: 淤积让河岸向前长了好几米。

items.meaningCN: 以冲积方式（-ly 构成副词）
items.example: The basin filled alluvially.
items.exampleCN: 这个盆地以冲积方式填高。

items.example: Fluvial transport sorts the grains.
items.exampleCN: 河流搬运把颗粒分选开来。

items.meaning: deposited by gravity on a slope
items.meaningCN: 崩积的；坡面重力堆积的
items.example: Colluvial soil collects at the foot of the cliff.
items.exampleCN: 崩积土在崖脚堆积。

items.meaningCN: 洪积的；与大洪水沉积有关的
items.example: The old diluvial theory was replaced.
items.exampleCN: 旧的洪积说已被取代。

items.structure: Old English lafian, from Latin lavare
items.example: The verb survives mainly in poetry.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词主要残留在诗歌中。

items.meaning: a washing, especially a ritual one
items.example: The rite begins with ablution.
items.exampleCN: 仪式从净洗开始。

4.definition_zh: 天文学；对天体与宇宙的观测与研究
4.definition_en: the science that studies stars, planets and other bodies beyond the Earth
4.core_image: 圆顶屋在夜里打开，望远镜缓缓转向，记录册上画着月亮的一格格位置
4.scene: 天文台的圆顶在夜里打开，学生轮流守着望远镜，记录月亮每晚的位置。Students here learn astronomy by tracking the Moon across the sky each night.
4.sceneCN: 这里 astronomy 指「研究天体与宇宙的天文学」（第 1 个义项：以观测与理论描述天体的学科）；句意为这里的学生通过每晚追踪月亮来学习天文学。可辨识物件：圆顶、望远镜、记录册、月相草图。

pos.zh: 不可数名词：天文学；天文观测与研究

senses.title: The science of celestial bodies
senses.definition: the branch of science that studies the positions, motions and nature of celestial bodies
senses.definitionCN: 研究天体位置、运动与性质的科学分支
senses.example: Students here learn astronomy by tracking the Moon across the sky each night.
senses.exampleCN: 这里的学生通过每晚追踪月亮来学习天文学。
senses.why: Greek astronomia joined astron 'star' to -nomia 'arranging, law', so the word began as the ordered account of the stars rather than a general curiosity about the sky.
senses.whyCN: 希腊 astronomia 把 astron「星」与 -nomia「安排、法则」结合，因此这个词最初是「对星辰的有序记述」，而非对天空的一般好奇。

senses.title: The practice of observing the sky
senses.definition: the activity of observing and recording celestial events systematically
senses.definitionCN: 系统地观察并记录天象的活动
senses.example: Winter astronomy here means long nights and clear cold air.
senses.exampleCN: 在这里，冬季天文意味着长夜与清冷的空气。
senses.why: the discipline is built on watching, so the same noun also names the nightly work rather than only the field of study.
senses.whyCN: 这门学科建立在观看之上，因此同一个名词也指夜复一夜的工作，而不只是研究领域。

senses.title: A subject taught in school
senses.definition: a course or subject in which the science of celestial bodies is taught
senses.definitionCN: 讲授天体知识的课程或科目
senses.example: Astronomy is offered as an elective in the second year.
senses.exampleCN: 天文学在第二年作为选修课开设。
senses.why: when a science enters a curriculum it takes its proper name as a subject label, which is why the word appears on timetables unchanged.
senses.whyCN: 当一门科学进入课程，它就以专名作为科目名称，因此这个词原封不动地出现在课表上。

senses.title: Positional astronomy: measuring the sky
senses.titleCN: 方位天文学：测量天体位置
senses.definition: the branch that measures positions and motions of celestial objects with great precision
senses.definitionCN: 以极高精度测量天体位置与运动的分支
senses.example: Positional astronomy supplies the frame for every other observation.
senses.exampleCN: 方位天文学为其他一切观测提供坐标框架。
senses.why: the oldest task is simply to say where a body is and when, so measurement became a named branch while physics came later.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的任务只是说出天体在哪里、在何时，因此测量先成为一个有名称的分支，物理学则更晚。

senses.title: Radio and infrared astronomy
senses.titleCN: 射电天文学等非可见光分支
senses.definition: the branches that observe wavelengths the eye cannot see, from radio waves to infrared
senses.definitionCN: 观测肉眼看不见的波段（从射电波到红外）的分支
senses.example: Radio astronomy revealed jets that optical telescopes miss.
senses.exampleCN: 射电天文学揭示了光学望远镜看不到的喷流。
senses.why: once detectors extended the eye beyond visible light, the discipline split into bands, each keeping astronomy in its name.
senses.whyCN: 当探测器把眼睛延伸到可见光之外，这门学科便按波段分家，每一支都在名称里保留 astronomy。

senses.title: Amateur astronomy
senses.definition: sky observation carried out by enthusiasts outside professional institutions
senses.definitionCN: 专业机构之外的爱好者所作的天空观测
senses.example: Amateur astronomy still discovers comets and variable stars.
senses.exampleCN: 业余天文仍在发现彗星与变星。
senses.why: the field depends on many eyes, so a word that names a profession also names a hobby pursued with the same instruments.
senses.whyCN: 这个领域依赖众多眼睛，因此一个本指专业的词也指用同样仪器从事的爱好。

senses.title: A culture's ordered knowledge of the sky
senses.titleCN: 某一文化对天空的系统知识
senses.definition: the body of sky knowledge, calendars and star lore built up by a particular culture
senses.definitionCN: 某一文化积累的天空知识、历法与星象传统
senses.example: Polynesian astronomy guided voyages across open ocean.
senses.exampleCN: 波利尼西亚的天文知识指引了穿越外海的航行。
senses.why: before the modern discipline existed, the same ordering work was done inside cultures, so historians extend the word backward to their star lore.
senses.whyCN: 在现代学科出现之前，同样的整理工作在各文化内部进行，因此史学家把这个词回溯用于他们的星象知识。

senses.title: Space-based astronomy
senses.titleCN: 空间天文：在大气层外观测
senses.definition: observation carried out by instruments placed above the Earth's atmosphere
senses.definitionCN: 由置于地球大气层之上的仪器进行的观测
senses.example: Space-based astronomy escapes the blurring of the air.
senses.exampleCN: 空间天文摆脱了大气的模糊效应。
senses.why: leaving the atmosphere removes the distortion that ground telescopes fight, so the place of the instrument became another named branch.
senses.whyCN: 离开大气层就消除了地面望远镜要对抗的畸变，因此仪器所在的位置又成了一个有名称的分支。

intro.en: Astronomy is a Greek compound that reached English through Latin and French, and its second element concerns law and arrangement rather than writing about stars. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: astronomy 是一个希腊复合词，经拉丁语与法语进入英语；它的第二部分讲的是法则与安排，而不是「书写星辰」。年代均为约数。

items.en: Astronomia meant 'astronomy' and also 'the arrangement of the stars'. It joined astron 'star' to -nomia, from nemein 'to distribute, apportion, manage'.
items.cn: astronomia 意为「天文学」，也指「星辰的安排」。它把 astron「星」与 -nomia 结合，后者来自 nemein「分配、分派、管理」。

items.en: Astron came from aster 'star', whose diminutive asteriskos gives English asterisk and whose compound asteriskos also names a small star-shaped mark.
items.cn: astron 来自 aster「星」，其指小形式 asteriskos 衍生英语 asterisk，也指一种星形小符号。

items.en: The suffix -nomia also appears in economy and autonomy, where it still carries the sense of managing or laying down a law; astronomy is therefore 'the law of the stars'.
items.cn: 后缀 -nomia 也出现在 economy 与 autonomy 中，仍带「管理」或「立规」的意思；因此 astronomy 是「星辰的法则」。

items.en: Latin borrowed the Greek noun as astronomia, Old French reshaped it as astronomie, and Middle English took it over in the late fourteenth century.
items.cn: 拉丁语把希腊名词借作 astronomia，古法语改写为 astronomie，中古中古英语在十四世纪末接收了这个词。

items.en: From the seventeenth century the field split into positional, optical and later radio astronomy, while astrophysics took over the physics of the same bodies.
items.cn: 从十七世纪起，这个领域分出了方位天文、光学天文，后来又分出射电天文，而同一天体的物理学则归入天体物理学。

items.en: Source uncertain: the exact first English citation is not firmly identified, though the word is usually placed in the late fourteenth century; the earliest Greek use of astron for star is a reconstruction from later texts.
items.cn: 来源不确定：英语首见的确切出处尚未确定，但通常定在十四世纪末；希腊语中 astron「星」的最早用法是根据后世文本作出的重构。

note.en: Group one separates astronomy from the words it is most often confused with; group two holds neighbouring sciences of the same sky.
note.cn: 第一组把 astronomy 与最常混淆的词分开；第二组是同一天空下的邻近学科。

entries.definition: The reading of stars as signs affecting human affairs; it shares astron but replaces -nomia 'law' with -logia 'discourse'.
entries.definitionCN: 把星辰当作影响人事的征兆来解读；它共享 astron，但把 -nomia「法则」换成了 -logia「论说」。

entries.definition: One who studies or observes celestial bodies; the noun ending -er marks the practitioner.
entries.definitionCN: 研究或观测天体的人；-er 结尾标记从业者。

entries.definition: A traveller in space; built from astro- 'star' and nautes 'sailor', so it means 'star sailor'.
entries.definitionCN: 太空旅行者；由 astro-「星」与 nautes「水手」构成，意为「星际水手」。

entries.definition: The precise measurement of celestial positions; -metry is 'measurement', not the whole discipline.
entries.definitionCN: 对天体位置的精密测量；-metry 意为「测量」，并不指整门学科。

entries.definition: The physics of stars and galaxies; astronomy observes and maps, astrophysics explains the mechanisms.
entries.definitionCN: 研究恒星与星系的物理学；天文学负责观测与制图，天体物理学解释机制。

entries.definition: The study of the origin and structure of the universe; it is a branch of astronomy with a much wider scope.
entries.definitionCN: 研究宇宙起源与结构；它是天文学的一个分支，但范围大得多。

entries.definition: The mathematical study of the motions of bodies under gravity; it supplies astronomy's predictions.
entries.definitionCN: 用数学研究天体在引力下的运动；它为天文学提供预测。

entries.definition: Traditional knowledge about the sky held by a community; it overlaps with sense seven but carries no method.
entries.definitionCN: 某一群体持有的传统天空知识；它与第七义项重叠，但不含方法。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Greek parts, the real sibling words and the real branch names.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的希腊成分、真实的同族词与真实的分支名称。

normal.en: astron 'star' + nomia 'law': the law of the stars, not the love of the stars.
normal.cn: astron「星」+ nomia「法则」：星辰的法则，而不是对星辰的爱好。

normal.en: The family splits three ways: astronomy, astronomer, astronomical.
normal.cn: 词族分三路：astronomy、astronomer、astronomical。

normal.en: -nomy marks a law or system, as in economy and autonomy; -logy marks discourse, as in astrology.
normal.cn: -nomy 标记法则或体系，如 economy、autonomy；-logy 标记论说，如 astrology。

normal.en: Branch phrases: radio astronomy, optical astronomy, positional astronomy, space-based astronomy.
normal.cn: 分支搭配：射电天文学、光学天文学、方位天文学、空间天文。

normal.en: Astronomy observes; astrophysics explains; cosmology asks about the whole.
normal.cn: 天文学观测；天体物理学解释；宇宙学追问整体。

abstract.en: Picture a dome opening like an eye at dusk.
abstract.cn: 想象黄昏时圆顶像一只眼睛那样张开。

abstract.en: Picture a single star's position written down night after night until a path appears.
abstract.cn: 想象一夜夜记下一颗星的位置，直到一条轨迹浮现。

abstract.en: Picture the sky as a page ruled with invisible lines, waiting to be read.
abstract.cn: 想象天空是一页画着无形横线的纸，等着被读。

examples.en: Astronomy began as calendar-keeping and became a physical science.
examples.cn: 天文学始于编历，后来成为一门物理科学。

examples.en: She took astronomy to learn how distances are measured.
examples.cn: 她选修天文学，是为了了解距离如何测量。

examples.en: Radio astronomy opened a window that had been closed for centuries.
examples.cn: 射电天文学打开了一扇关闭了数个世纪的窗。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿（a）+ 斯（s）+ 戳（tro）+ 诺（no）+ 米（my）」——在夜里戳着星记法 → 天文学

4.root: 希腊 astronomia ← astron「星」（来自 aster）+ -nomia「法则、安排」（来自 nemein「分配、管理」）；经拉丁 astronomia 与古法语进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one ordered account of the sky: the discipline, the nightly work, the school subject, the measuring branch, the non-visible bands, the amateur, the culture's lore and the instrument placed above the air.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一份「天空的有序记述」展开：学科本身、夜间工作、学校科目、测量分支、不可见波段、业余爱好者、文化传统，以及置于大气层之上的仪器。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a dome opening at night while a telescope writes a star's path into a notebook.
core.cn: 核心意象：夜里圆顶打开，望远镜把一颗星的轨迹写进记录册。

branches.en: THE DISCIPLINE: the ordered account of the stars, which is the dictionary reading.
branches.cn: 学科：对星辰的有序记述，也就是词典义。

branches.en: WORK AND SCHOOL: the same noun names the nightly practice and the timetable slot.
branches.cn: 工作与课堂：同一个名词既指夜间实践，也指课表上的一格。

branches.en: BANDS AND METHODS: measuring positions first, then watching wavelengths the eye cannot see.
branches.cn: 波段与方法：先测量位置，再观测肉眼看不见的波段。

branches.en: WHO DOES IT: professionals and amateurs, and cultures that ordered the sky before the science existed.
branches.cn: 谁在做：专业者与爱好者，以及在学科出现之前就已整理天空的文化。

branches.en: WHERE THE INSTRUMENT SITS: above the atmosphere, the air stops blurring the view.
branches.cn: 仪器在哪里：置于大气层之上，空气便不再模糊视野。

intro.en: Astronomy is a Greek compound of two bound forms, and its second form is shared with words about law and management.
intro.cn: astronomy 是由两个粘着成分构成的希腊复合词，其中第二个成分与表示法则、管理的词共享。

latinIntro.en: Latin took the Greek noun as astronomia and also used astrum for 'star'; English drew both on the Greek side and on the Latin.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语把希腊名词借作 astronomia，也用 astrum 表示「星」；英语则同时取自希腊与拉丁两面。

items.structure: Greek astron (star) used as a combining form
items.example: Astrobiology asks whether life exists elsewhere.
items.exampleCN: 天体生物学追问别处是否存在生命。

items.meaningCN: 法则或管理体系（来自 nemein「分配」）
items.example: Economy and autonomy share this ending.
items.exampleCN: economy 与 autonomy 共享这个结尾。

items.example: Astrology uses this ending, astronomy does not.
items.exampleCN: astrology 用这个结尾，astronomy 不用。

items.meaningCN: 天文学家（-er 表示从业者）
items.example: The astronomer logged the transit.
items.exampleCN: 天文学家记录了凌日。

items.meaningCN: 天文学的；也指极其巨大的
items.example: The cost was astronomical.
items.exampleCN: 费用高得惊人。

items.meaningCN: 天体测量学（-metry 表示测量）
items.example: Astrometry fixes the reference frame.
items.exampleCN: 天体测量学确定参考框架。

items.meaningCN: 宇航员（字面义「星际水手」）
items.example: The astronaut described the view.
items.exampleCN: 宇航员描述了那番景象。

items.example: An asterisk marks the footnote.
items.exampleCN: 星号标出脚注。

latinEntries.structure: aster, asteris (noun, third declension, from Greek)

5.definition_zh: 天文学的；天文上的；（数量、价格）极其巨大的
5.definition_en: relating to astronomy, or (of an amount) extremely large
5.core_image: 屏幕上跳出一串长得读不完的数字，研究者盯着它愣了几秒
5.scene: 夜里，研究者盯着屏幕上一串长长的数字，那是到邻近星系的测算结果。The distance to the next galaxy is astronomical, far beyond any earthly scale.
5.sceneCN: 这里 astronomical 指「（数量）极其巨大、超出日常尺度」（第 3 个义项：借天文尺度形容极大）；句意为到下一个星系的距离极其巨大，远超地面尺度。可辨识物件：屏幕上的长串数字、星图、观测记录、台灯。

pos.zh: 天文学的；天文上的；（数量、价格）极其巨大的

senses.title: Relating to astronomy
senses.definition: of or connected with the science of celestial bodies
senses.definitionCN: 与天体科学有关的
senses.example: The library holds a rare astronomical atlas.
senses.exampleCN: 这家图书馆藏有一册珍稀的天文图集。
senses.why: the adjective simply attaches -ical 'relating to' to astronomy, so its first job is to name the field it belongs to.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词只是把表示「与……相关」的 -ical 接到 astronomy 上，因此它的首要作用是指明所属领域。

senses.title: Measured on a celestial scale
senses.definition: of distances or units used for bodies beyond the Earth
senses.definitionCN: 指用于地球之外天体的距离或单位
senses.example: One astronomical unit is the mean distance from Earth to the Sun.
senses.exampleCN: 一个天文单位是地球到太阳的平均距离。
senses.why: when ordinary units become unwieldy, the field defines its own, and the adjective marks that specialised scale.
senses.whyCN: 当常用单位变得笨重，这一领域便自定单位，而这个形容词标记的就是那套专用尺度。

senses.title: Impossibly large, in everyday speech
senses.titleCN: 日常口语中的「极其巨大」
senses.definition: of an amount, distance or number, so large that it is hard to imagine
senses.definitionCN: 指数量、距离或数字大到难以想象
senses.example: The distance to the next galaxy is astronomical, far beyond any earthly scale.
senses.exampleCN: 到下一个星系的距离极其巨大，远超地面尺度。
senses.why: the figurative jump is natural: what is literally measured in astronomical units is, to ordinary minds, simply enormous.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻跳跃很自然：凡真正以天文单位计量的东西，对日常心智而言就只是「巨大得离谱」。

senses.title: A price beyond reason
senses.definition: of a cost, far higher than is reasonable or expected
senses.definitionCN: 指费用远高于合理或预期水平
senses.example: The repair bill was astronomical for a broken hinge.
senses.exampleCN: 不过是一个坏合页，修理费却高得离谱。
senses.why: money is the commonest everyday quantity, so the loose sense settled on prices and fees before on anything else.
senses.whyCN: 钱是日常最常见的数量，因此这个宽松义先落在价格与费用上，然后才用到别处。

senses.title: Of observations and instruments
senses.definition: describing observations, data or instruments used in the science
senses.definitionCN: 形容该学科所用的观测、数据或仪器
senses.example: Astronomical data were pooled across three continents.
senses.exampleCN: 三个大洲的天文数据被汇总到一起。
senses.why: the adjective marks anything that belongs to observing work, which is why it sits before data and instruments so often.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词标记属于观测工作的一切，因此常出现在 data 与 instrument 之前。

senses.title: An astronomical clock
senses.titleCN: 天文钟：显示天体位置的机械钟
senses.definition: of a clock that shows the positions of the Sun, Moon or planets as well as the time
senses.definitionCN: 指除时间外还能显示日、月或行星位置的钟
senses.example: The cathedral's astronomical clock still turns after six centuries.
senses.exampleCN: 大教堂的天文钟过了六个世纪仍在转动。
senses.why: the name is literal: the dial carries a sky map, so the clock is astronomical in what it displays, not in size.
senses.whyCN: 这个名称是字面的：表盘上带着星图，因此这座钟的「天文」在于它显示的内容，而不是尺寸。

senses.title: The astronomical year
senses.definition: of the year measured from equinox to equinox, used in older calendars
senses.definitionCN: 指从春分点到下一春分点量出的年，用于较早的历法
senses.example: The astronomical year is a few minutes shorter than the calendar year.
senses.exampleCN: 天文年比日历年短几分钟。
senses.why: astronomers needed a year defined by the sky rather than by decree, so the adjective distinguishes the measured year from the civil one.
senses.whyCN: 天文学家需要一个由天空而非由政令定义的年，因此这个形容词把实测年与民用年区分开。

senses.title: Numbers too large to compare
senses.titleCN: 数值大到无法直观比较
senses.definition: of figures, so far outside ordinary range that comparison loses meaning
senses.definitionCN: 指数值远超日常范围，比较已失去意义
senses.example: The possible combinations are astronomical, not merely large.
senses.exampleCN: 可能的组合数大到无法比较，而不只是「多」。
senses.why: the word does not just mean big; it means big in the way sky distances are big, beyond the scale that intuition can hold.
senses.whyCN: 这个词不只是「大」，而是像星空距离那样大，超出直觉能把握的尺度。

senses.title: Odds so small they seem impossible
senses.definition: of a probability, so slight that the event seems practically impossible
senses.definitionCN: 指概率极小，事情近乎不可能发生
senses.example: The odds of that alignment are astronomical.
senses.exampleCN: 那种排列出现的概率小得近乎不可能。
senses.why: the same word serves both extremes because both lie outside human scale, which is why astronomical odds and astronomical costs sound equally natural.
senses.whyCN: 同一个词能用于两个极端，因为两端都超出人的尺度，所以「天文数字般的概率」与「天文数字般的费用」听起来同样自然。

intro.en: Astronomical is the adjective of astronomy, formed in Latin and Greek and later extended to mean 'vast'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: astronomical 是 astronomy 的形容词，在拉丁与希腊语中成形，后来扩展出「巨大」的意思。年代均为约数。

items.en: Greek astronomikos meant 'of astronomy', built from astronomia with the adjective suffix -ikos 'relating to'.
items.cn: 希腊 astronomikos 意为「天文学的」，由 astronomia 加形容词后缀 -ikos「与……相关」构成。

items.en: Late Latin took the Greek adjective as astronomicus; English formed astronomical by adding -al to the same stem, so astronomic and astronomical are doublets.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语把希腊形容词借作 astronomicus；英语在同一词干上加 -al 构成 astronomical，因此 astronomic 与 astronomical 是同源双重形式。

items.en: English records astronomical in the sixteenth century in the plain sense 'of astronomy', used of tables, instruments and observations.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪记录到 astronomical 的朴素义「天文学的」，用于表格、仪器与观测。

items.en: The sense 'extremely large' is generally dated to the nineteenth century, when popular writing about sky distances began to use the adjective as a synonym for immense.
items.cn: 「极其巨大」这一义项一般认为是十九世纪出现的，当时关于星空距离的通俗写作开始把这个形容词当作「巨大」的同义词。

items.en: Technical phrases fixed the literal uses: astronomical unit for the Earth-Sun distance, astronomical clock for a dial showing the sky, astronomical year for the equinox year.
items.cn: 技术搭配固定了字面用法：astronomical unit 指地日距离，astronomical clock 指显示天空的表盘，astronomical year 指分至年。

items.en: Source uncertain: the exact decade when the 'huge' sense became common is not firmly established, and the first English citation of the adjective is dated only approximately.
items.cn: 来源不确定：「巨大」义普及的确切年代没有定论；这个形容词的英语首见只有约略年代。

note.en: Group one holds the closely spelled variants and neighbours; group two holds the words that also mean very large, each with a different flavour.
note.cn: 第一组是拼写接近的变体与邻词；第二组是同样表示「很大」的词，各自语感不同。

entries.definition: The shorter Latin-derived adjective; it is rare outside older scientific writing and shares the same two senses.
entries.definitionCN: 较短的拉丁来源形容词；除较早的科学文献外很少见，两个义项相同。

entries.definition: A defined distance, not a vague largeness; the adjective here is literal and technical.
entries.definitionCN: 一个有定义的距离，不是笼统的「大」；这里的形容词是字面技术义。

entries.definition: The science itself; astronomical is what belongs to it or what resembles its scale.
entries.definitionCN: 学科本身；astronomical 指属于它的，或与其尺度相似的。

entries.definition: Relating to star signs and their supposed influence; the ending -logical replaces -nomical.
entries.definitionCN: 与星座及其所谓影响有关的；结尾 -logical 取代了 -nomical。

entries.definition: Very large in size or degree; it describes bulk, while astronomical suggests a scale beyond intuition.
entries.definitionCN: 体积或程度很大；它描述体量，而 astronomical 暗示超出直觉的尺度。

entries.definition: Extremely great in extent; it is more formal than enormous and less technical than astronomical.
entries.definitionCN: 范围极大；比 enormous 正式，但不如 astronomical 技术化。

entries.definition: Of gigantic size, originally of a giant statue; it keeps a physical, almost visual force.
entries.definitionCN: 巨大的，原指巨型雕像；保留着物理的、近乎视觉上的力量。

entries.definition: Of a charge, unreasonably high; it is the precise word when the huge number is money.
entries.definitionCN: 指收费高得不合理；当巨大的数字是钱时，这个词最精确。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real suffix, the real technical phrases and the real pair with enormity.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的后缀、真实的技术搭配，以及与「巨大」类词的对比。

normal.en: astronomy + -ical: belonging to the study of stars.
normal.cn: astronomy + -ical：属于星辰之学的。

normal.en: astronomic and astronomical are doublets, both from astronomicus.
normal.cn: astronomic 与 astronomical 是同源双重形式，都来自 astronomicus。

normal.en: Technical phrases: astronomical unit, astronomical clock, astronomical year.
normal.cn: 技术搭配：天文单位、天文钟、天文年。

normal.en: Everyday phrases: astronomical cost, astronomical odds, astronomical figure.
normal.cn: 日常搭配：天文数字般的费用、概率、数值。

normal.en: Keep the literal and the figurative apart: a unit is literal, a bill is figurative.
normal.cn: 把字面义与比喻义分开：单位是字面义，账单是比喻义。

abstract.en: Picture a number so long that the screen must scroll to show it.
abstract.cn: 想象一个长得屏幕必须滚动才能显示完的数字。

abstract.en: Picture a coin so large that the whole town stands on its edge.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚大到全城都站在它边缘上的硬币。

abstract.en: Picture odds so small that a lifetime of trying would still miss them.
abstract.cn: 想象概率小到穷尽一生也碰不上。

examples.en: Astronomical observations now come from orbiting telescopes.
examples.cn: 如今的天文观测来自在轨望远镜。

examples.en: The hotel charges astronomical prices during the festival.
examples.cn: 节庆期间这家酒店收费高得离谱。

examples.en: In astronomical terms, the comet passed almost inside our atmosphere.
examples.cn: 从天文学尺度看，那颗彗星几乎是贴着大气层掠过。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿（a）+ 斯戳（stro）+ 诺米（nomi）+ 扣（cal）」——数字大得像天上的星 → 天文数字般的

5.root: 希腊 astronomikos「天文学的」← astronomia + -ikos；晚期拉丁 astronomicus，英语加 -al 构成 astronomical。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses start from the literal link to astronomy, pass through units, instruments and the astronomical year, then widen into huge distances, huge prices, huge figures and tiny odds, all because they lie outside human scale.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项从与天文学的字面联系出发，经过单位、仪器与天文年，再扩展到巨大距离、高昂价格、庞大数据与极小概率，原因都是它们超出人的尺度。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a string of digits on a screen so long that it outgrows the room.
core.cn: 核心意象：屏幕上的一串数字长得超出这间屋子。

branches.en: LITERAL FIELD: belongs to astronomy, and to its observations and data.
branches.cn: 字面领域：属于天文学，也属于它的观测与数据。

branches.en: FIXED TECHNICAL USES: a unit of distance, a sky-showing clock, a measured year.
branches.cn: 固定技术用法：距离单位、显示天空的钟、实测年。

branches.en: SCALE BEYOND INTUITION: distances so great that ordinary words fail.
branches.cn: 超出直觉的尺度：距离大到常用词失效。

branches.en: HUGE NUMBERS IN LIFE: prices and figures borrow the same scale.
branches.cn: 生活中的巨大数字：价格与数值借用同一尺度。

branches.en: THE OTHER EXTREME: probabilities so small that the event seems impossible.
branches.cn: 另一个极端：概率小到事情近乎不可能。

intro.en: Astronomical is a Greek stem with a Latin adjective ending, and it competes with a shorter doublet formed without -al.
intro.cn: astronomical 是希腊词干加拉丁形容词词尾，并与一个不带 -al 的较短同源形式并存竞争。

latinIntro.en: Late Latin astronomicus supplies both English astronomic and astronomical; the suffix -alis / -al is the ordinary Latin means of turning a noun into an adjective.
latinIntro.cn: 晚期拉丁 astronomicus 同时提供英语 astronomic 与 astronomical；后缀 -alis / -al 是拉丁语把名词变形容词的常规手段。

items.meaningCN: 把名词变为形容词（表示「与……相关」）
items.example: Astronomy gives astronomical by this ending.
items.exampleCN: astronomy 靠这个后缀构成 astronomical。

items.meaning: relating to, of the nature of
items.example: Historical and historical share this shape.
items.exampleCN: historic 与 historical 共享这一形式。

items.example: Older texts prefer astronomic.
items.exampleCN: 较早的文本更常用 astronomic。

items.example: The project is astronomically expensive.
items.exampleCN: 这个项目贵得惊人。

items.meaningCN: 天文单位（地日平均距离）
items.example: The comet's orbit reaches sixty astronomical units.
items.exampleCN: 这颗彗星的轨道远达六十个天文单位。

items.meaningCN: 天文钟（显示天体位置的钟）
items.example: The astronomical clock has four dials.
items.exampleCN: 这座天文钟有四个表盘。

items.example: The astronomical year is measured by the equinoxes.
items.exampleCN: 天文年以分至点来量度。

items.example: Astrometry fixes star positions precisely.
items.exampleCN: 天体测量学精确测定恒星位置。

6.definition_zh: 天文学家；研究或观测天体的人
6.definition_en: a person who studies or observes stars, planets and other celestial bodies
6.core_image: 夜里一个人裹着厚外套站在圆顶下，手扶镜筒等云散开
6.scene: 夜里，一位研究者裹着厚外套，在圆顶下调整镜筒，等云层散开。The astronomer waits under the dome until the clouds finally clear.
6.sceneCN: 这里 astronomer 指「以观测和研究天体为业的人」（第 1 个义项：天文学家这一职业身份）；句意为这位天文学家在圆顶下等待，直到云层终于散开。可辨识物件：圆顶、镜筒、厚外套、云层。

pos.zh: 可数名词：天文学家；天文研究者

forms.label: 相关职业（天体物理学家）

derivatives.zh: 皇家天文学家（英国宫廷职位）

senses.title: A professional who studies the sky
senses.titleCN: 以研究天体为职业的人
senses.definition: a scientist whose profession is the study of celestial bodies and phenomena
senses.definitionCN: 以研究天体及其现象为职业的科学家
senses.example: The astronomer waits under the dome until the clouds finally clear.
senses.exampleCN: 这位天文学家在圆顶下等待，直到云层终于散开。
senses.why: the Greek source already meant 'one who arranges the stars', so the agent noun names a person whose work is to put the sky in order.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语源头本义就是「安排星辰的人」，因此这个施动名词指以整理天空为工作的人。

senses.title: The person at the eyepiece
senses.definition: a person who actually observes through a telescope, as opposed to one who only works on theory
senses.definitionCN: 实际通过望远镜观测的人，相对只做理论工作的人
senses.example: The observing astronomer logged forty measurements before dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 观测天文学家在黎明前记录了四十次测量。
senses.why: in an observatory the word often shifts from the profession to the shift, because someone must sit at the instrument all night.
senses.whyCN: 在天文台里，这个词常从「职业」滑向「班次」，因为总得有人整夜守在仪器旁。

senses.title: The catalogue builder
senses.definition: historically, a person who compiles tables of star positions and magnitudes
senses.definitionCN: 历史上编制恒星位置与星等表的人
senses.example: The medieval astronomer listed a thousand stars by hand.
senses.exampleCN: 中世纪的天文学家用手工列出了一千颗星。
senses.why: before photography and computers, the visible product of the profession was a catalogue, so the title belonged to anyone who made one.
senses.whyCN: 在摄影与计算机出现之前，这一行业可见的成果就是星表，因此凡是编出星表的人都能得到这个称号。

senses.title: A radio astronomer
senses.definition: a specialist who observes celestial objects at radio wavelengths
senses.definitionCN: 以射电波段观测天体的专家
senses.example: Radio astronomers mapped gas clouds the eye cannot see.
senses.exampleCN: 射电天文学家绘制出了肉眼看不见的气体云。
senses.why: once the discipline split by wavelength, the compound put the band before the person's title.
senses.whyCN: 当学科按波段分家，复合词就把波段放在职业称谓之前。

senses.title: An amateur astronomer
senses.definition: an enthusiast who observes the sky without holding a professional post
senses.definitionCN: 不担任专业职位而观测天空的爱好者
senses.example: Amateur astronomers reported the outburst first.
senses.exampleCN: 业余天文爱好者最先报告了那次爆发。
senses.why: the same word covers the hobby because the work, looking and recording, is identical whether or not anyone is paid.
senses.whyCN: 同一个词也覆盖这一爱好，因为无论是否有人付钱，「看与记」这件事完全相同。

senses.title: The specialist for one object
senses.titleCN: 专攻某一类天体的研究者
senses.definition: a researcher identified by the kind of body studied, as a planetary or solar astronomer
senses.definitionCN: 按所研究天体类别称呼的研究者，如行星天文学家或太阳天文学家
senses.example: A planetary astronomer joined the mission team.
senses.exampleCN: 一位行星天文学家加入了这次任务团队。
senses.why: modern teams divide by object, and the word attaches to the specialism rather than to the general field.
senses.whyCN: 现代团队按对象分工，这个词便附着在专长上，而不是泛指整个领域。

senses.title: Institutional title in a court
senses.titleCN: 宫廷或国家设置的官方天文职位
senses.definition: a formal post such as Astronomer Royal, held at a court or state observatory
senses.definitionCN: 如皇家天文学家这类设于宫廷或国家天文台的正式职位
senses.example: The Astronomer Royal answered directly to the monarch.
senses.exampleCN: 皇家天文学家直接向君主负责。
senses.why: when states needed calendars and navigation tables, the skill became an office, and the title passed into institutional language.
senses.whyCN: 当国家需要历法与航海表，这门技艺就变成一个官职，称号也随之进入制度语言。

senses.title: Figurative: one who reads far-off signs
senses.titleCN: 比喻义：能从远处迹象读出规律的人
senses.definition: used figuratively for someone who reads distant or faint patterns carefully
senses.definitionCN: 比喻用法，指能仔细读出遥远或微弱迹象的人
senses.example: As an astronomer of market cycles, she watched small signals for years.
senses.exampleCN: 她像研究市场周期的天文学家，多年只盯微小的信号。
senses.why: the image is patience and distance: an astronomer cannot touch the object, only its light, and the metaphor keeps that detachment.
senses.whyCN: 这个意象关乎耐心与距离：天文学家碰不到对象，只能读它的光，比喻保留的正是这种隔空观察。

intro.en: Astronomer is a Greek agent noun that entered English through Latin and French; for a time it covered stargazers of every kind. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: astronomer 是一个希腊施动名词，经拉丁语与法语进入英语；有一段时间它能指任何看星的人。年代均为约数。

items.en: Greek astronomos meant 'arranging the stars', built from astron 'star' and nemein 'to distribute, apportion, manage'; the word described the ordering work before it named a person.
items.cn: 希腊 astronomos 意为「安排星辰的」，由 astron「星」与 nemein「分配、分派、管理」构成；这个词先描述整理的工夫，后才指人。

items.en: Latin took the Greek word as astronomus, a noun of the second declension, and used it for anyone skilled in star knowledge.
items.cn: 拉丁语把希腊词借作 astronomus，属第二变格法名词，用来指任何精通星辰知识的人。

items.en: Old French formed astronomien with the French agent ending -ien; Middle English borrowed this shape in the late fourteenth century.
items.cn: 古法语用本族施动后缀 -ien 构成 astronomien；中古英语在十四世纪末借入了这一形式。

items.en: English replaced the French ending with its own -er, the same agent suffix as in baker and writer, giving the modern astronomer.
items.cn: 英语用本族的 -er 替换法语词尾，这个施动后缀与 baker、writer 相同，于是形成现代形式 astronomer。

items.en: The two titles overlapped for several centuries: an astronomer could mean a forecaster by the stars, and the modern split between astronomy and astrology is generally dated to the seventeenth century.
items.cn: 这两个称号重叠了好几个世纪：astronomer 也曾指靠星辰预测的人；天文学与占星学的现代分工一般认为是十七世纪才确立的。

items.en: Source uncertain: the precise date when astronomer lost its predictive sense is not settled, and the earliest Greek use of astronomos as a personal title rests on limited texts.
items.cn: 来源不确定：astronomer 何时失去预测义没有确切年代；希腊 astronomos 最早作为个人称号的用法依据的文本有限。

note.en: Group one holds titles that differ by a suffix; group two holds the neighbouring experts of the same sky.
note.cn: 第一组是只差后缀的称号；第二组是同一天空下的邻近专家。

entries.definition: The reading of stars as signs; its practitioner is an astrologer, not an astronomer.
entries.definitionCN: 把星辰当作征兆来解读；其从业者叫 astrologer，而不是 astronomer。

entries.definition: A person who interprets star signs; it looks like astronomer but the -log- root marks a different discipline.
entries.definitionCN: 解读星座征兆的人；外形像 astronomer，但 -log- 词根标记的是另一门行当。

entries.definition: The science itself; astronomer is the person who works in it.
entries.definitionCN: 学科本身；astronomer 是在其中工作的人。

entries.definition: A space traveller; the second element is nautes 'sailor', not nemein 'to arrange'.
entries.definitionCN: 太空旅行者；第二部分是 nautes「水手」，不是 nemein「安排」。

entries.definition: A specialist in the physics of celestial bodies; an astronomer may observe, while an astrophysicist must explain the mechanism.
entries.definitionCN: 研究天体物理的专家；天文学家可以只做观测，而天体物理学家必须解释机制。

entries.definition: A specialist in the origin and large-scale structure of the universe, a narrower and grander brief.
entries.definitionCN: 研究宇宙起源与大尺度结构的专家，职责更窄也更大。

entries.definition: The building and instruments where astronomers work; the word names the site rather than the practitioner.
entries.definitionCN: 天文学家工作的建筑与仪器；这个词指场所而非从业者。
