entries.definition: An informal name for anyone who watches the sky, professional or not; astronomer is the formal title.
entries.definitionCN: 对任何看天的人的通俗称呼，不论是否专业；astronomer 是正式称号。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Greek parts, the real agent suffix and the real professional distinctions.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的希腊成分、真实的施动后缀与真实的职业区分。

normal.en: astron 'star' + nemos 'arranging' + -er 'person': the star-arranger.
normal.cn: astron「星」+ nemos「安排」+ -er「人」：安排星辰的人。

normal.en: The family runs astronomy, astronomer, astronomical, astronomically.
normal.cn: 词族包括 astronomy、astronomer、astronomical、astronomically。

normal.en: Title phrases: Astronomer Royal, amateur astronomer, radio astronomer.
normal.cn: 称号搭配：皇家天文学家、业余天文爱好者、射电天文学家。

normal.en: Keep astronomer and astrologer apart: -nomer orders the sky, -loger reads it as signs.
normal.cn: 把 astronomer 与 astrologer 分开：前者整理天空，后者把天空读作征兆。

normal.en: An astronomer observes; an astrophysicist explains; a cosmologist generalises.
normal.cn: 天文学家观测；天体物理学家解释；宇宙学家作整体概括。

abstract.en: Picture someone standing all night simply to let one point of light cross a hairline.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人整夜站着，只为让一个光点划过一根细线。

abstract.en: Picture a notebook filling with numbers that no one else will read for a century.
abstract.cn: 想象一本笔记本写满数字，要过一个世纪才有人去读。

abstract.en: Picture a person who knows every star by name but can never touch one.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人叫得出每颗星的名字，却永远碰不到它们。

examples.en: The astronomer published the orbit after twenty years of measurement.
examples.cn: 这位天文学家在测量二十年后公布了那条轨道。

examples.en: Astronomers now share data instead of guarding it.
examples.cn: 如今的天文学家共享数据，而不再把它藏起来。

examples.en: She became an astronomer because a neighbour lent her a small telescope.
examples.cn: 她成为天文学家，起因是邻居借给她一架小望远镜。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿（a）+ 斯戳（stro）+ 诺默（nomer）」——默默记下星星位置的人 → 天文学家

6.root: 希腊 astronomos「安排星辰的」← astron「星」+ nemein「分配、管理」；经拉丁 astronomus 与古法语 astronomien，英语换用 -er。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses revolve around one working person: the profession, the night shift at the eyepiece, the catalogue maker, the radio specialist, the amateur, the object specialist, the state office and finally anyone who reads distant signals patiently.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕同一个「做事的人」展开：职业身份、目镜前的夜班、编制星表者、射电专家、业余爱好者、按对象分工的专家、国家官职，最后是任何耐心读远处信号的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person at a cold eyepiece, waiting for one point of light.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人守在冰冷的目镜前，等一个光点。

branches.en: THE WORKER: the profession first, then the person actually on shift.
branches.cn: 从业者：先是职业，后是真正值班的人。

branches.en: THE PRODUCT: whoever produces the catalogue earns the title.
branches.cn: 产物：谁编出星表，谁就得到这个称号。

branches.en: DIVISIONS OF LABOUR: by wavelength, by payment, by object.
branches.cn: 分工：按波段、按是否有报酬、按研究对象。

branches.en: THE OFFICE: state and court turn the skill into a formal post.
branches.cn: 官职：国家与宫廷把技艺变成正式职位。

branches.en: THE METAPHOR: patient reading of distant signs in any field.
branches.cn: 比喻：在任何领域耐心读取远处的迹象。

intro.en: Astronomer is the Greek stem plus the ordinary English agent suffix, and that suffix is what makes it a person rather than a science.
intro.cn: astronomer 是希腊词干加普通英语施动后缀，正是这个后缀使它指人而不指学科。

latinIntro.en: Latin astronomus supplies the stem, and English -er replaces the French -ien; the agent suffix is native Germanic.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 astronomus 提供词干，英语用本族 -er 替换法语 -ien；这个施动后缀属日耳曼本族。

items.example: Baker, writer and astronomer share it.
items.exampleCN: baker、writer 与 astronomer 共享这个后缀。

items.meaningCN: 从事……的人（古法语施动后缀）
items.example: Astronomien was the older French shape.
items.exampleCN: astronomien 是较早的法语形式。

items.example: Latin kept the Greek ending -us.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语保留了希腊词尾 -us。

items.example: Astronomy is the field, astronomer the person.
items.exampleCN: astronomy 是学科，astronomer 是人。

items.example: The observatory cost an astronomical sum.
items.exampleCN: 这座天文台耗资巨大。

items.meaning: one who reads stars as signs
items.meaningCN: 占星者（把星辰读作征兆的人）
items.example: Astrologer differs from astronomer by its root.
items.exampleCN: astrologer 与 astronomer 的不同在词根。

items.example: Astrometry serves every observer.
items.exampleCN: 天体测量服务于每一位观测者。

items.example: The astronaut trained for two years.
items.exampleCN: 这位宇航员训练了两年。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 无人（与希腊 nemein 无关，仅拼写相近）

7.definition_en: the branch of science that applies physics to stars, galaxies and other celestial bodies
7.core_image: 一条光谱曲线在屏幕上展开，暗线一道道标出元素的名字
7.scene: 屏幕上一条光谱曲线缓缓展开，研究者标出各条吸收线的位置。Astrophysics explains that spectrum by tracing which elements absorbed which wavelengths.
7.sceneCN: 这里 astrophysics 指「用物理定律研究天体的学科」（第 1 个义项：天体物理学这一学科）；句意为天体物理学通过追踪哪些元素吸收了哪些波长来解释这条光谱。可辨识物件：光谱曲线、吸收线标记、元素标签、观测屏。

pos.zh: 不可数名词：天体物理学

forms.label: 名词复数（天体物理学家们）

senses.title: Physics applied to celestial bodies
senses.definition: the science that applies physical laws to stars, galaxies and interstellar matter
senses.definitionCN: 把物理定律应用于恒星、星系与星际物质的科学
senses.example: Astrophysics explains that spectrum by tracing which elements absorbed which wavelengths.
senses.exampleCN: 天体物理学通过追踪哪些元素吸收了哪些波长来解释这条光谱。
senses.why: the compound is literal: astro- supplies the object, physics supplies the method, and the method is what separates it from descriptive astronomy.
senses.whyCN: 这个复合词是字面的：astro- 提供对象，physics 提供方法，而方法正是它区别于描述性天文学的地方。

senses.title: The study of stellar structure
senses.definition: the study of how stars form, burn and die, including their internal layers
senses.definitionCN: 研究恒星如何形成、燃烧与死亡，包括其内部圈层
senses.example: Stellar astrophysics predicts the colour of a star from its mass.
senses.exampleCN: 恒星天体物理学由质量预测恒星的颜色。
senses.why: stars are the commonest laboratory of the field, so the discipline's name often narrows to stellar interiors.
senses.whyCN: 恒星是这一领域最常见的实验室，因此学科名称常收窄到恒星内部。

senses.title: The analysis of radiation
senses.definition: the analysis of the light and other radiation that celestial bodies emit
senses.definitionCN: 对天体发出的光及其他辐射所作的分析
senses.example: Astrophysics reads temperature and motion from a single line.
senses.exampleCN: 天体物理学能从一条谱线读出温度与运动。
senses.why: almost all information arrives as radiation, so the physics of spectra became the core skill of the field.
senses.whyCN: 几乎所有信息都以辐射形式到达，因此光谱物理学成了这一领域的核心技能。

senses.title: High-energy astrophysics
senses.definition: the branch that studies extreme objects such as neutron stars and black holes
senses.definitionCN: 研究中子星、黑洞等极端天体的分支
senses.example: High-energy astrophysics needs detectors above the atmosphere.
senses.exampleCN: 高能天体物理需要置于大气层之上的探测器。
senses.why: when the energies involved exceed anything on Earth, the subfield takes the adjective high-energy and keeps the discipline's name.
senses.whyCN: 当涉及的能量超过地面上任何条件，这个子领域就冠以「高能」，并保留学科名称。

senses.title: Theoretical modelling
senses.definition: the branch that builds mathematical models of celestial processes
senses.definitionCN: 为天体过程建立数学模型的分支
senses.example: Theoretical astrophysics predicted the signal before it was seen.
senses.exampleCN: 理论天体物理在这道信号被看到之前就预言了它。
senses.why: the field splits into people who compute and people who measure, and the adjective theoretical marks the first half.
senses.whyCN: 这个领域分成「算的人」与「测的人」，形容词 theoretical 标记的是前一半。

senses.title: Observational astrophysics
senses.definition: the branch that tests physical models against measured data
senses.definitionCN: 用实测数据检验物理模型的分支
senses.example: Observational astrophysics confirmed the predicted cooling rate.
senses.exampleCN: 观测天体物理证实了预测的冷却速率。
senses.why: models must be checked against photons, so the observing side takes the same name with observational in front.
senses.whyCN: 模型必须用光子来检验，因此观测一侧在同一名称前加上 observational。

senses.title: A department or degree title
senses.definition: used as the name of a university department, degree or journal
senses.definitionCN: 用作大学院系、学位或期刊的名称
senses.example: The astrophysics group shares a building with the mathematicians.
senses.exampleCN: 天体物理研究组与数学系共用一栋楼。
senses.why: an established science becomes an administrative unit, and the name then labels offices, courses and journals rather than work.
senses.whyCN: 一门成熟的科学会变成一个行政单位，名称随之标记办公室、课程与期刊，而不只是研究工作。

senses.title: Particle astrophysics
senses.definition: the branch that uses neutrinos and cosmic rays to study celestial objects
senses.definitionCN: 用中微子与宇宙线研究天体的分支
senses.example: Particle astrophysics caught neutrinos from the Sun first.
senses.exampleCN: 粒子天体物理最先捕获了来自太阳的中微子。
senses.why: when the messengers are particles rather than light, a new subfield prefixes the same discipline name.
senses.whyCN: 当信使是粒子而不是光时，新的子领域就在同一学科名前加一个限定词。

intro.en: Astrophysics is a nineteenth-century compound of a Greek star prefix and a Greek-derived noun for the study of nature. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: astrophysics 是十九世纪的复合词，由一个希腊「星」前缀与一个源自希腊的「自然之学」名词组合而成。年代均为约数。

items.en: Greek physis meant 'nature' and came from phyein 'to grow, bring forth'; ta physika meant 'natural things', the title of Aristotle's lectures on nature.
items.cn: 希腊 physis 意为「自然」，来自 phyein「生长、产生」；ta physika 意为「自然之物」，是亚里士多德论自然诸篇的标题。

items.en: Latin borrowed ta physika as physica, 'natural science', which passed through French into English as physics, still covering medicine and nature in its early English use.
items.cn: 拉丁语把 ta physika 借作 physica「自然之学」，经法语进入英语成为 physics；在早期英语中它仍涵盖医学与自然。

items.en: The combining form astro- from Greek astron 'star' had already produced astronomy and astronomer before it was attached to physics.
items.cn: 来自希腊 astron「星」的组合成分 astro- 在接上 physics 之前，已经造出 astronomy 与 astronomer。

items.en: The compound astrophysics is generally dated to the mid-nineteenth century, when spectroscopy first allowed the chemical make-up of stars to be read from their light.
items.cn: 复合词 astrophysics 一般认为是十九世纪中叶所造，当时光谱学首次让人能从星光读出恒星的化学成分。

items.en: In the twentieth century astrophysics became a distinct department and degree, separate from positional astronomy, and the derived titles astrophysical and astrophysicist followed.
items.cn: 二十世纪，天体物理成为独立的系与学位，与方位天文学分开，随后衍生出 astrophysical 与 astrophysicist 两个称号。

items.en: Source uncertain: the exact first printed use of astrophysics is not firmly established, and the claim that the term was coined by a single named person has competing accounts.
items.cn: 来源不确定：astrophysics 最早的印刷用例没有定论；认为该词由某一位特定人物所造的说法存在多种版本。

note.en: Group one separates the compound from its parts and neighbours; group two holds the sciences that share the same objects or methods.
note.cn: 第一组把这个复合词与它的构件、邻词分开；第二组是对象或方法相同的邻近学科。

entries.definition: Relating to astrophysics; the noun names the field, the adjective describes work done in it.
entries.definitionCN: 与天体物理有关的；名词指学科，形容词形容在其中做的工作。

entries.definition: A practitioner of astrophysics; -ist marks the person where -ics marks the field.
entries.definitionCN: 从事天体物理的人；-ist 标记人，而 -ics 标记学科。

entries.definition: The study of celestial bodies by observation and measurement; astrophysics adds physical explanation.
entries.definitionCN: 以观测与测量研究天体；天体物理则加上物理解释。

entries.definition: The physics of the Earth; it replaces astro- with geo- and studies a completely different body.
entries.definitionCN: 研究地球的物理学；它把 astro- 换成 geo-，研究对象完全不同。

entries.definition: The study of the universe's origin and large-scale structure; it uses astrophysics but asks a wider question.
entries.definitionCN: 研究宇宙起源与大尺度结构；它使用天体物理，但追问的范围更大。

entries.definition: The physics of stars only; astrophysics also covers galaxies, gas and compact objects.
entries.definitionCN: 只研究恒星的物理；天体物理还涵盖星系、气体与致密天体。

entries.definition: The mathematics of orbital motion; it is a tool inside astrophysics rather than its whole scope.
entries.definitionCN: 轨道运动的数学；它是天体物理内部的工具，而非全部范围。

entries.definition: The physics of plasmas and fields around the Earth and planets; it stops well short of stars.
entries.definitionCN: 研究地球与行星周围的等离子体与场；范围远不到恒星。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Greek parts, the real subfield labels and the real split between observing and modelling.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的希腊成分、真实的子领域名称，以及观测与建模之间的真实分工。

normal.en: astro- 'star' + physics 'study of nature': the nature of stars.
normal.cn: astro-「星」+ physics「自然之学」：星辰的自然之理。

normal.en: The family runs astrophysics, astrophysical, astrophysicist.
normal.cn: 词族包括 astrophysics、astrophysical、astrophysicist。

normal.en: Subfield labels: theoretical, observational, high-energy, particle astrophysics.
normal.cn: 子领域名称：理论、观测、高能、粒子天体物理。

normal.en: Astronomy measures, astrophysics explains.
normal.cn: 天文学测量，天体物理学解释。

normal.en: physics itself comes from Greek physis 'nature', not from anything physical in the everyday sense.
normal.cn: physics 本身来自希腊 physis「自然」，并非日常意义上的「身体」。

abstract.en: Picture a line on a screen turning into a list of chemical elements.
abstract.cn: 想象屏幕上的一条线变成一串化学元素的名字。

abstract.en: Picture a star weighed without ever being put on a scale.
abstract.cn: 想象一颗从未上过秤却被称出重量的恒星。

abstract.en: Picture light arriving after a thousand years and still carrying its message.
abstract.cn: 想象光走了一千年到达，仍带着原来的信息。

examples.en: Astrophysics turned the stars from points of light into physical objects.
examples.cn: 天体物理把恒星从光点变成了物理对象。

examples.en: She moved from mathematics into astrophysics after a lecture on spectra.
examples.cn: 一场关于光谱的讲座之后，她从数学转入天体物理。

examples.en: Modern astrophysics relies on gravity-wave detectors as well as telescopes.
examples.cn: 现代天体物理既依靠望远镜，也依靠引力波探测器。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「astro（星星）+ physics（物理）」——用物理定律算星星 → 天体物理学

7.root: astro-（希腊 astron「星」）+ physics（希腊 physis「自然」，经拉丁 physica）；整个复合词一般认为形成于十九世纪中叶。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses narrow one method: physics applied to the sky, then to stellar interiors, then to radiation, then to extreme energies; the field splits into theory and observation, becomes an institution, and finally takes particles as its messengers.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项收窄同一种方法：物理用于天空，再用于恒星内部、辐射与极端能量；这一领域分成理论与观测，成为制度单位，最后又把粒子当作信使。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a spectrum on a screen turning into a list of elements.
core.cn: 核心意象：屏幕上的一条光谱变成一串元素名单。

branches.en: METHOD: physical law applied to light, which is nearly all the data we get.
branches.cn: 方法：把物理定律用于光，而光几乎是我们能得到的全部数据。

branches.en: OBJECT: stars are the main laboratory, so the name often narrows to them.
branches.cn: 对象：恒星是主要实验室，因此名称常收窄到恒星。

branches.en: EXTREMES AND MESSENGERS: high energies and particles open two more windows.
branches.cn: 极端与信使：高能量与粒子又打开两扇窗。

branches.en: DIVIDED LABOUR: computing models and measuring data are two halves of one field.
branches.cn: 分工：算模型与测数据是同一领域的两半。

branches.en: INSTITUTION: a science becomes a department, a degree and a journal.
branches.cn: 制度：一门科学变成系、学位与期刊。

intro.en: Astrophysics joins a Greek star prefix to a Greek noun of nature, and its ending -ics marks a discipline rather than a single thing.
intro.cn: astrophysics 把希腊「星」前缀接在希腊「自然」名词上，结尾 -ics 标记学科而非单个事物。

latinIntro.en: Latin physica, from Greek ta physika, gives physics; astron gives astro-; the compound itself is modern and has no Latin original.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 physica 来自希腊 ta physika，衍生 physics；astron 提供 astro-；这个复合词本身是现代产物，没有拉丁原形。

items.example: Astrochemistry studies molecules in space.
items.exampleCN: 天体化学研究太空中的分子。

items.structure: Latin physica, from Greek ta physika (natural things)
items.meaning: the science of matter, energy and motion
items.meaningCN: 研究物质、能量与运动的科学
items.example: Physics supplies the laws used here.
items.exampleCN: 物理学提供这里所用的定律。

items.example: The root phy- also appears in physics and physique.
items.exampleCN: 词根 phy- 也出现在 physics 与 physique 中。

items.structure: Greek -ika, neuter plural used for sciences
items.meaningCN: 一门学科（希腊中性复数后缀）
items.example: Physics, economics and ethics share this ending.
items.exampleCN: physics、economics、ethics 共享这个结尾。

items.example: The jet is an astrophysical laboratory.
items.exampleCN: 这束喷流是一个天体物理实验室。

items.example: The astrophysicist modelled the collapse.
items.exampleCN: 这位天体物理学家模拟了坍缩。

items.example: Geophysics maps the mantle.
items.exampleCN: 地球物理学绘制地幔结构。

items.example: Biophysics measures forces inside cells.
items.exampleCN: 生物物理测量细胞内部的力。

items.meaningCN: 形而上学（在物理之后、之外的研究）
items.example: The title came from an editor's shelf label.
items.exampleCN: 这个名称原是一份编书者的书架标签。

8.definition_zh: 天体物理学的；天体物理的
8.definition_en: relating to the physics of celestial bodies and the processes that occur in them
8.core_image: 新生恒星两极射出细长的喷流，远处的射电阵列把它拍成一条亮线
8.scene: 喷流从新生恒星的两极射出，远方的射电阵列把它拍成一条细长的亮线。The jet is a laboratory for astrophysical processes that no tank on Earth can reproduce.
8.sceneCN: 这里 astrophysical 指「属于天体物理过程、可用天体物理方法研究的」（第 2 个义项：恒星与星系中的物理过程）；句意为这束喷流是研究天体物理过程的实验室，地球上没有任何容器能复现。可辨识物件：新生恒星、两极喷流、射电阵列、亮线状图像。

pos.zh: 天体物理学的；天体物理的

senses.title: Relating to the discipline
senses.titleCN: 与天体物理学学科相关的
senses.definition: of or belonging to the science of astrophysics
senses.definitionCN: 属于天体物理学这门科学的
senses.example: The paper appears in an astrophysical journal.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇论文发表在一份天体物理期刊上。
senses.why: the suffix -al turns the discipline noun into an adjective, so the first sense simply marks membership in the field.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -al 把学科名词变成形容词，因此第一个义项只是标记「属于该领域」。

senses.title: Of processes in stars and galaxies
senses.titleCN: 恒星与星系中的物理过程
senses.definition: describing physical processes that occur in celestial objects
senses.definitionCN: 描述发生于天体内部的物理过程
senses.example: The jet is a laboratory for astrophysical processes that no tank on Earth can reproduce.
senses.exampleCN: 这束喷流是研究天体物理过程的实验室，地球上没有任何容器能复现。
senses.why: the adjective is most useful when it names the process rather than the department, and such processes are defined by conditions no laboratory reaches.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词最有用的用法是指过程而不是指院系，而这些过程的定义特征正是实验室无法达到的条件。

senses.title: An astrophysical jet
senses.definition: of the narrow streams of matter shot out along the poles of a young star or a black hole
senses.definitionCN: 指沿年轻恒星或黑洞两极射出的狭窄物质流
senses.example: The astrophysical jet stretches for several light years.
senses.exampleCN: 这束天体物理喷流延伸了好几个光年。
senses.why: the fixed term keeps the adjective because the jet is explained by physics no earthbound flow resembles.
senses.whyCN: 这个固定说法保留形容词，是因为这种喷流要由地球上任何流体都无法类比的物理来解释。

senses.title: An astrophysical black hole
senses.definition: of a black hole formed by the collapse of a star, as opposed to a hypothetical primordial one
senses.definitionCN: 指由恒星坍缩形成的黑洞，区别于假想的原初黑洞
senses.example: The team confirmed an astrophysical black hole, not a primordial one.
senses.exampleCN: 团队确认这是一个天体物理黑洞，而非原初黑洞。
senses.why: the adjective separates objects that actually exist in the sky from ones that only appear in theory.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词把天空中真实存在的对象与只出现在理论中的对象区分开。

senses.title: Measured quantities of a body
senses.definition: describing measurable quantities such as mass, temperature, spin or luminosity
senses.definitionCN: 形容质量、温度、自转或光度这类可测量
senses.example: Mass is the key astrophysical parameter of a star.
senses.exampleCN: 质量是恒星最关键的物理参数。
senses.why: a discipline needs a word for the numbers it actually fits, and those numbers are called its parameters.
senses.whyCN: 一门学科需要一个词来指它真正拟合的那些数，而这些数就被称为它的参数。

senses.title: Simulations of celestial systems
senses.definition: describing computer models that reproduce the behaviour of celestial matter
senses.definitionCN: 指复现天体物质行为的计算机模型
senses.example: An astrophysical simulation reproduced the spiral arms.
senses.exampleCN: 一次天体物理模拟复现了旋臂结构。
senses.why: when equations cannot be solved by hand, the field computes, and the adjective marks models rather than observations.
senses.whyCN: 当方程无法手算时，这一领域转向计算，这个形容词便标记模型而非观测。

senses.title: Bounds set by what the sky allows
senses.titleCN: 由天体观测给出的约束
senses.definition: describing limits placed on theories by what celestial observations permit
senses.definitionCN: 指天体观测对理论所施加的限制
senses.example: The new limit is an astrophysical constraint on dark matter.
senses.exampleCN: 这个新上限是对暗物质的一项天体物理约束。
senses.why: theory can propose almost anything, but the sky vetoes some options, and those vetoes are called constraints.
senses.whyCN: 理论几乎可以提出任何设想，但天空会否决其中一些，这些否决就叫约束。

senses.title: On a scale no tank can hold
senses.titleCN: 地球上无法容纳的尺度
senses.definition: describing conditions of temperature, density or size impossible to create on Earth
senses.definitionCN: 形容地球上无法制造的温度、密度或尺度条件
senses.example: The pressure here is astrophysical, not industrial.
senses.exampleCN: 这里的压强属于天体物理量级，而非工业量级。
senses.why: the adjective also works as a scale marker, since the objects it describes exceed every terrestrial limit.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词也可作尺度标记，因为它所描述的对象超过一切地面极限。

intro.en: Astrophysical is a modern adjective built from astrophysics with the ordinary Latin ending -al; it has no classical original. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: astrophysical 是现代形容词，由 astrophysics 加普通拉丁词尾 -al 构成；它没有古典原形。年代均为约数。

items.en: Astron 'star' supplies the first element; the same noun gave astronomy, astronomer and the combining form astro-.
items.cn: astron「星」提供第一个成分；同一个名词也衍生 astronomy、astronomer 与组合成分 astro-。

items.en: Physis 'nature', from phyein 'to grow', supplies the second element through ta physika and Latin physica.
items.cn: physis「自然」来自 phyein「生长」，经 ta physika 与拉丁 physica 提供第二个成分。

items.en: The noun astrophysics is generally dated to the mid-nineteenth century, once spectroscopy made the chemistry of stars readable.
items.cn: 名词 astrophysics 一般认为是十九世纪中叶所造，当时光谱学使恒星的化学成分变得可读。

items.en: The adjective ending -al comes from Latin -alis 'relating to' and is the standard way English turns a science into a describing word.
items.cn: 形容词词尾 -al 来自拉丁 -alis「与……相关」，是英语把学科变成描述词的常规手段。

items.en: Twentieth-century research fixed phrases such as astrophysical jet and astrophysical black hole, where the adjective separates real sky objects from theoretical ones.
items.cn: 二十世纪的研究固定了 astrophysical jet、astrophysical black hole 等说法，其中的形容词把真实的天空对象与理论对象区分开。

items.en: Source uncertain: the first recorded use of the adjective is not well dated, and the noun's exact coinage date has competing accounts.
items.cn: 来源不确定：这个形容词的首见记录年代不详；名词的确切造词年代也存在多种说法。

note.en: Group one holds the look-alike forms of the same family; group two holds adjectives for neighbouring physical sciences.
note.cn: 第一组是同族中易混的形式；第二组是邻近物理学科的形容词。

entries.definition: The discipline itself; astrophysical can only describe work, objects or parameters.
entries.definitionCN: 学科本身；astrophysical 只能形容工作、对象或参数。

entries.definition: Relating to astronomy and also used for 'very large'; astrophysical never carries the 'huge' sense.
entries.definitionCN: 与天文学相关，也用于「极大」；astrophysical 从不带「巨大」义。

entries.definition: Relating to the physics of the Earth; the prefix geo- replaces astro- and the object changes entirely.
entries.definitionCN: 与地球物理有关；前缀 geo- 取代 astro-，对象彻底改变。

entries.definition: Relating to star signs; the -logical ending marks interpretation rather than physics.
entries.definitionCN: 与星座征兆有关；-logical 结尾标记解读，而非物理。

entries.definition: Relating to stars; it is narrower than astrophysical, which also covers galaxies and gas.
entries.definitionCN: 与恒星有关；比 astrophysical 窄，后者还涵盖星系与气体。

entries.definition: Relating to the universe as a whole; it is a larger frame than a single astrophysical process.
entries.definitionCN: 与整个宇宙有关；框架比单个天体物理过程更大。

entries.definition: Relating to matter and energy in general; astrophysical restricts that to celestial settings.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指与物质和能量有关；astrophysical 把它限定到天体环境。

entries.definition: Of extreme particle energies; it describes a subfield of astrophysical work rather than the whole of it.
entries.definitionCN: 指极高粒子能量；它描述天体物理工作的一个子领域，而非全部。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real two halves of the compound, the real fixed terms and the real contrast with astronomical.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用复合词真实的两半、真实的固定术语，以及与 astronomical 的对比。

normal.en: astrophysics + -al: belonging to the physics of stars.
normal.cn: astrophysics + -al：属于星辰之物理的。

normal.en: Fixed terms: astrophysical jet, astrophysical black hole, astrophysical parameters.
normal.cn: 固定术语：天体物理喷流、天体物理黑洞、天体物理参数。

normal.en: The adverb astrophysically exists but is rare outside technical writing.
normal.cn: 副词 astrophysically 存在，但除技术文献外很少见。

normal.en: Unlike astronomical, astrophysical never means 'huge'.
normal.cn: 与 astronomical 不同，astrophysical 从不表示「巨大」。

normal.en: Pair it with its neighbours: astrophysical processes, geophysical processes, cosmological processes.
normal.cn: 与邻词配对记忆：天体物理过程、地球物理过程、宇宙学过程。

abstract.en: Picture a flame taller than a solar system, lit by a single young star.
abstract.cn: 想象一束比太阳系还高的火焰，由一颗年轻恒星点燃。

abstract.en: Picture a black hole that is real enough to cast a shadow on a detector.
abstract.cn: 想象一个真实到能在探测器上投下阴影的黑洞。

abstract.en: Picture a scale so extreme that every earthly unit must be abandoned.
abstract.cn: 想象一种尺度极端到必须放弃一切地面单位。

examples.en: Astrophysical models now include magnetic fields as a matter of course.
examples.cn: 天体物理模型如今通常都会包含磁场。

examples.en: The observed flare matched the astrophysical prediction almost exactly.
examples.cn: 观测到的耀发几乎完全符合天体物理的预测。

examples.en: Some constants are astrophysical in origin and cannot be tuned in a lab.
examples.cn: 有些常数源自天体物理条件，无法在实验室里调节。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「astro（星）+ physical（物理的）」——星星身上的物理 → 天体物理的

8.root: astrophysics + -al；astrophysics 由希腊 astron「星」与 physis「自然」（经拉丁 physica）构成，一般认为成词于十九世纪中叶。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all mark things that belong to the physics of the sky: the discipline, its processes, its jets, its real black holes, its measurable parameters, its simulations, its constraints and its unearthly scales.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都标记属于「天空之物理」的事物：学科、过程、喷流、真实黑洞、可测参数、模拟、约束，以及非地面的尺度。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a jet from a newborn star, photographed as one bright line.
core.cn: 核心意象：新生恒星射出的喷流，被拍成一条亮线。

branches.en: MEMBERSHIP: work that belongs to the field, plain and simple.
branches.cn: 归属：属于该领域的工作，最朴素的用法。

branches.en: REAL SKY OBJECTS AND PROCESSES: jets, stellar-collapse black holes, processes no tank holds.
branches.cn: 真实的天空对象与过程：喷流、恒星坍缩黑洞，以及没有容器能容纳的过程。

branches.en: THE NUMBERS: mass, temperature, spin and luminosity are the quantities the field fits.
branches.cn: 数字：质量、温度、自转与光度是该领域拟合的量。

branches.en: COMPUTATION AND LIMITS: models reproduce behaviour, observations veto theories.
branches.cn: 计算与限制：模型复现行为，观测否决理论。

branches.en: SCALE: conditions beyond every terrestrial limit become a description in themselves.
branches.cn: 尺度：超出一切地面极限的条件本身成了一种描述。

intro.en: Astrophysical is a modern compound plus -al, and its parts are still transparent enough to read separately.
intro.cn: astrophysical 是现代复合词加 -al，其构件仍透明到可以分开读。

latinIntro.en: Latin contributes only the adjective ending -alis and the borrowed noun physica; astron and physis remain Greek at root.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语只贡献了形容词词尾 -alis 与借入的 physica；astron 与 physis 在根部仍属希腊语。

items.meaningCN: 构成关系形容词（表示「与……相关」）
items.example: Physics gives physical by this ending.
items.exampleCN: physics 靠这个后缀构成 physical。

items.example: Astro- appears in astronomy and astrophysics.
items.exampleCN: astro- 出现在 astronomy 与 astrophysics 中。

items.example: Phys- appears in physics, physical, physique.
items.exampleCN: phys- 出现在 physics、physical、physique 中。

items.example: Astrophysics explains the spectrum.
items.exampleCN: 天体物理学解释这条光谱。

items.example: The astrophysicist ran the simulation.
items.exampleCN: 这位天体物理学家运行了模拟。

items.meaning: from an astrophysical point of view
items.example: The event is astrophysically ordinary.
items.exampleCN: 这样的事件在天体物理上很普通。

items.example: Geophysical surveys map the crust.
items.exampleCN: 地球物理勘探绘制地壳。

items.example: The telescope cost an astronomical sum.
items.exampleCN: 这架望远镜耗资巨大。

9.definition_en: a scientist who studies the physical nature of stars, galaxies and other celestial bodies
9.core_image: 会议室墙上投着一张模拟图，一只激光笔的红点停在坍缩的核上
9.scene: 会议室里，研究者把一张模拟图投到墙上，用激光笔圈出正在坍缩的核心。The astrophysicist circled the collapsing core on the projected simulation.
9.sceneCN: 这里 astrophysicist 指「以天体物理为专业的研究者」（第 1 个义项：天体物理学家这一职业）；句意为这位天体物理学家在投影的模拟图上圈出了正在坍缩的核心。可辨识物件：投影模拟图、激光笔红点、坍缩核、会议桌。

pos.zh: 可数名词：天体物理学家

collocations.zh: 受过训练的天体物理学家

senses.title: A scientist of the physics of stars
senses.titleCN: 以天体物理为专业的科学家
senses.definition: a scientist whose profession is the physical study of celestial bodies
senses.definitionCN: 以天体的物理研究为职业的科学家
senses.example: The astrophysicist circled the collapsing core on the projected simulation.
senses.exampleCN: 这位天体物理学家在投影的模拟图上圈出了正在坍缩的核心。
senses.why: astrophysics names the field and -ist marks the person, so the word is simply 'one who works in that field'.
senses.whyCN: astrophysics 指领域，-ist 标记人，因此这个词就是「在该领域工作的人」。

senses.title: The reader of spectra and light curves
senses.titleCN: 解读光谱与光变曲线的人
senses.definition: one whose daily work is to extract physical quantities from spectra and light curves
senses.definitionCN: 日常工作是从光谱与光变曲线中提取物理量的人
senses.example: The astrophysicist read the spin rate from a single line.
senses.exampleCN: 这位天体物理学家从一条谱线读出了自转速率。
senses.why: since almost all data arrive as light, the characteristic skill of the profession is turning photons into numbers.
senses.whyCN: 由于几乎所有数据都以光的形式到达，这一职业的标志性本领就是把光子变成数字。

senses.title: The builder of models
senses.definition: one who constructs mathematical or numerical models of celestial processes
senses.definitionCN: 为天体过程构建数学或数值模型的人
senses.example: A theoretical astrophysicist predicted the flare years early.
senses.exampleCN: 一位理论天体物理学家提前数年预言了那次耀发。
senses.why: the field splits between measuring and modelling, and the model side is often named with theoretical in front.
senses.whyCN: 这一领域分为测量与建模两侧，建模一侧常在名称前加 theoretical。

senses.title: The scientist on a mission team
senses.titleCN: 任务团队中的天体物理学家
senses.definition: a researcher attached to a space mission to interpret its data
senses.definitionCN: 隶属于某项太空任务、负责解读其数据的研究者
senses.example: The mission's astrophysicist argued for one more orbit.
senses.exampleCN: 该任务的天体物理学家主张再多绕一圈。
senses.why: missions need someone who can convert instrument output into physics, so the role becomes a post on a team.
senses.whyCN: 任务需要有人把仪器产出转成物理结论，于是这一身份成了团队里的一个岗位。

senses.title: The instrument specialist
senses.definition: a researcher who designs or calibrates the detectors used in the field
senses.definitionCN: 设计或校准该领域所用探测器的研究者
senses.example: An instrument astrophysicist rebuilt the calibration table.
senses.exampleCN: 一位仪器天体物理学家重做了校准表。
senses.why: when a measurement is the whole product, the person who knows the instrument becomes a distinct kind of specialist.
senses.whyCN: 当测量本身就是最终产品时，懂仪器的人便成为一类独立的专家。

senses.title: The teacher and supervisor
senses.definition: a university researcher who teaches the subject and supervises students
senses.definitionCN: 在大学讲授该学科并指导学生的研究者
senses.example: The astrophysicist supervised four doctoral students.
senses.exampleCN: 这位天体物理学家指导了四名博士生。
senses.why: a discipline reproduces itself through teaching, so the same title covers the classroom as well as the observatory.
senses.whyCN: 学科靠教学自我延续，因此同一个称号既覆盖天文台，也覆盖课堂。

senses.title: The public explainer
senses.definition: a researcher known for explaining the field to non-specialists
senses.definitionCN: 以向非专业者解释该领域而著称的研究者
senses.example: The astrophysicist's radio series reached millions.
senses.exampleCN: 这位天体物理学家主持的广播系列节目触达了数百万人。
senses.why: public explanation is now part of the job, and the title alone can identify someone known mainly for it.
senses.whyCN: 公众解说如今是工作的一部分，因此单凭这个称号就能指以解说著称的人。

senses.title: Historical: the first spectroscopists
senses.titleCN: 历史上：最早的光谱分析者
senses.definition: one of the nineteenth-century researchers who first applied physics to starlight
senses.definitionCN: 十九世纪最早把物理用于星光的那些研究者之一
senses.example: The first astrophysicists worked with prisms, not rockets.
senses.exampleCN: 最早的天体物理学家用的是棱镜，不是火箭。
senses.why: before the title existed, the work was done by spectroscopists, so historians apply the word backward to them.
senses.whyCN: 在这个称号出现之前，工作是由光谱学家做的，因此史学家把这个词回溯用在他们身上。

intro.en: Astrophysicist is a nineteenth-century agent noun made from astrophysics with the Greek-derived suffix -ist. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: astrophysicist 是十九世纪由 astrophysics 加希腊来源后缀 -ist 构成的施动名词。年代均为约数。

items.en: Astron 'star' supplies astro-, the first half of the compound; the same element appears in astronomy, astronomer and astronaut.
items.cn: astron「星」提供 astro-，即复合词的前半；同一成分也出现在 astronomy、astronomer 与 astronaut 中。

items.en: Physis 'nature' gives physics through ta physika and Latin physica; the second half of the compound names the method.
items.cn: physis「自然」经 ta physika 与拉丁 physica 给出 physics；复合词的后半命名方法。

items.en: Astrophysics is generally dated to the mid-nineteenth century, when spectroscopy first allowed the chemistry of stars to be read from their light.
items.cn: astrophysics 一般认为是十九世纪中叶所造，当时光谱学首次让人能从星光读出恒星的化学成分。

items.en: The agent suffix -ist came into English through Latin -ista from Greek -istes, and marks a person devoted to a practice, as in physicist and geologist.
items.cn: 施动后缀 -ist 经拉丁 -ista 从希腊 -istes 进入英语，标记专注于某项实践的人，如 physicist 与 geologist。

items.en: The compound title followed once the field gained its own departments and journals; institutions needed a word for the person that matched the name of the discipline, and -ist supplied it.
items.cn: 随着这一领域有了自己的系与期刊，这个复合称号也随之固定；机构需要一个与学科名称相配的词来指人，-ist 正好提供了它。

items.en: Source uncertain: the first printed use of astrophysicist is not precisely dated, and the coinage date of astrophysics itself has competing accounts.
items.cn: 来源不确定：astrophysicist 最早的印刷用例没有确切年代；astrophysics 本身的造词年代也存在多种说法。

note.en: Group one separates this personal title from the field and from near spellings; group two holds neighbouring specialists.
note.cn: 第一组把这个人称称号与学科名、近形词分开；第二组是邻近的专家称谓。

entries.definition: The discipline; astrophysicist is the person who practises it.
entries.definitionCN: 学科；astrophysicist 是从事它的人。

entries.definition: A scientist of physics in general; astrophysicist adds the celestial restriction.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指物理学家；astrophysicist 加了天体的限定。

entries.definition: One who studies or observes celestial bodies; the title does not promise physical explanation.
entries.definitionCN: 研究或观测天体的人；这个称号并不承诺物理解释。

entries.definition: One who reads star signs; the -log- root marks interpretation, not measurement.
entries.definitionCN: 解读星座征兆的人；-log- 词根标记解读，而非测量。

entries.definition: A specialist in the origin and structure of the universe; the brief is larger than one star or galaxy.
entries.definitionCN: 研究宇宙起源与结构的专家；职责范围比单颗恒星或星系更大。

entries.definition: A specialist in spectra; many early astrophysicists were spectroscopists first.
entries.definitionCN: 光谱专家；许多早期天体物理学家原本就是光谱学家。

entries.definition: A broad mission title covering instruments, biology and physics; it is less specific than astrophysicist.
entries.definitionCN: 任务语境中的宽泛称号，涵盖仪器、生物与物理；不如 astrophysicist 具体。

entries.definition: A physicist of the Earth; the methods are similar but the object is entirely different.
entries.definitionCN: 研究地球的物理学家；方法相似，对象完全不同。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real suffix -ist, the real field name and the real division between observing and modelling.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的 -ist 后缀、真实的领域名称，以及观测与建模之间的真实分工。

normal.en: astrophysics + -ist: the person who works in astrophysics.
normal.cn: astrophysics + -ist：在天体物理领域工作的人。

normal.en: The -ist family: physicist, geophysicist, astrophysicist.
normal.cn: -ist 词族：physicist、geophysicist、astrophysicist。

normal.en: Title pairs: theoretical astrophysicist, observational astrophysicist.
normal.cn: 称号配对：理论天体物理学家、观测天体物理学家。

normal.en: Astronomer observes, astrophysicist explains.
normal.cn: 天文学家观测，天体物理学家解释。

normal.en: The early ones used prisms; the modern ones use detectors and code.
normal.cn: 早期的人用棱镜，现代的人用探测器与代码。

abstract.en: Picture a red dot from a laser pointer resting on a star's collapsing heart.
abstract.cn: 想象激光笔的红点停在一颗恒星正在坍缩的核心上。

abstract.en: Picture a person turning a wavy line into a temperature.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人把一条波浪线换算成温度。

abstract.en: Picture someone who reads light the way others read handwriting.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人读光，就像别人读字迹。

examples.en: The astrophysicist spent a decade on one supernova.
examples.cn: 这位天体物理学家在一颗超新星上花了十年。

examples.en: Astrophysicists disagree about how the first stars formed.
examples.cn: 天体物理学家对最初的恒星如何形成仍有分歧。

examples.en: She trained as an astrophysicist before moving into science policy.
examples.cn: 她先受训成为天体物理学家，后来转入科学政策。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「astro（星）+ physicist（物理学家）」——研究星星的物理学家 → 天体物理学家

9.root: astrophysics + -ist（希腊 -istes，经拉丁 -ista）；astrophysics 由希腊 astron「星」与 physis「自然」构成，一般认为成词于十九世纪中叶。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses describe one practitioner from different angles: the profession, the spectral reader, the modeller, the mission scientist, the instrument specialist, the teacher, the public explainer and the nineteenth-century pioneer.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从不同角度描述同一个从业者：职业身份、读谱者、建模者、任务科学家、仪器专家、教师、公众解说者，以及十九世纪的先驱。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a red laser dot on a projected image of a collapsing stellar core.
core.cn: 核心意象：投影图上，一个红色激光点停在坍缩的恒星核心。

branches.en: THE TITLE: -ist simply marks the person who belongs to the field.
branches.cn: 称号：-ist 只标记属于该领域的人。

branches.en: THE CORE SKILL: reading photons and turning them into physical quantities.
branches.cn: 核心技能：读光子并把它转成物理量。

branches.en: THE DIVISION OF LABOUR: build models, or interpret a mission's data.
branches.cn: 分工：构建模型，或解读任务数据。

branches.en: THE INSTRUMENT: whoever knows the detector becomes a specialist in their own right.
branches.cn: 仪器：懂探测器的人本身也成了一类专家。

branches.en: REPRODUCTION AND HISTORY: teaching, explaining to the public, and the prism pioneers behind the title.
branches.cn: 传承与历史：教学、向公众解释，以及称号背后的棱镜先驱。

intro.en: Astrophysicist is a compound field name plus a person suffix, and the suffix is what separates the practitioner from the science.
intro.cn: astrophysicist 是复合领域名加人称后缀，正是这个后缀把从业者与学科分开。

latinIntro.en: Latin -ista supplies the person suffix -ist; Latin physicus 'natural philosopher' and astronomus 'star-arranger' supply the older names for the same kind of worker.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 -ista 提供人称后缀 -ist；拉丁 physicus「自然研究者」与 astronomus「安排星辰者」提供了同一类工作者的旧称。

items.meaning: one who practises or believes in
items.meaningCN: 从事或信奉某事的人（施动后缀）
items.example: Physicist and geologist use the same suffix.
items.exampleCN: physicist 与 geologist 用同一后缀。

items.example: Astrophysics is the field; astrophysicist the person.
items.exampleCN: astrophysics 是学科，astrophysicist 是人。

items.example: Astrophysical processes need extreme conditions.
items.exampleCN: 天体物理过程需要极端条件。

items.example: Every astrophysicist is a physicist first.
items.exampleCN: 每位天体物理学家首先是物理学家。

items.example: Geophysicists model the mantle.
items.exampleCN: 地球物理学家为地幔建模。

items.example: The astronomer logged the position.
items.exampleCN: 天文学家记录了位置。

items.example: Early astrophysicists were spectroscopists.
items.exampleCN: 早期天体物理学家是光谱专家。

items.example: Astro- begins the compound.
items.exampleCN: astro- 是这个复合词的开头。

10.definition_zh: 宇宙；天地万物；（个人的）整个世界；某一领域
10.definition_en: everything that exists, especially all of space and matter taken as a whole
10.core_image: 夜空下孩子仰头指着星群，问星群之外还有什么
10.scene: 夜里孩子指着满天星问，这些之外还有什么。Everything we can see is only a small part of the universe.
10.sceneCN: 这里 universe 指「一切存在之物构成的整体」（第 1 个义项：宇宙这一整体）；句意为我们能看到的一切只是宇宙的一小部分。可辨识物件：星空、孩子的手、地平线、远处的灯。

pos.zh: 可数或不可数名词：宇宙；万物；个人世界；某一领域

derivatives.zh: 大学（同源但语义已分化）

senses.title: All that exists
senses.definition: all matter, energy and space taken together as one whole
senses.definitionCN: 把一切物质、能量与空间合为一个整体
senses.example: Everything we can see is only a small part of the universe.
senses.exampleCN: 我们能看见的一切只是宇宙的一小部分。
senses.why: the Latin source meant 'turned into one', so the word begins as a totality made from many parts rather than as a place.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词源意为「转成一个」，因此这个词一开始指的是由许多部分合成的整体，而不是一个地点。

senses.title: The observable universe
senses.definition: the part of the universe whose light has had time to reach us
senses.definitionCN: 光有时间抵达我们的那部分宇宙
senses.example: The observable universe is wider than its age in light years.
senses.exampleCN: 可观测宇宙的尺度大于以光年计它的年龄。
senses.why: physics must limit itself to what can be seen, so a phrase cuts the whole down to the reachable part.
senses.whyCN: 物理学必须把自己限制在能看到的部分，因此一个短语把整体裁成可及的那一块。

senses.title: A person's whole world
senses.definition: the whole of a person's experience, interests or social surroundings
senses.definitionCN: 一个人的全部经历、兴趣或社会环境
senses.example: The village was her entire universe for eighteen years.
senses.exampleCN: 十八年里，这个村子就是她的整个宇宙。
senses.why: the metaphor is scale inversion: what fills one life is a universe to that life, however small it looks from outside.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻把尺度倒置：填满一个人一生的东西，对那个生命来说就是一个宇宙，无论从外面看多小。

senses.title: A field of discourse
senses.definition: a particular sphere of activity, thought or discussion with its own limits
senses.definitionCN: 具有自身边界的一定的活动、思想或讨论范围
senses.example: In the universe of contract law, silence rarely means consent.
senses.exampleCN: 在合同法的领域里，沉默很少等于同意。
senses.why: logic and law needed a word for the set of things under discussion, and borrowed the totality noun for a bounded world.
senses.whyCN: 逻辑学与法学需要一个词来指讨论所及事物的集合，于是借用了这个表示整体的名词来指一个有限世界。

senses.title: A fictional world
senses.definition: the self-contained world in which a story, film or game takes place
senses.definitionCN: 故事、电影或游戏在其中发生的自足世界
senses.example: The novelist built a universe with its own physics.
senses.exampleCN: 这位小说家构建了一个有自己的物理法则的宇宙。
senses.why: a fiction is complete on its own terms, so writers borrow the strongest word for completeness that English offers.
senses.whyCN: 虚构作品按自身规则自成一体，因此作者借用了英语中表示「完整」最强的词。

senses.title: The universe of discourse in logic
senses.definition: the set of individuals that a statement or quantifier ranges over
senses.definitionCN: 一个陈述或量词所涵盖的个体集合
senses.example: Every variable is bound to a universe of discourse.
senses.exampleCN: 每个变项都受一个论域约束。
senses.why: a quantifier is meaningless without saying what it ranges over, so logicians named that range with the totality word.
senses.whyCN: 量词若不说明涵盖范围便无意义，因此逻辑学家用这个「整体」词来命名那个范围。

senses.title: The whole set of something
senses.definition: the complete range of a kind of thing, as in the universe of ideas or of brands
senses.definitionCN: 某一类事物的完整范围，如观念或品牌的全体
senses.example: The universe of available materials is surprisingly small.
senses.exampleCN: 可用材料的全体范围小得惊人。
senses.why: once 'everything' can be restricted by of, it becomes a handy word for any closed inventory.
senses.whyCN: 一旦「一切」可以用 of 来限定，它就变成指任何封闭清单的方便说法。

senses.title: A self-contained system
senses.definition: a closed system whose rules generate everything inside it
senses.definitionCN: 由自身规则生成内部一切事物的封闭系统
senses.example: The game's universe is generated by three simple rules.
senses.exampleCN: 这个游戏的宇宙由三条简单规则生成。
senses.why: simulation and game design adopted the word because a closed rule-set really does make its own world.
senses.whyCN: 模拟与游戏设计采用这个词，因为一套封闭规则确实会造出它自己的世界。

intro.en: Universe is Latin for 'turned into one', a word about unity before it was a word about space. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: universe 在拉丁语中意为「转成一个」，它在指空间之前，先是一个关于「合一」的词。年代均为约数。

items.en: Universus meant 'all together, entire', built from unus 'one' and versus, the past participle of vertere 'to turn'. Literally: many things turned into one.
items.cn: universus 意为「全体、整个」，由 unus「一」与 versus（vertere「转」的过去分词）构成。字面义：许多东西转成了一个。

items.en: The related noun universitas meant 'the whole, a corporation, a guild'. Medieval Latin used it for a body of masters and students, which is how university acquired its meaning.
items.cn: 相关名词 universitas 意为「整体、团体、行会」。中世纪拉丁语用它指师生团体，大学一词的意义就是这样来的。

items.en: Old French univers carried the word into English in the late fourteenth century, at first in the sense 'the whole of created things'.
items.cn: 古法语 univers 在十四世纪末把这个词带进英语，最初意为「受造万物的整体」。

items.en: Early modern astronomy fixed the word as the name of the whole material system, and the phrase 'the universe' replaced older terms such as 'the heavens'.
items.cn: 近代早期天文学把这个词固定为整个物质系统的名称，短语 the universe 取代了「诸天」之类的旧说法。

items.en: Logic, law and later fiction applied the totality word to bounded sets, producing fixed phrases such as universe of discourse and fictional universe.
items.cn: 逻辑学、法学以及后来的虚构写作把这个「整体」词用于有限集合，产生 universe of discourse、fictional universe 等固定说法。

items.en: Source uncertain: the exact first English use is dated only approximately, and the semantic path from 'whole' to 'cosmos' is inferred from later texts rather than recorded step by step.
items.cn: 来源不确定：英语首见只有约略年代；从「整体」到「宇宙」的语义路径是根据后世文本推断，而非逐步记录在案。

note.en: Group one holds the words most often confused with universe; group two holds the neighbouring ideas of the whole of things.
note.cn: 第一组是最常与 universe 混淆的词；第二组是表示「万物整体」的邻近概念。

entries.definition: Applying to all cases; it comes from the same Latin stem but describes a quality rather than the cosmos.
entries.definitionCN: 适用于一切情况的；来自同一拉丁词干，但描述性质而非宇宙。

entries.definition: An institution of higher learning, from Latin universitas 'corporation'; it is not a shortened universe.
entries.definitionCN: 高等教育机构，来自拉丁 universitas「团体」；它不是 universe 的缩写。

entries.definition: An obsolete or rare spelling of the same word, met in older French-influenced texts.
entries.definitionCN: 同一词的废弃或罕见拼法，见于较早受法语影响的文本。

entries.definition: A line of poetry, from Latin versus 'a turning'; it shares vertere with universe but means something else entirely.
entries.definitionCN: 诗行，来自拉丁 versus「转折」；它与 universe 共享 vertere，但意思完全不同。

entries.definition: The universe viewed as an ordered system; it adds the Greek idea of order that universe does not carry.
entries.definitionCN: 被看作有序系统的宇宙；它多了希腊语「秩序」的观念，而 universe 没有。

entries.definition: The Earth and its inhabitants, or a sphere of human life; it is warmer and smaller than universe.
entries.definitionCN: 地球及其居民，或人的某种生活领域；比 universe 更贴近人、范围更小。

entries.definition: Everything made by a creator; the word carries a maker that universe does not require.
entries.definitionCN: 造物主所造的一切；这个词带有 universe 所不需要的「制造者」。

entries.definition: The great world, often contrasted with the human microcosm; it is a philosophical pairing, not a physical term.
entries.definitionCN: 大世界，常与人的小宇宙对举；它是哲学配对，而非物理术语。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Latin parts, the real fixed phrases and the real split from university.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的拉丁成分、真实的固定搭配，以及与 university 的真实分化。

normal.en: unus 'one' + versus 'turned': many things turned into one whole.
normal.cn: unus「一」+ versus「转」：许多东西转成一个整体。

normal.en: The family runs universe, universal, universally, universality.
normal.cn: 词族包括 universe、universal、universally、universality。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: observable universe, expanding universe, parallel universe.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：可观测宇宙、膨胀的宇宙、平行宇宙。

normal.en: university is a cousin, not a child: it comes from universitas 'corporation'.
normal.cn: university 是表亲而非子嗣：它来自 universitas「团体」。

normal.en: Scale ladder: universe > galaxy > star system > planet.
normal.cn: 尺度阶梯：宇宙 > 星系 > 恒星系 > 行星。

abstract.en: Picture a child asking what lies beyond the last visible star.
abstract.cn: 想象一个孩子问：最后一颗看得见的星之外还有什么。

abstract.en: Picture a single village that fills a whole life.
abstract.cn: 想象一个村庄填满了一整个人生。

abstract.en: Picture a story so complete that its own rules replace physics.
abstract.cn: 想象一个完整到用自身规则取代物理的故事。

examples.en: The universe is expanding, but galaxies themselves are not.
examples.cn: 宇宙在膨胀，但星系本身并没有。

examples.en: For a child, a single street can be the whole universe.
examples.cn: 对一个孩子来说，一条街就可能是整个宇宙。

examples.en: Each novel creates a universe with its own history.
examples.cn: 每部小说都造出一个有自己的历史的宇宙。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「uni（一）+ verse（转）」——万物转成一个整体 → 宇宙

10.root: 拉丁 universus「全体」← unus「一」+ versus（vertere「转」的过去分词）；经古法语 univers 进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses begin with totality and then shrink it: the whole of existence, the part we can see, one person's world, a field, a fiction, a logical range, a closed inventory and a rule-generated system.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从「整体」出发再逐步缩小：存在的一切、我们能看到的部分、一个人的世界、一个领域、一部虚构、一个逻辑范围、一份封闭清单，以及由规则生成的系统。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a child under the stars asking what lies beyond the last light.
core.cn: 核心意象：星空下的孩子问，最后一道光之外还有什么。

branches.en: THE PHYSICAL WHOLE: everything, then the slice of it whose light reaches us.
branches.cn: 物理整体：先是一切，再是光能抵达我们的那一块。

branches.en: PERSONAL SCALE: one life's surroundings become a universe in metaphor.
branches.cn: 个人尺度：一个人一生的周遭在比喻中成为宇宙。

branches.en: BOUNDED SETS: law and logic cut the whole down to a stated range.
branches.cn: 有限集合：法学与逻辑把整体裁成一个明确范围。

branches.en: MADE WORLDS: fiction and simulation generate self-contained systems.
branches.cn: 造出的世界：虚构与模拟生成自足系统。

branches.en: INVENTORY: the complete range of one kind of thing.
branches.cn: 清单：某一类事物的完整范围。

intro.en: Universe is a Latin participle phrase frozen into a noun; its family later produced universal, universality and the separate university.
intro.cn: universe 是一个凝固成名词的拉丁分词短语；其词族后来产生 universal、universality，以及另一个来源的 university。

latinIntro.en: Latin universus and universitas both rest on unus plus vertere; English drew universe from the first and university from the second.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 universus 与 universitas 都建于 unus 加 vertere 之上；英语从前者取 universe，从后者取 university。

items.meaningCN: 适用于全体的（-alis 表示相关）
items.example: The rule is universal in this model.
items.exampleCN: 这条规则在这个模型中是普遍适用的。

items.example: The claim is not universally accepted.
items.exampleCN: 这一说法并未被普遍接受。

items.meaning: the state of applying to all
items.example: They argued for the universality of the right.
items.exampleCN: 他们主张这项权利的普遍性。

items.example: The reform was universalized within a decade.
items.exampleCN: 这项改革在十年内普及。

items.meaningCN: 大学（源自「团体」而非「宇宙」）
items.example: The university began as a guild of masters.
items.exampleCN: 这所大学起初是教师的行会。

items.meaning: the set a statement ranges over
items.meaningCN: 论域（陈述所涵盖的集合）
items.example: Fix the universe of discourse first.
items.exampleCN: 先确定论域。

items.example: The multiverse remains a hypothesis.
items.exampleCN: 多元宇宙仍是一种假说。

items.meaning: a small world reflecting the large one
items.example: The pond is a microcosm of the lake.
items.exampleCN: 这池塘是湖泊的缩影。

11.definition_zh: 普遍的；全体的；通用的；宇宙的
11.definition_en: applying to all people or all cases, or existing everywhere
11.core_image: 不同文字的指示牌上，同一个被斜线划掉的烟形图案
11.scene: 车站里，各式文字的指示牌上都印着同一个被斜线划掉的香烟图案。A crossed cigarette is a universal sign, understood even where no words are shared.
11.sceneCN: 这里 universal 指「所有人、所有地方都通用的」（第 3 个义项：为全体成员共同理解）；句意为被斜线划掉的香烟是通用标志，即使彼此语言不通也能看懂。可辨识物件：多语指示牌、香烟图案、斜线、行人。

pos.zh: 普遍的；全体的；通用的；宇宙的

senses.title: True of everyone
senses.definition: affecting or applying to all people without exception
senses.definitionCN: 无例外地影响或适用于所有人
senses.example: Clean water is a universal need, not a luxury.
senses.exampleCN: 洁净的水是普遍需求，而非奢侈品。
senses.why: the Latin stem already meant 'turned into one whole', so the adjective says that a quality holds across the whole set.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词干本义就是「转成一个整体」，因此这个形容词表示某种性质在整体上都成立。

senses.title: True in every case
senses.titleCN: 逻辑上对所有情形成立
senses.definition: of a statement, holding for every member of a class
senses.definitionCN: 指陈述对某一类中的每个成员都成立
senses.example: A universal claim fails on a single counterexample.
senses.exampleCN: 一个全称陈述只要遇到一个反例就失败。
senses.why: logic borrowed the word for statements whose subject is 'all', and that technical sense is the strictest one.
senses.whyCN: 逻辑学借这个词来指主语为「所有」的陈述，这一技术义是最严格的用法。

senses.title: Understood by all
senses.titleCN: 所有人都能理解的通用
senses.definition: of a sign or meaning, recognised by people regardless of language
senses.definitionCN: 指符号或意义不分语言都能被识别
senses.example: A crossed cigarette is a universal sign, understood even where no words are shared.
senses.exampleCN: 被斜线划掉的香烟是通用标志，即使彼此语言不通也能看懂。
senses.why: some meanings travel without translation, and the adjective marks exactly that freedom from a particular language.
senses.whyCN: 有些意义无需翻译就能通行，这个形容词标记的正是这种脱离特定语言的能力。

senses.title: Universal grammar
senses.definition: of the features claimed to be shared by all human languages
senses.definitionCN: 指被认为为一切人类语言共有的特征
senses.example: Universal grammar is a hypothesis about what children bring to language.
senses.exampleCN: 普遍语法是一种关于儿童天生带来什么的假说。
senses.why: if every child acquires any language, linguists ask what must be shared, and the adjective names that common core.
senses.whyCN: 既然每个孩子都能习得任何语言，语言学家便追问哪些东西必然共有，这个形容词命名那个共同核心。

senses.title: The universal set in mathematics
senses.definition: of the set that contains every object under consideration
senses.definitionCN: 指包含所讨论一切对象的集合
senses.example: The complement is taken relative to the universal set.
senses.exampleCN: 补集是相对全集来取的。
senses.why: set theory needed one container for everything discussed, and reused the totality adjective for it.
senses.whyCN: 集合论需要一个容纳所有讨论对象的容器，于是复用了这个表示整体的形容词。

senses.title: A universal joint
senses.definition: of a coupling that transmits motion through a variable angle
senses.definitionCN: 指能在变化角度下传递运动的联轴装置
senses.example: The universal joint lets the axle work at an angle.
senses.exampleCN: 万向节让传动轴在倾斜角度下工作。
senses.why: the joint works in every direction, so nineteenth-century engineering called it universal rather than flexible.
senses.whyCN: 这种接头在任何方向都能工作，因此十九世纪的工程称之为「通用」而不是「柔性」。

senses.title: A universal donor
senses.definition: of a blood type that can be given to patients of any group
senses.definitionCN: 指可输给任何血型病人的血型
senses.example: Group O negative is treated as the universal donor.
senses.exampleCN: 阴性 O 型被视为通用供血者。
senses.why: medicine applies the word where compatibility holds across every group, which is the same logic as sense one.
senses.whyCN: 医学把这个词用于在所有血型间都相容的情形，逻辑与第一义项相同。

senses.title: A universal language
senses.definition: of a language or medium meant to be learned and used by everyone
senses.definitionCN: 指意在让所有人学习并使用的语言或媒介
senses.example: Music is often called a universal language.
senses.exampleCN: 音乐常被称为一种通用语言。
senses.why: the phrase expresses an aspiration rather than a fact, and the adjective carries that ambition of covering all speakers.
senses.whyCN: 这个说法表达的是愿望而非事实，这个形容词承载的正是「覆盖所有使用者」的雄心。

senses.title: Universal suffrage
senses.definition: of the right to vote extended to all adult citizens
senses.definitionCN: 指选举权扩展到全体成年公民
senses.example: Universal suffrage arrived later than universal schooling.
senses.exampleCN: 普选权的到来比普及教育更晚。
senses.why: political history needed a precise word for extending a right to the whole adult population, and universal supplied it.
senses.whyCN: 政治史需要一个精确的词来表示把权利扩展到全体成年人，universal 正好提供了它。

intro.en: Universal is the adjective of Latin universus, and it reached English through French as a word about wholes before it became a word about the cosmos. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: universal 是拉丁 universus 的形容词，经法语进入英语；它在指宇宙之前，先是一个关于「整体」的词。年代均为约数。

items.en: Universus 'all together, whole' was built from unus 'one' plus versus, the past participle of vertere 'to turn'; the whole is what has been turned into one.
items.cn: universus「全体、整个」由 unus「一」加 versus（vertere「转」的过去分词）构成；整体就是被转成一个的东西。

items.en: Universalis meant 'of or belonging to all', and in medieval philosophy it named a concept said to hold of many individuals, the source of the logical sense.
items.cn: universalis 意为「属于全体的」，在中世纪哲学中它指被认为适用于许多个体的概念，这就是逻辑义的来源。

items.en: Old French universel carried the adjective into English in the late fourteenth century, at first in philosophy and theology.
items.cn: 古法语 universel 在十四世纪末把这个形容词带进英语，最初用于哲学与神学。

items.en: From the eighteenth century the word moved into political language, where universal suffrage and universal schooling meant extending an institution to every adult.
items.cn: 从十八世纪起，这个词进入政治语言，universal suffrage 与 universal schooling 都表示把某项制度扩展到每个成年人。

items.en: Mathematics fixed universal set, engineering fixed universal joint, and medicine fixed universal donor, each applying the same logic of 'no exceptions'.
items.cn: 数学固定了 universal set，工程固定了 universal joint，医学固定了 universal donor，各自用的都是「无例外」这同一逻辑。

items.en: Source uncertain: the first English citation is dated only approximately, and the medieval philosophical sense has a long and disputed history.
items.cn: 来源不确定：英语首见只有约略年代；中世纪哲学义的历史漫长且存在争议。

note.en: Group one separates universal from its own family and from the noun universe; group two holds the adjectives of wide coverage.
note.cn: 第一组把 universal 与同族词及名词 universe 分开；第二组是表示覆盖范围广的形容词。

entries.definition: Everything that exists; universal describes what holds across all of it or all people.
entries.definitionCN: 存在的一切；universal 形容在全体或所有人中都成立的。

entries.definition: The state of being universal; the adjective names the property, the noun names its presence.
entries.definitionCN: 普遍性这一状态；形容词指性质，名词指该性质的存在。

entries.definition: A belief that something applies to or saves all; it adds -ism and turns the quality into a movement.
entries.definitionCN: 认为某事物适用于或拯救全体的信念；加上 -ism 后把性质变成一种主张。

entries.definition: To make something apply to all; the suffix -ize marks the act of extending coverage.
entries.definitionCN: 使某事物适用于全体；后缀 -ize 标记扩展覆盖的行为。

entries.definition: Applying in most cases but allowing exceptions; universal admits none.
entries.definitionCN: 适用于多数情形但允许例外；universal 则不允许例外。

entries.definition: Covering the whole world; it is about geography, while universal is about the whole of a class.
entries.definitionCN: 覆盖全世界的；关乎地理，而 universal 关乎某一类别的全体。

entries.definition: Found in all places at once; it describes presence, not validity.
entries.definitionCN: 到处同时存在的；它描述存在，而非有效性。

entries.definition: Shared by many or most; it makes no claim of covering everyone.
entries.definitionCN: 为许多或多数人所共有；不声称覆盖每一个人。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Latin stem, the real technical phrases and the real contrast with general.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的拉丁词干、真实的技术搭配，以及与 general 的对比。

normal.en: unus 'one' + versus 'turned' + -al: belonging to the whole turned into one.
normal.cn: unus「一」+ versus「转」+ -al：属于那个转成一体的整体。

normal.en: The family runs universal, universally, universality, universalize, universalism.
normal.cn: 词族包括 universal、universally、universality、universalize、universalism。

normal.en: Technical phrases: universal set, universal joint, universal donor, universal grammar.
normal.cn: 技术搭配：全集、万向节、通用供血者、普遍语法。

normal.en: Political phrases: universal suffrage, universal access, universal healthcare.
normal.cn: 政治搭配：普选权、普遍可及、全民医疗。

normal.en: Universal allows no exceptions; general allows some.
normal.cn: universal 不允许例外；general 允许一些例外。

abstract.en: Picture one pictogram that needs no translation in any airport.
abstract.cn: 想象一个在任何机场都不需要翻译的图示。

abstract.en: Picture a single key that opens every door in a building.
abstract.cn: 想象一把能打开楼里每一扇门的钥匙。

abstract.en: Picture a claim that survives every attempt to find a counterexample.
abstract.cn: 想象一个经受住每一次反例检验的论断。

examples.en: The right to a fair hearing is not yet universal in practice.
examples.cn: 获得公正听证的权利在实践中尚未普及。

examples.en: Universal precautions treat every sample as potentially infectious.
examples.cn: 普遍防护把每一份样本都当作可能带传染性。

examples.en: The claim is universal in form but limited in scope.
examples.cn: 这个论断在形式上是全称的，但范围有限。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「uni（一）+ versal（转的）」——转成一体、人人都算 → 普遍的；通用的

11.root: 拉丁 universalis ← universus「全体」← unus「一」+ versus（vertere「转」的过去分词）；经古法语 universel 进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses all deny exceptions: everyone is affected, every case satisfies a claim, every language user understands a sign, all languages share a core, all objects fill a set, all angles a joint, all blood groups a donor, all speakers a language, all adults a vote.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项都在否定例外：影响所有人、每个情形都满足论断、任何语言使用者都懂同一符号、一切语言共享核心、所有对象填满一个集合、任何角度都可用同一接头、任何血型都可接受同一供血、所有说话者共用一种语言、全体成年人都有选举权。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one pictogram repeated on signs in many scripts, understood without words.
core.cn: 核心意象：同一个图示印在许多文字的指示牌上，不用文字也看得懂。

branches.en: PEOPLE: a need or right that reaches every person.
branches.cn: 人：抵达每一个人的需求或权利。

branches.en: LOGIC AND SETS: a claim for all members, a set that holds every object.
branches.cn: 逻辑与集合：对全体成员的论断，容纳一切对象的集合。

branches.en: MEANING WITHOUT TRANSLATION: signs and languages that cross speech communities.
branches.cn: 无需翻译的意义：跨越语言共同体的符号与语言。

branches.en: SHARED ACROSS DIFFERENCES: a grammar core, a joint at any angle, a blood type for all groups.
branches.cn: 跨越差异的共享：语法核心、任意角度的接头、适用于所有血型的血型。

branches.en: POLITICS: extending an institution to the whole adult population.
branches.cn: 政治：把制度扩展到全体成年人口。

intro.en: Universal is a Latin adjective ending on a Latin adjective stem, and its derivatives turn the quality into a noun, a verb and a doctrine.
intro.cn: universal 是拉丁形容词词干加拉丁形容词词尾，其派生词把这一性质变成名词、动词与一种主张。

latinIntro.en: Latin universalis comes from universus; the English family keeps -al, -ly, -ity, -ize and -ism as the ordinary layers of derivation.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 universalis 来自 universus；英语词族以 -al、-ly、-ity、-ize、-ism 作为常规派生层。

items.example: The method is not universally reliable.
items.exampleCN: 这种方法并非普遍可靠。

items.meaning: the quality of applying to all
items.example: The universality of the pattern surprised them.
items.exampleCN: 这一模式的普遍性让他们吃惊。

items.example: They universalized the benefit over ten years.
items.exampleCN: 他们用十年把这项福利普及。

items.meaning: a belief in universal scope or salvation
items.meaningCN: 普遍主义（主张普遍适用或普遍得救）
items.example: Universalism shaped the reform movement.
items.exampleCN: 普遍主义塑造了那场改革运动。

items.meaning: the set of all objects under discussion
items.meaningCN: 全集（所讨论对象的集合）
items.example: The complement depends on the universal set.
items.exampleCN: 补集取决于全集。

items.meaning: a coupling working at any angle
items.meaningCN: 万向节（可在任意角度工作的接头）
items.example: The universal joint removed the vibration.
items.exampleCN: 万向节消除了震动。

items.meaning: a blood type acceptable to all
items.meaningCN: 通用供血者（可为所有血型接受）
items.example: The universal donor is kept for emergencies.
items.exampleCN: 通用供血者的血留作急救用。

items.example: The universe is wider than the visible part.
items.exampleCN: 宇宙比可见部分更宽广。

12.definition_zh: 宇宙；有序的整体；秩序与和谐
12.definition_en: the universe considered as an ordered whole
12.core_image: 一只古希腊陶盘上刻着一圈匀称的星点，被摆在祭台正中
12.scene: 古希腊的陶盘上刻着一圈匀称的星点，匠人把它摆到祭台正中。For the Pythagoreans the cosmos was not merely everything, but everything arranged in order.
12.sceneCN: 这里 cosmos 指「被视为有序整体的宇宙」（第 1 个义项：兼含「全部」与「秩序」的整体）；句意为对毕达哥拉斯学派而言，宇宙不只是万物，而是万物按秩序排列。可辨识物件：陶盘、环形星点、祭台、刻线。

pos.zh: 不可数名词：宇宙；有序整体；（古义）装饰、秩序

forms.label: 复数（多个宇宙或多种秩序体系）

derivatives.zh: 化妆的（同源但语义分化）

senses.title: The universe as an ordered whole
senses.definition: the universe thought of as a single ordered system rather than a random collection
senses.definitionCN: 把宇宙当作一个有序系统而非杂乱集合来看
senses.example: For the Pythagoreans the cosmos was not merely everything, but everything arranged in order.
senses.exampleCN: 对毕达哥拉斯学派而言，宇宙不只是万物，而是万物按秩序排列。
senses.why: Greek kosmos first meant 'order' and only later 'world', so the English word inherits both ideas at once.
senses.whyCN: 希腊 kosmos 先意为「秩序」，后来才指「世界」，因此英语这个词同时继承了这两层意思。

senses.title: The physical universe of astronomy
senses.titleCN: 天文学研究的物质宇宙
senses.definition: all of space and matter studied by astronomy and physics
senses.definitionCN: 天文学与物理学所研究的一切空间与物质
senses.example: The observable cosmos is about ninety billion light years across.
senses.exampleCN: 可观测宇宙的直径约九百亿光年。
senses.why: modern science keeps the word but drops the moral idea of order, using it as a neutral name for everything there is.
senses.whyCN: 现代科学保留这个词，却放下「秩序」的道德含义，只把它当作「一切存在」的中性名称。

senses.title: Order and harmony themselves
senses.definition: the quality of being arranged harmoniously, especially in Greek philosophy
senses.definitionCN: 和谐排列的性质，尤用于希腊哲学
senses.example: The early thinkers asked how cosmos could arise from chaos.
senses.exampleCN: 早期思想家追问秩序如何能从混沌中产生。
senses.why: the oldest sense is abstract: before the word named a world, it named the arrangement that makes a world worth calling a world.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的义项是抽象的：在指世界之前，它先指那种使世界配得上称为世界的安排。

senses.title: An ordered world of ideas
senses.definition: a complete, internally ordered system of thought or culture
senses.definitionCN: 一个完整且内部有序的思想或文化体系
senses.example: Medieval scholars built a cosmos of signs around scripture.
senses.exampleCN: 中世纪的学者围绕经文构建了一个符号的有序世界。
senses.why: if a world is an ordered whole, then any ordered whole can be called a world, which is how the metaphor extends to thought.
senses.whyCN: 如果世界就是一个有序整体，那么任何有序整体都可称为一个世界，比喻便这样扩展到思想。

senses.title: Ornament and adornment, the archaic sense
senses.definition: in older usage, ornament or adornment, especially of speech or dress
senses.definitionCN: 较古的用法，指言语或衣着的装饰、修饰
senses.example: Rhetoricians praised the cosmos of a well-ordered sentence.
senses.exampleCN: 修辞学家称赞一个组织良好的句子的「修饰」。
senses.why: kosmos meant 'ornament' as well as 'order', because an ornament is a thing put in its proper place; the two senses grew from one root.
senses.whyCN: kosmos 既指「装饰」也指「秩序」，因为装饰就是把东西放到恰当位置；两义同出一根。

senses.title: The cosmos flower
senses.titleCN: 植物学中的大波斯菊属
senses.definition: a genus of plants with neatly arranged petals, named from the Greek word for order
senses.definitionCN: 花瓣排列整齐的一属植物，名字取自希腊语「秩序」
senses.example: Cosmos grows easily in poor soil.
senses.exampleCN: 大波斯菊在贫瘠的土壤里也容易生长。
senses.why: the botanist saw regular petals and reached for the word for ordered arrangement, so the flower carries the oldest sense.
senses.whyCN: 植物学家看到整齐的花瓣，便取用了表示「有序排列」的词，因此这朵花承载着最古老的义项。

senses.title: A self-enclosed literary world
senses.definition: the complete world a poem, novel or myth builds for itself
senses.definitionCN: 诗、小说或神话为自身构建的完整世界
senses.example: Each myth has its own cosmos, with its own geography.
senses.exampleCN: 每个神话都有自己的宇宙，也有自己的地理。
senses.why: a fiction must be ordered to be believed, so critics borrow the Greek word that joins order with world.
senses.whyCN: 虚构作品必须有秩序才可信，因此批评家借用了这个把「秩序」与「世界」结合起来的希腊词。

senses.title: A harmonious social order
senses.definition: an ordered human community conceived as a harmonious whole
senses.definitionCN: 被设想为和谐整体的人类有序共同体
senses.example: Stoics imagined a cosmos of rational citizens.
senses.exampleCN: 斯多葛派想象过一个由理性公民构成的有序整体。
senses.why: philosophy applied the word to human arrangements, because a city, like a sky, can be well or badly ordered.
senses.whyCN: 哲学把这个词用于人的安排，因为城邦与天空一样，都可以有序或失序。

intro.en: Cosmos is a Greek word for order that became a word for the world; it reached English through Latin and French. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: cosmos 是一个意为「秩序」的希腊词，后来变成指「世界」的词；它经拉丁语与法语进入英语。年代均为约数。

items.en: Kosmos meant 'order, arrangement, ornament' and also 'the ordered world'. The world sense is generally attributed to the Pythagoreans, who heard harmony in the movements of the heavens.
items.cn: kosmos 意为「秩序、排列、装饰」，也指「有序的世界」。指世界的义项一般认为源自毕达哥拉斯学派，他们在天体的运动中听出了和谐。

items.en: Kosmetikos meant 'skilled in arranging or adorning', and it gives English cosmetic: the cosmetic arts put the face in order.
items.cn: kosmetikos 意为「擅长整理或修饰的」，衍生英语 cosmetic：化妆术就是把面容整理有序。

items.en: Latin did not simply borrow the Greek word for the world; it used mundus, which itself meant both 'world' and 'ornament', an exact parallel to kosmos.
items.cn: 拉丁语并未直接借用希腊的「世界」一词，而是用 mundus；mundus 本身既指「世界」也指「装饰」，与 kosmos 完全平行。

items.en: Late and medieval Latin did borrow kosmos as cosmus, chiefly in philosophical and astronomical writing, and from there it entered French and English.
items.cn: 晚期与中世纪拉丁语确实把 kosmos 借作 cosmus，主要用于哲学与天文学写作，并由此进入法语与英语。

items.en: From the seventeenth century cosmos served as the dignified name for the whole material system, and cosmology, cosmogony and cosmic were built on it.
items.cn: 从十七世纪起，cosmos 成为整个物质系统的庄重名称，cosmology、cosmogony、cosmic 都建于其上。

items.en: Source uncertain: the attribution of the world sense to Pythagoras rests on later reports rather than his own words, and the first English use is dated only approximately.
items.cn: 来源不确定：把「世界」义归给毕达哥拉斯，依据的是后世记述而非他本人的文字；英语首见也只有约略年代。

note.en: Group one holds the words closest in sound or root; group two holds the names for the whole of things.
note.cn: 第一组是音形或词根最近的词；第二组是「万物整体」的各种名称。

entries.definition: Relating to beauty treatment; from kosmetikos 'skilled in adorning', a direct cousin of cosmos through the ornament sense.
entries.definitionCN: 与美容有关的；来自 kosmetikos「擅长修饰」，经「装饰」义与 cosmos 成为直系表亲。

entries.definition: Of the cosmos; the adjective is far more common than the noun in everyday speech.
entries.definitionCN: 宇宙的；在日常口语中，形容词远比名词常用。

entries.definition: The study of the universe's structure and history; -logy marks the discourse about the cosmos.
entries.definitionCN: 研究宇宙结构与历史的学科；-logy 标记关于宇宙的论说。

entries.definition: A garden plant named for its evenly arranged petals; here the word keeps the old sense of order.
entries.definitionCN: 因花瓣排列整齐而得名的园艺植物；此处保留「秩序」的古义。

entries.definition: Everything that exists; it makes no claim that the whole is ordered, which is exactly what cosmos adds.
entries.definitionCN: 存在的一切；它不主张整体有序，而「有序」正是 cosmos 多出来的意思。

entries.definition: Everything made by a creator; it presupposes a maker that cosmos does not.
entries.definitionCN: 造物主所造的一切；它预设一位制造者，而 cosmos 不需要。

entries.definition: The Earth and human life on it; it is concrete and social where cosmos is vast and philosophical.
entries.definitionCN: 地球及其上的人类生活；它具体而社会，cosmos 则宏大而哲学。

entries.definition: The universe as the large counterpart of the human microcosm; it is a pairing, not a synonym.
entries.definitionCN: 作为人的小宇宙之对应的大世界；它是一种对举，而非同义词。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Greek senses of order and ornament, the real Latin parallel and the real family.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用希腊语「秩序」与「装饰」的真实义项、真实的拉丁平行词与真实的词族。

normal.en: kosmos 'order' first, 'world' second: order is the older half of the meaning.
normal.cn: kosmos 先指「秩序」，后指「世界」：秩序是这层意思更老的一半。

normal.en: The family runs cosmos, cosmic, cosmology, cosmologist, cosmogony.
normal.cn: 词族包括 cosmos、cosmic、cosmology、cosmologist、cosmogony。

normal.en: cosmetic is a cousin: both come from the idea of putting things in order.
normal.cn: cosmetic 是表亲：两者都来自「把东西整理有序」的观念。

normal.en: Latin mundus means both 'world' and 'ornament', exactly like kosmos.
normal.cn: 拉丁 mundus 既指「世界」也指「装饰」，与 kosmos 完全一致。

normal.en: Pair words: cosmos and chaos, order and disorder.
normal.cn: 成对记忆：cosmos 与 chaos，秩序与混乱。

abstract.en: Picture a dish of stars laid out in a perfect ring.
abstract.cn: 想象一盘星星被摆成一个完美的圆环。

abstract.en: Picture a sentence so well built that it looks like an ornament.
abstract.cn: 想象一个结构精良到看起来像饰物的句子。

abstract.en: Picture a city that behaves like a well-tuned sky.
abstract.cn: 想象一座运作得像校准过的天空那样的城。

examples.en: The Greeks did not separate the beauty of the cosmos from its order.
examples.cn: 希腊人并未把宇宙的美与它的秩序分开。

examples.en: Modern cosmology treats the cosmos as a single measurable system.
examples.cn: 现代宇宙学把宇宙当作一个可测量的单一系统。

examples.en: His essays describe a cosmos of signs that only initiates can read.
examples.cn: 他的随笔描述了一个只有入门者能读懂的符号世界。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「科（co）+ 斯（s）+ 莫斯（mos）」——把万物排得整整齐齐 → 有序的宇宙

12.root: 希腊 kosmos「秩序、装饰、有序世界」；经晚期拉丁 cosmus 与法语进入英语。拉丁对应词 mundus 同样兼指「世界」与「装饰」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses begin with the marriage of order and totality: the ordered universe, the physical universe, order itself, an ordered world of thought, the old sense of ornament, the flower named for order, a fiction's closed world and a harmonious human order.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项始于「秩序」与「整体」的结合：有序的宇宙、物质宇宙、秩序本身、观念的有序世界、装饰的古义、因秩序得名的花、虚构的封闭世界，以及和谐的人类秩序。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a ring of stars carved in even spacing on a Greek dish.
core.cn: 核心意象：希腊陶盘上刻着一圈间距匀称的星点。

branches.en: ORDER AND WORLD TOGETHER: the oldest marriage of meanings, kept in the modern noun.
branches.cn: 秩序与世界的结合：最古老的意义联姻，保存在现代名词中。

branches.en: THE PHYSICAL WHOLE: the same word used neutrally by astronomy.
branches.cn: 物质整体：天文学中性使用同一个词。

branches.en: ORDERED WORLDS OF MIND: systems of thought and the closed worlds of fiction.
branches.cn: 心智的有序世界：思想体系与虚构的封闭世界。

branches.en: ORNAMENT: the archaic sense survives in rhetoric and in the cosmos flower.
branches.cn: 装饰：古义残留在修辞学与波斯菊的属名里。

branches.en: HUMAN HARMONY: a community imagined as a well-ordered whole.
branches.cn: 人的和谐：被想象为有序整体的共同体。

intro.en: Cosmos is a bare Greek noun, and its family grows by suffixes that name sciences, origins and qualities.
intro.cn: cosmos 是一个光秃秃的希腊名词，其词族靠命名学科、起源与性质的后缀生长。

latinIntro.en: Latin preferred mundus for the world but borrowed cosmus for philosophy; English took the Greek form through French and added Latin-style suffixes.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语指世界时更常用 mundus，但在哲学中借入 cosmus；英语经法语取用希腊词形，再加拉丁式后缀。

items.example: Cosmology is the study of the cosmos.
items.exampleCN: 宇宙学是对宇宙的研究。

items.example: Cosmogony asks how the world began.
items.exampleCN: 宇宙起源论追问世界如何开始。

items.example: Cosmic rays arrive from outside the solar system.
items.exampleCN: 宇宙线来自太阳系之外。

items.example: Cosmology dates the expansion to a single beginning.
items.exampleCN: 宇宙学把膨胀追溯到一个起点。

items.example: The cosmologist modelled the early universe.
items.exampleCN: 这位宇宙学家为早期宇宙建模。

items.meaningCN: 宇宙的起源；宇宙起源论
items.example: Every culture has its own cosmogony.
items.exampleCN: 每个文化都有自己的宇宙起源故事。

items.example: The cosmetic sense comes from 'ornament'.
items.exampleCN: 「化妆」义来自「装饰」这一层。

items.meaning: a small world reflecting the great one
items.example: The cell is a microcosm of the body.
items.exampleCN: 细胞是身体的一个缩影。

items.example: The macrocosm was thought to mirror the body.
items.exampleCN: 古人认为大宇宙与人体相互映照。

latinEntries.structure: cosmus, cosmi (noun, second declension, from Greek)

13.definition_zh: 宇宙的；宇宙空间的；极其巨大的
13.definition_en: relating to the universe, or extremely large in scale
13.core_image: 无月的山脊上，一道微弱的辉光横过整个天空
13.scene: 山顶的夜里没有月光，一道微弱的辉光横过整个天空。On a moonless ridge, the cosmic background shows as a faint band across the sky.
13.sceneCN: 这里 cosmic 指「属于宇宙、来自宇宙空间的」（第 2 个义项：宇宙辐射与背景这类宇宙尺度现象）；句意为在无月的山脊上，宇宙背景辐射呈现为横跨天空的微弱光带。可辨识物件：山脊、无月的夜空、微弱光带、观测设备。

pos.zh: 宇宙的；宇宙空间的；极其巨大的

forms.label: 副词（从宇宙角度；极其地）

senses.title: Relating to the universe
senses.definition: of or relating to the universe as a whole
senses.definitionCN: 与作为整体的宇宙有关的
senses.example: The cosmic expansion carries galaxies apart.
senses.exampleCN: 宇宙膨胀把星系彼此拉开。
senses.why: the suffix -ic simply makes an adjective of cosmos, so the plain sense covers anything belonging to the whole system.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ic 只是把 cosmos 变成形容词，因此最朴素的义项涵盖属于整个系统的一切。

senses.title: Coming from space
senses.definition: of radiation or particles that arrive from outside the Earth and its atmosphere
senses.definitionCN: 指从地球与大气层之外到达的辐射或粒子
senses.example: On a moonless ridge, the cosmic background shows as a faint band across the sky.
senses.exampleCN: 在无月的山脊上，宇宙背景辐射呈现为横跨天空的微弱光带。
senses.why: once instruments could detect what the air filters out, the adjective marked the extraterrestrial origin of the signal.
senses.whyCN: 当仪器能探测到被大气滤掉的东西，这个形容词便标记信号的「地球之外」来源。

senses.title: Cosmic rays and particles
senses.definition: of the high-energy particles that bombard the atmosphere from space
senses.definitionCN: 指从太空轰击大气层的高能粒子
senses.example: Cosmic rays can flip a bit in a satellite's memory.
senses.exampleCN: 宇宙线能翻转卫星存储器中的一个位。
senses.why: the phrase cosmic rays is fixed, and it keeps the adjective even though the 'rays' are mostly particles.
senses.whyCN: cosmic rays 是固定说法，尽管这些「射线」多半是粒子，形容词仍保留下来。

senses.title: Cosmic dust and gas
senses.definition: of the fine matter that fills interstellar space
senses.definitionCN: 指充满星际空间的细微物质
senses.example: Cosmic dust reddens the light of distant stars.
senses.exampleCN: 宇宙尘埃使远处恒星的光偏红。
senses.why: the material is not exotic in itself, only in its setting, so the adjective carries the location rather than the substance.
senses.whyCN: 这些物质本身并不奇特，奇特的是它们所在的环境，因此这个形容词承载的是位置而非材质。

senses.title: Cosmic time and scale
senses.definition: of the very long intervals and vast distances used for the universe
senses.definitionCN: 指用于宇宙的极长时间间隔与极大距离
senses.example: In cosmic time, a human life is a flicker.
senses.exampleCN: 按宇宙时计，人的一生只是一闪。
senses.why: the universe needs units larger than human history, and the adjective marks that shift of scale.
senses.whyCN: 宇宙需要比人类历史更大的单位，这个形容词标记的正是尺度的切换。

senses.title: Extremely large, in loose speech
senses.definition: of an amount or event, so large that it seems to belong to another scale
senses.definitionCN: 指数量或事件大到仿佛属于另一套尺度
senses.example: The failure was a cosmic embarrassment for the agency.
senses.exampleCN: 这次失败对该机构来说是一次极其难堪的事件。
senses.why: the figurative use works because the literal scale is unimaginable, which makes it a natural intensifier.
senses.whyCN: 比喻用法之所以成立，是因为字面尺度无法想象，因此它天然适合当强调词。

senses.title: Cosmic order and harmony
senses.definition: of an ordered, harmonious arrangement of the whole, in philosophy and poetry
senses.definitionCN: 指哲学与诗歌中整体有序、和谐的安排
senses.example: The poem trusts a cosmic order behind the noise.
senses.exampleCN: 这首诗相信喧闹背后有一种宇宙秩序。
senses.why: this sense returns to the Greek noun's first meaning, where cosmos was order before it was world.
senses.whyCN: 这一义项回到希腊名词最初的意思：cosmos 先指秩序，后才指世界。

senses.title: Cosmic irony
senses.definition: of a literary situation in which fate seems to mock human plans
senses.definitionCN: 指命运仿佛在嘲弄人类计划的文学处境
senses.example: The ending depends on cosmic irony, not on character.
senses.exampleCN: 这个结局靠的是宇宙性的反讽，而不是人物。
senses.why: the term imagines the universe as a spectator with a sense of humour, an old idea dressed in a modern adjective.
senses.whyCN: 这个术语把宇宙想象成一个有幽默感的旁观者，是旧观念穿上了现代形容词。

intro.en: Cosmic is the Greek adjective of kosmos, formed with -ikos and borrowed through Latin. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: cosmic 是希腊 kosmos 的形容词，由 -ikos 构成，并经拉丁语借入。年代均为约数。

items.en: Kosmikos meant 'of the world or of order', built from kosmos with the adjective suffix -ikos 'relating to'.
items.cn: kosmikos 意为「世界的」或「秩序的」，由 kosmos 加形容词后缀 -ikos「与……相关」构成。

items.en: Late Latin borrowed the Greek adjective as cosmicus, mainly in philosophical and astronomical texts.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语把希腊形容词借作 cosmicus，主要用于哲学与天文文本。

items.en: English records cosmic in the seventeenth century, at first in the sense 'of the ordered world' rather than 'of outer space'.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪记录到 cosmic，最初意为「有序世界的」，而非「外太空的」。

items.en: Nineteenth- and twentieth-century astronomy fixed phrases such as cosmic rays and cosmic dust, moving the adjective firmly into the physical register.
items.cn: 十九与二十世纪的天文学固定了 cosmic rays、cosmic dust 等说法，把这个形容词稳固地移入物理语境。

items.en: The loose sense 'extremely large' is generally dated to the twentieth century, when the scale of the universe became a familiar comparison.
items.cn: 「极其巨大」这一宽松义项一般认为是二十世纪出现的，当时宇宙的尺度成了人们熟悉的比较对象。

items.en: Source uncertain: the first English citation is dated only approximately, and the exact moment when the 'huge' sense entered colloquial use is not recorded.
items.cn: 来源不确定：英语首见只有约略年代；「巨大」义进入口语的确切时间没有记录。

note.en: Group one separates cosmic from close forms and from the noun; group two holds adjectives of enormous scale.
note.cn: 第一组把 cosmic 与近形词及名词分开；第二组是表示巨大尺度的形容词。

entries.definition: The ordered universe as a whole; cosmic describes what belongs to it.
entries.definitionCN: 作为整体的有序宇宙；cosmic 形容属于它的事物。

entries.definition: Of beauty treatment; it descends from kosmetikos 'skilled in adorning' and shares only the ornamental branch of the root.
entries.definitionCN: 与美容有关的；源自 kosmetikos「擅长修饰」，只共享词根中「装饰」那一支。

entries.definition: Relating to cosmology as a discipline; it is narrower and more academic than cosmic.
entries.definitionCN: 与宇宙学这门学科相关；比 cosmic 更窄、更学术。

entries.definition: In cosmic terms or to an extreme degree; the adverb often carries the intensifier sense.
entries.definitionCN: 从宇宙角度或达到极端程度；这个副词常带强调义。

entries.definition: Of astronomy, and informally very large; it overlaps with cosmic as an intensifier but not as a technical term.
entries.definitionCN: 天文学的，口语中也指极大；作强调词时与 cosmic 重叠，但技术义不同。

entries.definition: Applying to everyone or everything; cosmic locates things in the universe rather than asserting coverage.
