entries.definitionCN: 适用于所有人或物；cosmic 是把事物定位在宇宙中，而非断言覆盖范围。

entries.definition: Originating beyond the Earth; it is narrower than cosmic and says nothing about scale.
entries.definitionCN: 源自地球之外；比 cosmic 窄，也不涉及尺度。

entries.definition: Of the sky or the bodies in it; celestial is poetic and local, cosmic is total and physical.
entries.definitionCN: 天空或天体的；celestial 偏诗性且局部，cosmic 则整体而物理。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real suffix, the real fixed phrases and the real shift from order to vastness.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的后缀、真实的固定搭配，以及从「秩序」到「巨大」的真实转变。

normal.en: cosmos + -ic: belonging to the whole ordered universe.
normal.cn: cosmos + -ic：属于那个有序整体的宇宙。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: cosmic rays, cosmic dust, cosmic background radiation, cosmic time.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：宇宙线、宇宙尘埃、宇宙背景辐射、宇宙时。

normal.en: The adverb cosmically usually carries the intensifier sense.
normal.cn: 副词 cosmically 通常带强调义。

normal.en: cosmic time makes a human life a flicker; that is why the word also means 'huge'.
normal.cn: 宇宙时让人的一生只是一闪；正因为如此，这个词也指「巨大」。

normal.en: The old sense of order survives in cosmic irony and cosmic harmony.
normal.cn: 「秩序」的旧义残留在 cosmic irony 与 cosmic harmony 中。

abstract.en: Picture a faint band of ancient light lying across a dark ridge.
abstract.cn: 想象一道古老而微弱的横过黑暗山脊的光带。

abstract.en: Picture a grain of dust that has travelled longer than the Earth has existed.
abstract.cn: 想象一粒尘埃，它旅行的时间比地球存在的时间还长。

abstract.en: Picture a joke told by the whole universe at one person's expense.
abstract.cn: 想象整个宇宙拿一个人开玩笑。

examples.en: Cosmic radiation limits how long crews can stay in orbit.
examples.cn: 宇宙辐射限制了乘组在轨停留的时间。

examples.en: The film ends on a cosmic irony: the rescue arrives too late.
examples.cn: 影片以宇宙性的反讽收尾：救援来得太晚。

examples.en: On a cosmic scale, the mountain range is a scratch.
examples.cn: 按宇宙尺度，这条山脉只是一道划痕。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「cos（科斯）+ mic（麦克）」——麦克风对着整个宇宙 → 宇宙的；极大的

13.root: 希腊 kosmikos「世界的、有序的」← kosmos + -ikos；晚期拉丁 cosmicus；英语 cosmic。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses start from belonging to the whole, then mark extraterrestrial origin, rays, dust, cosmic time, huge amounts, the old harmony of order, and finally the literary joke of cosmic irony.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从「属于整体」出发，随后标记地球之外的来源、射线、尘埃、宇宙时、巨大数量、古老的秩序和谐，最后是文学中的宇宙性反讽。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a faint glow spanning the whole sky above a dark ridge.
core.cn: 核心意象：黑暗山脊之上，一道微光横跨整个天空。

branches.en: THE WHOLE: belonging to the universe, and to its old idea of harmony.
branches.cn: 整体：属于宇宙，也属于它古老的和谐观念。

branches.en: FROM OUTSIDE: background radiation, rays and dust all arrive from beyond the air.
branches.cn: 来自外面：背景辐射、射线与尘埃都从大气之外到达。

branches.en: UNITS OF THE UNIVERSE: cosmic time and distance outgrow human history.
branches.cn: 宇宙的单位：宇宙时与距离超出人类历史。

branches.en: INTENSIFIER: the unimaginable scale becomes a way of saying 'enormous'.
branches.cn: 强调词：无法想象的尺度变成说「巨大」的方式。

branches.en: COSMIC IRONY: the universe imagined as a spectator laughing at plans.
branches.cn: 宇宙性反讽：把宇宙想象成嘲笑人类计划的旁观者。

intro.en: Cosmic is a Greek noun plus -ikos, and its family supplies the names of sciences and of origins.
intro.cn: cosmic 是希腊名词加 -ikos，其词族提供学科与起源的名称。

latinIntro.en: Late Latin cosmicus carries the adjective; Latin itself preferred mundanus for 'of the world', built on mundus.
latinIntro.cn: 晚期拉丁 cosmicus 承载这个形容词；拉丁语本身更常用 mundanus「世界的」，建于 mundus 之上。

items.example: Cosmos gives cosmic by this suffix.
items.exampleCN: cosmos 靠这个后缀构成 cosmic。

items.example: The cosmos is treated as one system.
items.exampleCN: 宇宙被当作一个系统。

items.example: The event was cosmically unlikely.
items.exampleCN: 这件事在宇宙尺度上极不可能。

items.example: Cosmology uses cosmic background data.
items.exampleCN: 宇宙学使用宇宙背景数据。

items.example: Cosmogony overlaps with mythology.
items.exampleCN: 宇宙起源论与神话有重叠。

items.meaningCN: 宇宙成因的；由宇宙线产生的
items.example: Cosmogenic isotopes date old surfaces.
items.exampleCN: 宇宙成因同位素为古老地表定年。

items.meaningCN: 宇宙线（来自太空的高能粒子）
items.example: Cosmic rays ionise the upper air.
items.exampleCN: 宇宙线使高层大气电离。

items.meaningCN: 宇宙尘埃（太空中的细微固体物质）
items.example: Cosmic dust dims background stars.
items.exampleCN: 宇宙尘埃使背景恒星变暗。

items.example: The pond is a microcosm.
items.exampleCN: 这池塘是一个缩影。

14.definition_zh: 星系；银河；银河系；一群杰出人物
14.definition_en: a vast system of stars, gas and dust held together by gravity
14.core_image: 乡野夜空里，一条乳白色光带横过天顶，两旁是密集的暗星
14.scene: 乡下的夜空里，一条乳白色的光带横过天顶，两旁散着密集的暗星。On a clear night the galaxy appears as a pale band, though it is really a disc seen from inside.
14.sceneCN: 这里 galaxy 指「银河系这条横跨天空的光带」（第 3 个义项：从内部看到的银河外观）；句意为晴夜里银河看起来是一条淡色带子，其实它是一个从内部看去的盘。可辨识物件：乳白光带、密集暗星、地平线、村舍灯。

pos.zh: 可数名词：星系；银河系；一群杰出人物

senses.title: A gravitationally bound system of stars
senses.titleCN: 由引力束缚的恒星系统
senses.definition: a very large system of stars, gas and dust held together by gravity
senses.definitionCN: 由引力维系在一起的巨大恒星、气体与尘埃系统
senses.example: The telescope resolved the smudge into a separate galaxy.
senses.exampleCN: 望远镜把那个模糊斑点分辨成一个独立的星系。
senses.why: the word moved from naming one band to naming any such system, once telescopes showed that faint patches are separate islands of stars.
senses.whyCN: 当望远镜显示那些模糊斑点其实是独立的恒星岛，这个词便从指一条光带转为指任何这类系统。

senses.title: Our own galaxy, the Milky Way
senses.definition: the specific system of stars that contains the Sun, often written with a capital
senses.definitionCN: 包含太阳的那个特定恒星系统，常大写
senses.example: The Sun takes two hundred million years to orbit the galaxy.
senses.exampleCN: 太阳绕银河系一圈需要两亿年。
senses.why: before other galaxies were known, there was only one, so 'the galaxy' needed no further specification and the capital remained.
senses.whyCN: 在其他星系被发现之前，只有一个星系，因此「the galaxy」无需再加限定，大写形式也保留了下来。

senses.title: The pale band in the night sky
senses.definition: the faint luminous band visible across the sky on clear dark nights
senses.definitionCN: 晴朗暗夜里横跨天空的微弱光带
senses.example: On a clear night the galaxy appears as a pale band, though it is really a disc seen from inside.
senses.exampleCN: 晴夜里银河看起来是一条淡色带子，其实它是一个从内部看去的盘。
senses.why: the oldest sense is what the eye sees: the Greek name literally meant the milky circle, a description of appearance rather than of structure.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的义项是肉眼所见：希腊原名本义就是「乳白色的环」，描述的是外观而非结构。

senses.title: A galaxy of talent
senses.definition: a brilliant assemblage of people, especially in entertainment or sport
senses.definitionCN: 一批光彩夺目的人，尤用于演艺或体育
senses.example: The cast was a galaxy of talent.
senses.exampleCN: 这个演员阵容群星云集。
senses.why: the metaphor keeps the idea of many bright points gathered in one place, which is exactly how a crowd of stars looks.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻保留了「许多亮点聚在一处」的意象，而一群明星看上去正是如此。

senses.title: A dazzling multitude of things
senses.titleCN: 令人眼花缭乱的大量事物
senses.definition: a large, impressive collection of objects or options
senses.definitionCN: 大量而引人注目的物品或选项集合
senses.example: A galaxy of colours filled the market stalls.
senses.exampleCN: 市场摊位上是一片令人眼花缭乱的色彩。
senses.why: once the word meant a multitude of lights, any bright abundance could borrow it, and the metaphor widened beyond people.
senses.whyCN: 一旦这个词指大量光点，任何明亮的丰盛都能借用它，比喻便从人扩展到物。

senses.title: A structured system of related things
senses.definition: a complex system of related elements organised around a centre
senses.definitionCN: 围绕中心组织起来的复杂要素系统
senses.example: The novel maps a galaxy of institutions around one family.
senses.exampleCN: 这部小说围绕一个家族描绘了一个由机构构成的星系。
senses.why: the scientific sense supplies structure as well as size, so the metaphor can describe any centred network.
senses.whyCN: 科学义同时提供「规模」与「结构」，因此这个比喻可以描述任何以中心组织的网络。

senses.title: A self-contained world of activity
senses.definition: a closed social or professional world with its own rules
senses.definitionCN: 有自身规则、自成一体的社交或职业世界
senses.example: Fashion is a galaxy with its own gravity.
senses.exampleCN: 时尚是一个有自己的引力的星系。
senses.why: a galaxy holds its members by gravity, and the metaphor maps that pull onto the way a social world keeps its people.
senses.whyCN: 星系靠引力维系成员，这个比喻把这种拉力映射到某个社交世界留住人的方式上。

senses.title: A class of galaxy by shape
senses.titleCN: 按形态划分的星系类别
senses.definition: used in compounds for a morphological type, as spiral, elliptical or irregular galaxy
senses.definitionCN: 用于复合词中表示形态类别，如旋涡、椭圆或不规则星系
senses.example: An elliptical galaxy lacks the arms of a spiral.
senses.exampleCN: 椭圆星系没有旋涡星系的旋臂。
senses.why: astronomy classifies what it names, so the word became the head of a family of type labels.
senses.whyCN: 天文学会对所命名之物分类，于是这个词成了一组形态标签的中心词。

intro.en: Galaxy began as a Greek description of a milky band and grew into the name of whole star systems. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: galaxy 起初是希腊语对一条乳白光带的描述，后来长成整个恒星系统的名称。年代均为约数。

items.en: Gala (genitive galaktos) meant 'milk'. The adjective galaxias 'milky' came from it, and the phrase galaxias kyklos meant 'the milky circle'.
items.cn: gala（属格 galaktos）意为「奶」。形容词 galaxias「乳白色的」由它而来，短语 galaxias kyklos 意为「乳白色的环」。

items.en: Latin rendered the Greek phrase as via lactea 'milky road', using lac 'milk' rather than borrowing the Greek noun; both names describe the same band.
items.cn: 拉丁语把希腊短语译作 via lactea「乳汁之路」，用本族的 lac「奶」而不借希腊名词；两个名字描述同一条光带。

items.en: English borrowed the Greek-derived form through Old French galaxie in the fourteenth century, still meaning the visible band and its supposed milky material.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪经古法语 galaxie 借入这个源自希腊的形式，仍指可见光带及其被认为的乳状物质。

items.en: In the 1920s observations of variable stars settled that faint nebulae lie far outside the Milky Way, and galaxy then became a count noun for any such system.
items.cn: 二十世纪二十年代对变星的观测确定，那些微弱星云远在银河系之外，galaxy 由此成为可数名词，指任何这类系统。

items.en: The sense 'a brilliant group of people' is generally dated to the nineteenth century, when galaxy was already a stock image for a crowd of bright points.
items.cn: 「一群杰出人物」这一义项一般认为是十九世纪出现的，当时 galaxy 已成为「一群亮点」的常用意象。

items.en: Source uncertain: the first English use is dated only approximately, and the exact date when the word became a general count noun for star systems is debated among historians of astronomy.
items.cn: 来源不确定：英语首见只有约略年代；这个词何时成为指恒星系统的通用可数名词，在天文学史家中仍有争论。

note.en: Group one holds close forms and the milk-root trap; group two holds the objects galaxy is often confused with.
note.cn: 第一组是近形词与「奶」词根的陷阱；第二组是常与星系混淆的天体。

entries.definition: Of a galaxy; the adjective is used in phrases such as galactic centre and galactic plane.
entries.definitionCN: 星系的；形容词用于银河系中心、银道面等说法。

entries.definition: Sugar found in milk; it comes from Latin lac 'milk', while galaxy comes from Greek gala 'milk'. Same meaning, different root.
entries.definitionCN: 奶中的糖；来自拉丁 lac「奶」，而 galaxy 来自希腊 gala「奶」。意义相同，词源不同。

entries.definition: Lead sulphide ore; the word is Latin for lead ore and has no connection with milk or stars.
entries.definitionCN: 硫化铅矿石；这个词是拉丁语「铅矿」，与奶和星都没有关系。

entries.definition: The English translation of via lactea; it names the same band that galaxy first described.
entries.definitionCN: via lactea 的英译；它指的那条光带正是 galaxy 最初描述的对象。

entries.definition: A few stars bound together, such as a binary; a galaxy contains millions or billions of them.
entries.definitionCN: 少数恒星束缚在一起，如双星；一个星系包含数百万乃至数十亿颗。

entries.definition: A cloud of gas or dust in space; before 1920 many nebulae were mistaken for galaxies.
entries.definitionCN: 太空中的气体或尘埃云；一九二〇年之前许多星云被误认为星系。

entries.definition: A group of stars or galaxies gathered together; a galaxy cluster is made of galaxies.
entries.definitionCN: 聚集在一起的恒星或星系；星系团由星系组成。

entries.definition: Everything that exists; galaxies are the large structures inside it.
entries.definitionCN: 存在的一切；星系是它内部的大尺度结构。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Greek milk root, the real Latin parallel and the real morphological labels.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的希腊「奶」词根、真实的拉丁平行词与真实的形态标签。

normal.en: Greek gala 'milk' gives galaxias 'milky': the milky circle in the sky.
normal.cn: 希腊 gala「奶」给出 galaxias「乳白的」：天上那个乳白色的环。

normal.en: Latin said via lactea 'milky road', using lac for milk; English translates it as the Milky Way.
normal.cn: 拉丁语说 via lactea「乳汁之路」，用 lac 表示奶；英语把它译作 the Milky Way。

normal.en: The family runs galaxy, galactic, intergalactic, extragalactic.
normal.cn: 词族包括 galaxy、galactic、intergalactic、extragalactic。

normal.en: Type labels: spiral galaxy, elliptical galaxy, irregular galaxy, dwarf galaxy.
normal.cn: 形态标签：旋涡星系、椭圆星系、不规则星系、矮星系。

normal.en: lactose is not a cousin of galaxy: Latin lac and Greek gala both mean milk but are different roots.
normal.cn: lactose 不是 galaxy 的表亲：拉丁 lac 与希腊 gala 都指奶，但词根不同。

abstract.en: Picture a disc of light seen edge-on from inside it.
abstract.cn: 想象一个从内部侧看的光盘。

abstract.en: Picture a crowd of famous faces as bright points packed together.
abstract.cn: 想象一群名人的脸聚成密集的亮点。

abstract.en: Picture a social world that holds its members the way gravity holds stars.
abstract.cn: 想象一个像引力抓住恒星那样抓住成员的社交世界。

examples.en: Distant galaxies recede faster than nearby ones.
examples.cn: 遥远星系退行的速度比近处星系更快。

examples.en: The galaxy contains a supermassive black hole at its centre.
examples.cn: 这个星系的中心有一个超大质量黑洞。

examples.en: The festival assembled a galaxy of directors and actors.
examples.cn: 电影节聚集了一群导演与演员。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「嘎（ga）+ 拉克（lax）+ 西（y）」——天上那条乳白色的带子 → 银河；星系

14.root: 希腊 galaxias「乳白色的」← gala（属格 galaktos）「奶」；短语 galaxias kyklos 意为「乳白色的环」；经古法语 galaxie 进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one band of light: the bound system, our own system, the visible band itself, a crowd of stars in metaphor, any bright multitude, a centred system, a self-contained world, and finally a morphological class.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一条光带展开：受引力束缚的系统、我们自己所在的系统、可见的那条带、比喻中的一群明星、任何明亮的众多、以中心组织的系统、自成一体的世界，最后是形态类别。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a pale milky band across a dark country sky.
core.cn: 核心意象：乡野暗夜里横过天空的一条乳白光带。

branches.en: APPEARANCE: the oldest sense, what the eye sees as a milky band.
branches.cn: 外观：最古老的义项，肉眼所见的乳白光带。

branches.en: SYSTEM: the band turns out to be a disc, and our disc is one among many.
branches.cn: 系统：光带其实是一个盘，而我们的盘只是众多之一。

branches.en: CLASSIFICATION: astronomers sort these systems by shape.
branches.cn: 分类：天文学家按形态给这些系统分类。

branches.en: BRIGHT MULTITUDE: crowds, colours and structures borrow the image of many lights.
branches.cn: 明亮众多：人群、色彩与结构都借用「许多光点」的意象。

branches.en: SOCIAL GRAVITY: a closed world holds its members the way a galaxy holds stars.
branches.cn: 社交引力：一个封闭世界像星系抓住恒星那样抓住成员。

intro.en: Galaxy is a Greek adjective used as a noun; its family turns on the stem galact- and on prefixes meaning between and beyond.
intro.cn: galaxy 是一个用作名词的希腊形容词；其词族围绕 galact- 词干，以及表示「之间」与「之外」的前缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin preferred its own via lactea with lac 'milk', but also borrowed galaxias; English keeps the Greek stem and adds Latin prefixes.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语更常用本族的 via lactea 与 lac「奶」，但也借入了 galaxias；英语保留希腊词干并加拉丁前缀。
